title: Sr Manager, Real Estate and Workplace
description:
About ALSO.

We’re ALSO, an electric mobility company originally conceived as a part of Rivian. We’re a passionate team of builders, dreamers, doers and innovators, focused on creating entirely new (not to mention, innovative and delightful) vertically integrated, small EVs designed to meet the global mobility challenges of today and tomorrow. Our mission is to inspire everyone to ride ALSO—replacing many local car, truck and SUV miles with ones on vehicles that are more affordable, more enjoyable and 10-50x more efficient.



ALSO is seeking an execution-driven Sr Manager, Real Estate & Workplace, to lead workplace strategy, projects, programs, and teams based in our Palo Alto HQ for a global multi-site portfolio spanning office, R&D labs, commercial hubs, and retail.


This role owns team leadership, strategic planning, critical project execution, and executive-level representation alongside the Director, partnering daily with IT, Engineering, Purchasing, Finance, Legal, Insurance, People, and cross functional key stakeholders. Success requires ability to prioritize in a fast-paced environment, drive R&D projects to execution, disciplined governance, financial rigor, 3rd party management, and the ability to anticipate space and workplace service needs (ie, mail, logistics, culinary, janitorial, and moves). Onsite 3-5 days/week, with off-hours availability for time-sensitive and critical issues.



What You Will Do 

Team & Program Leadership

 - Lead the Real Estate & Workplace team (operations, facilities, mail, logistics, culinary, janitorial) as deputy lead, balancing competing priorities with long-term focus.

 - Manage projects end to end, including portfolio administration, R&D lab build-outs, workplace programs, and occupancy data.

Strategic Space Planning & Occupancy Analysis

 - Own headcount and occupancy analysis, turning hiring plans and growth into space strategy, capacity models, and scenarios.

 - Drive long-range workplace strategy and partner with Finance and Analytics on forecasting and tradeoff recommendations to leadership.

Vendor, Contract & Budget Management

 - Manage vendors, consultants, landlords, and GCs with negotiation and financial accountability.

 - Own budget tracking, forecasting, and RFPs with Purchasing and Finance, and oversee lease transactions end to end with Legal and Risk.

Cross-Functional Partnership

 - Act as the connective tissue across IT, Engineering, Purchasing, Finance, Legal/Compliance, Analytics, and G&A.

 - Support Executive Assistants on space, logistics, and events, and communicate credibly with landlords, brokers, executives, and building inspectors.

Technical R&D Project Delivery & Operations

 - Coordinate lab infrastructure and equipment installs with Engineering and vendors.

 - Partner with the IT and EHS & Security Manager on life-safety and compliance, and serve as a point of contact for after-hours facilities emergencies.

Process Governance & Data Enablement

 - Implement standard PM frameworks, ticketing, and KPI/milestone dashboards.

 - Adopt new technology and AI-assisted tools to streamline workflows as the portfolio grows.



What You Will Bring 

 - 7+ years of progressive real estate, workplace, or facilities operations experience, with demonstrated growth from individual execution into a leadership scope.

 - Track record leading teams and operating as a trusted second-in-command.

 - Comfortable partnering across IT, Engineering, Finance, Legal, and Purchasing, and communicating credibly from AHJs to executives.

 - Working knowledge of commercial leases, vendor contracts, and budget/financial management.

 - Comfortable with ambiguity and fast-changing priorities; adaptable to new technology, software, and AI-assisted tools.

 - Familiarity with EHS, physical security concepts, and specialized lab/R&D infrastructure preferred (this role partners with a dedicated EHS & Security Manager rather than owning those programs directly).

 - Experience scaling high-tech, EV, or R&D lab environments strongly preferred.

 - Able to respond to occasional off-hours emergencies.



The salary for this position ranges from $200,000 - $220,000 per year, depending on experience, qualifications, and location.


Perks and Benefits

 - Robust health coverage. Excellent health, dental and vision insurance covered up to 100% by Also. with FSA & HSA options.

 - One Medical membership and dedicated insurance advocates.

 - Rich fertility and family building benefits with Progyny.

 - Flexible time off. 

 - 401(k) match.



Why ALSO.

We’re passionate about helping the world find a better way to get there—wherever it is you’re headed.

We’re located in the heart of Silicon Valley and have brought together a world-class team from some of the biggest brands in the technology, automotive, cycling, outdoor recreation and retail spaces. 

Together we’re working hands-on to imagine, design and build an entirely new solution to a global set of transportation challenges.

ALSO. is looking for a Staff Manufacturing Engineer for Vehicle Final Assembly & Test, based in Palo Alto, CA with experience working with internal design teams on DFM and scaling initiatives for passenger or autonomous vehicles. You will be a key direct contributor to launching the manufacturing of new products at both domestic and international manufacturing partners and ramping production. This is a rare opportunity to have a front row seat and high-level impact on each new vehicle product from two to four-wheeled.



What You Will Do 

 - Lead manufacturing development for new automotive products, from pilot builds through production launch.

 - Design pilot lines, including layouts, assembly and test steps, tooling, and equipment.

 - Develop equipment and process specifications; lead design reviews and identify opportunities for automation.

 - Model production capacity, identify bottlenecks, and develop plans to meet output targets.

 - Work with equipment integrators and contract manufacturers to implement assembly automation and custom test systems, including dynamometers.

What You Will Bring 

 - Bachelor’s degree or higher in Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, or a related field, with NPI or manufacturing engineering experience in the automotive industry.

 - Experience leading products through prototype builds, validation, production launch, and high volume ramp at contract manufacturers.

 - Hands-on DFM experience partnering with design teams to improve manufacturability, including proficiency in CATIA or SolidWorks.

 - Experience selecting manufacturing processes and implementing automation, with an understanding of how tooling, supply chain, quality, cost, and cycle time affect production decisions.

 - Working knowledge of APQP and PPAP, with the ability to lead cross-functional decisions using data and take ownership of launch issues.

title: 2027 Drug Substance Engineering Intern (PhD)
description:
About AbbVie
AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. For more information about AbbVie, please visit us at  www.abbvie.com . Follow @abbvie on  LinkedIn,   Facebook ,  Instagram ,  X  and  YouTube.
Drug Substance Engineering Internship Overview
Envision spending your summer working with energetic colleagues and inspirational leaders, all while gaining world-class experience in one of the most dynamic organizations in the pharmaceutical industry. This is a reality for AbbVie Interns.
Micronization of drug substance is a critical process in API manufacturing for ensuring downstream critical quality attributes. Micronization processes such as pin milling and jet milling leverage feed rate control to optimize the process performance, and while feed rate is well understood for many powder systems there is a gap in understanding the feed rate control of poorly flowing materials in micronization techniques.
The Drug Substance Engineering Intern within Product Development, Science, and Technology (PDS&T) will help establish a systematic approach to understand how the physical properties of powder systems impact their feeding performance in micronization processes.
Key responsibilities include:
Experimental studies to understand and characterize powder properties
Evaluate performance of micronization techniques (i.e. jet mill, pin mill) with various feed mechanisms
Analyze data and trends to identify signatures for process performance
Develop and verify computational models
Summarize and present findings in departmental and cross-functional settings
Minimum Qualifications
Currently enrolled in university, pursuing a PhD in Chemical Engineering, Materials Engineering, or other related field
Must be enrolled in university for at least one semester following the internship
Preferred Qualifications
Expected graduation date between December 2027 – June 2028
Exposure to comminution processes
Experience with physical characterization techniques (flowability, adhesion, cohesion, bulk density, laser diffraction particle size determination)
Proficient in computational modeling techniques (e.g., fluid dynamics, discrete element method)

2027 Formulation Sciences Internship Overview
Envision spending your summer working with energetic colleagues and inspirational leaders, all while gaining world-class experience in one of the most dynamic organizations in the pharmaceutical industry. This is a reality for AbbVie Interns.
Join AbbVie's Pharmaceutical Technology team within Product Development, Science, and Technology (PDS&T) to support late-stage formulation development for a solid oral dosage form. This internship focuses on investigating excipient compatibility, specifically the interaction between common solid oral excipients and chemical stability. The intern will work alongside experienced formulation scientists and analytical chemists to characterize this phenomenon and help define strategies to ensure robust, high-quality drug product formulations. The intern will also present findings to department leadership and potentially contribute to an external conference poster or publication.
Key responsibilities include:
Investigate the mechanism of excipient degradation in the presence of pH modifiers using appropriate analytical techniques (e.g., HPLC, titration and colorimetrical methods).
Collaborate on LC/MS analysis to identify and characterize leachable degradants associated with the implications to stabilizing the drug substance in the formulation.
Evaluate degradation kinetics under varying temperature and relative humidity conditions.
Assess potential mitigation strategies, including formulation and process variables.
Summarize experimental results and present findings and recommendations to the project team and department.
Minimum Qualifications
Currently enrolled in university, pursuing a PhD in Pharmaceutical Sciences, Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, Materials Science, or a related scientific discipline.

The Associate Director, Pricing is the International pricing lead for RINVOQ . The role sets RINVOQ's International pricing strategy and preserves the integrity of RINVOQ's price across its indications and markets. It turns pricing analysis into clear guidance, robust business cases and accurate financial assumptions, and supports Area and affiliate teams in achieving broad, timely and sustainable patient access that reflects the value of RINVOQ.

Pricing Strategy and Guidance:
Develop and maintain International pricing guidance for RINVOQ (price corridors and launch and re-pricing recommendations) in line with brand strategy, the Integrated Access Strategy (IAS) and corporate objectives.
Apply the Strategic Pricing Framework to define the price potential of new indications and formulations, and recommend indication and country launch sequencing that maximizes International value.
Develop contracting guidance and access models that address payer objections and affordability concerns while preserving the integrity of RINVOQ's price.
Monitor International pricing policy and competitor pricing, and flag risks and opportunities for RINVOQ early.
Business Cases and Pricing Governance:
Lead the development, review and challenge of RINVOQ pricing business cases from affiliates and Areas, ensuring each is analytically sound, compliant with International pricing governance and ready for decision.
Prepare and present business cases to the Executive Pricing Councils, with a clear recommendation, quantified financial impact, risks and mitigations.
PVTO and IRP Analysis:
Build and run price-volume trade-off (PVTO) analyses to evaluate price and access scenarios, breakeven volumes and the net revenue impact of pricing decisions at market and International level.
Assess International Reference Pricing (IRP) implications of every proposed price change, launch price and confidential agreement. Quantify cross-country spill-over and recommend the sequencing and price levels that preserve the integrity of RINVOQ's price across International markets.
Work with International Pricing analysts to design, run and interpret IRP, PVTO and launch-sequencing models, and turn the outputs into clear recommendations for senior stakeholders.
Plan and LRP:
Own the RINVOQ pricing assumptions in the annual Plan and Long Range Plan (LRP) process, including price evolution, launch timing, price erosion, IRP impact and risk and opportunity scenarios.
Collect, challenge and align pricing assumptions with Areas, affiliates and Finance, so that forecasts are consistent and explained.
Cross-Functional Partnership:
Area and affiliates (primary partners): help key markets turn International pricing guidance into local outcomes, covering price potential, negotiation strategy, scenarios, fallback positions and objection handling for national and sub-national negotiations.

Finance: reconcile pricing inputs with Plan, LRP and business case financials, and agree the net revenue impact of pricing decisions.

Bachelor's degree in Finance, Economics, Health Economics, Statistics, Mathematics, Pharmacy or a related field.
At least 3 years' experience in pharmaceutical pricing, market access, health economics or commercial finance.
Strong quantitative and modelling skills, with experience building and interpreting pricing, forecasting or scenario models in Excel.
Working knowledge of International Reference Pricing and its impact on launch sequencing and price setting.
Ability to condense complex analysis into clear, concise recommendations for senior audiences. Excellent written and spoken English.
Able to influence without authority in a matrix organization, make sound calls on incomplete data, and challenge affiliate and Area proposals constructively.
Desired
Hands-on experience with pricing business cases for executive pricing committees, PVTO analysis and Plan/LRP pricing assumptions.
Knowledge of P&R systems in key markets, including Australia, Canada, China, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, Spain and the UK.
Understanding of HTA and health economic principles from a payer perspective.
Experience in immunology or another multi-indication specialty brand.

The Associate Director, Strategy & Operations, Practice Economics is responsible for helping build the structure, strategy, and operating discipline for a newly evolving Practice Economics organization within Allergan Aesthetics. This role will support the Vice President, Practice Economics and partner closely with the leadership team to translate strategic priorities into clear plans, governance, execution, and measurable customer and business impact.
This role is based in Irvine, California and will require close collaboration with Practice Economics leadership, cross-functional partners, and field-facing teams.
The ideal candidate will be a strategic, operationally strong leader who is comfortable operating in ambiguity, creating clarity, influencing across a matrixed organization, and driving disciplined follow-through on complex priorities. This individual will bring strong business judgment, executive communication skills, and the ability to connect strategy, governance, insights, cross-functional execution, and leadership communication in support of a newly evolving organization.
Key Responsibilities
Strategic Planning & Business Insights: Partner with the VP, Practice Economics and leadership team to define, refine, and execute Practice Economics strategic priorities, including annual planning, long-range planning, goal setting, prioritization, roadmaps, milestones, owners, and measurable outcomes.
Business Operations & Governance: Establish and manage the Practice Economics operating cadence, including leadership team meetings, business reviews, prioritization forums, governance mechanisms, decision-making processes, initiative tracking, and accountability routines.
Cross-Functional Initiative Leadership: Lead high-priority, cross-functional initiatives from strategy through execution by coordinating workstreams across Practice Consulting, National Accounts, Strategic Planning, Marketing, Analytics, Finance, Operations, and Field teams.
Organizational Effectiveness & Ways of Working: Help define and evolve the Practice Economics operating model, including workstream ownership, governance, decision rights, team interfaces, leadership alignment, role clarity, and repeatable processes that move the team from reactive work toward proactive planning and disciplined execution.
Executive Communications & Special Projects: Develop concise, executive-ready communications, presentations, briefing documents, strategic narratives, recommendations, decision points, and action plans for senior leadership audiences, business reviews, board-level discussions, and major stakeholder engagements.
Performance Management & Accountability: Develop and maintain dashboards, scorecards, operating tools, and progress updates that clarify performance, risks, dependencies, decisions, and execution status across key Practice Economics priorities.
Stakeholder Alignment & Influence: Facilitate alignment across stakeholders with different priorities, timelines, and decision rights while anticipating execution risks, removing barriers, escalating issues, and ensuring initiatives remain connected to broader Practice Economics strategy and customer and business impact.

Experience leading complex cross-functional initiatives in a matrixed environment. Healthcare, aesthetics, pharmaceutical, medical device, commercial excellence, or customer success experience preferred. Experience supporting senior leadership teams or helping build and scale a new function, center of excellence, or transformation capability preferred.
Skills: Strong business acumen, analytical capability, executive communication skills, and ability to influence without authority. title: Director, CMC Product Development
description:
About AbbVie
AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. For more information about AbbVie, please visit us at  www.abbvie.com . Follow @abbvie on  LinkedIn,   Facebook ,  Instagram ,  X  and  YouTube.
As a Director, CMC Product Development, you will bring together scientific insight, enterprise perspective, and cross-functional leadership to help transform promising assets into differentiated medicines. As a key member of the Asset Strategy Team (AST) and leader of the CMC team, you will develop and drive an integrated CMC strategy that enables the overarching asset strategy. Serving as the single CMC spokesperson and integrator for the asset, you will connect expertise across the enterprise to drive alignment, informed decisions, and successful product development. This highly visible role offers a unique opportunity to lead multidisciplinary teams, influence asset-level strategy and investment decisions, and engage with senior leaders, external partners, and global health authorities from late discovery through clinical development and transfer to commercial manufacturing. Through scientific judgment, enterprise leadership, and matrix influence, you will navigate complexity, manage risks, align stakeholders, and help advance innovative therapies that meaningfully impact patients’ lives.
0-3 direct reports. Scope: from late-stage Discovery through clinical development to technology and process transfer to commercial manufacturing sites.
Responsibilities:
Serve as the CMC leader, integrator, and spokesperson on the Asset Strategy Team (AST), connecting CMC strategy with the overarching asset strategy and ensuring clear, timely, and effective communication across the AST, CMC functions, and key stakeholders.
Lead and inspire highly matrixed, cross-functional Product Presentation and Device Strategy teams (PPDST) and CMC teams, creating clarity of purpose, aligning diverse perspectives, facilitating effective decision-making, and building a collaborative and accountable team culture.
Develop, communicate, and drive the integrated CMC strategy and development plan for complex assets, translating scientific and technical considerations into clear strategic choices, priorities, timelines, risks, and recommendations for teams and senior leaders.
Communicate with impact across organizational levels, translating complex CMC topics into clear messages and recommendations, proactively surfacing risks and opportunities, and enabling informed decisions by asset teams, senior leaders, and governance bodies.
Act as a connector across the organization and throughout the development lifecycle, from late discovery through clinical development and technology transfer to commercial manufacturing. Build strong relationships and alignment across CMC, Clinical, Regulatory, Quality, Operations, Preclinical Safety, ADME, Commercial, external partners, and other stakeholders, while mentoring and developing other CMC leaders and team members.
Build and sustain trust and credibility with team members, stakeholders, and leadership, leading through natural authority, scientific credibility, sound judgment, and influence rather than hierarchy. Leverage that trust and influence to align priorities, resources, and timelines across functions, navigate ambiguity, resolve issues, foster open dialogue, and build alignment around decisions that successfully advance the asset.
Shape and strengthen team culture by promoting scientific excellence, inclusion, collaboration, candid dialogue, entrepreneurial thinking, accountability, and a strong sense of shared ownership for the success of the asset and broader portfolio.
Lead a portfolio of programs across multiple modalities, which may include small molecules, biologics, antibody-drug conjugates, cell and gene therapies, toxins, devices, and implants. Program assignments will consider the CMC PDD’s experience and qualifications to set them up for success, while providing opportunities to broaden their experience, build new capabilities, and grow in the role.

The Facility Planner serves as a key figure in optimizing the use of an organization's physical spaces, ensuring they are both effective and efficient. Building and maintaining strong relationships with various business units and a diverse range of stakeholders to align organizational goals is key. By partnering with leadership, they develop strategic plans to reorganize groups, optimizing spaces to address the specific needs of different business units. Essential to the role is the enforcement of design standards, which ensures a consistent and functional environment across the organization. Reviews and manages service requests for renovations, handling projects from minor upgrades to large-scale transformations. Leading front-end planning efforts, the planner identifies space requirements early on and sets the scope. This proactive approach ensures that projects align with business objectives and are executed smoothly.
Responsibilities
Foster strong stakeholder relationships through proactive communication and collaboration, aligning goals with company values while maintaining transparency and recognizing contributions.
Gather and analyze data on space utilization, occupancy, and facility conditions to support informed strategic planning and initiatives. Understand data requirements by collaborating with the CAFM (Computer-Aided Facility Management) team to establish clear data quality standards and objectives. Understand what data is critical, the desired format, and any benchmarks for accuracy and completeness.
Optimize space, resources, and infrastructure to enhance efficiency, functionality, and cost-effectiveness within the organization.
Assess current and future space needs by analyzing organizational growth and operational demands to inform facility requirements.
Perform feasibility studies on space usage, suggesting improvements to maximize efficiency while collaborating with stakeholders to align facility planning with business objectives.
Strategically plan and manage space utilization, considering varying business needs to ensure optimal functionality.
Work closely with the design team to develop floor plan options and collaborate with the project management team to produce accurate cost estimates.
Develop comprehensive relocation plans for offices or facilities, ensuring alignment with organizational goals, timelines, and strategic objectives.
Utilize facility management software to monitor space utilization and manage service requests, providing timely and accurate project updates to stakeholders regarding status, milestones, risks, and changes.
Implement facility planning policies, procedures, and standards that ensure compliance with regulations and organizational values, while advocating change management initiatives to support workplace efficiency and innovation.
Bachelor’s degree required, with a preferred field in Facility Management, Architecture, Engineering, Business Administration, or a related field.
A minimum of 8 years of experience in space planning, facility management, or project management.

Strong analytical, problem-solving, and organizational skills.

Excellent communication and stakeholder management abilities.

Global Lab Solutions (GLS), part of Operations Quality Assurance, designs and enables the systems, capabilities, standards, and partnerships that strengthen laboratory performance, support pipeline progression, and promote consistent, compliant execution across AbbVie’s global Quality Control network. Within GLS, Global QC Product Governance translates product and analytical strategy into QC readiness by connecting R&D, Product Development Science & Technology (PDS&T), Operations Quality, and QC laboratories to ensure analytical methods, standards, critical reagents, and supporting controls are ready for reliable commercial execution. AbbVie is seeking an accomplished scientific and Quality leader for the role of Global QC Product Lead. This individual will provide strategic Quality leadership and governance for the implementation and lifecycle management of commercial analytical methods across AbbVie’s global QC network. Serving as a primary Global QC interface for assigned products, the Product Lead will integrate scientific, Quality, operational, and product considerations to enable analytical strategies that are compliant, fit for routine use, transferable, and sustainable.
The role provides independent oversight and decision-making for QC analytical implementation, including review and challenge of validation, co-validation, and method transfer strategies; assessment of laboratory capability and readiness; and determination of the QC method design needed for dependable commercial execution. Success requires deep analytical lifecycle expertise, enterprise thinking, strong risk-based judgment, and the ability to lead across a global matrix without direct authority.
Key Responsibilities
Lead the global QC analytical implementation and lifecycle strategy for assigned late-stage and commercial products.
Represent Global QC as a key Quality and scientific decision-maker in cross-functional product, CMC, analytical, validation, and transfer discussions.
Translate development analytical strategies into robust, compliant, and sustainable approaches for routine QC execution.
Provide strategic QC input from late-stage development through validation, co-validation, transfer, commercialization, troubleshooting, and ongoing lifecycle management.
Independently review, challenge, and approve proposed validation, co-validation, and analytical method transfer strategies from a QC implementation perspective.
Determine the final QC method design by balancing scientific requirements, product and regulatory needs, laboratory controls, network capability, and long-term sustainability.
Assess receiving-site readiness, including technical expertise, instrumentation, laboratory controls, capacity, documentation, and operational constraints.
Partner with QC sites and technical teams to identify and mitigate barriers to successful method implementation and reliable routine execution.
Lead alignment across R&D, PDS&T, QC Operations, Operations Quality Assurance, Regulatory Affairs, CMC, and product teams.
Provide scientific and Quality leadership for complex method transfer challenges, validation investigations, analytical issues, and cross-site troubleshooting.
Identify and communicate scientific, Quality, regulatory, operational, supply, and timeline risks, including clear recommendations, trade-offs, mitigations, and escalation plans.
Drive harmonization, platform approaches, reusable standards, lessons learned, and best practices that strengthen Global QC capability.
Mentor QC scientists and technical subject matter experts and communicate complex technical matters clearly to project teams and senior leadership.
Why This Role Matters
The Global QC Product Lead helps ensure that AbbVie’s analytical methods can be executed reliably where and when they are needed. The role strengthens commercial readiness, protects testing continuity and product supply, accelerates pipeline transitions into the QC network, and builds durable analytical capabilities that can be leveraged across products and laboratories.
Key Interfaces
R&D and BioARD analytical leaders; PDS&T analytical and commercial method leads; QC site management, scientists, and technical subject matter experts; Operations Quality Assurance; Regulatory Affairs; Manufacturing; CMC and product teams; and other Quality and technical functions supporting assigned products.
Bachelor’s degree with 16+ years of relevant industry experience, Master’s degree with 14+ years of relevant industry experience, or PhD with 8+ years of relevant industry experience in analytical chemistry, biochemistry, biological sciences, pharmaceutical sciences, chemistry, chemical engineering, pharmaceutics, or a related scientific discipline.

Comprehensive knowledge of the analytical method lifecycle and the transition of methods from development into sustainable commercial QC execution.

Demonstrated ability to solve complex scientific and operational problems and make timely, defensible, risk-based decisions.
Demonstrated success leading complex cross-functional initiatives and influencing outcomes across a matrixed, global organization.
Strong stakeholder management, organizational, and communication skills, including the ability to present recommendations, risks, decisions, and mitigation plans to technical and leadership audiences.
Preferred Qualifications
Broad experience across both analytical development and commercial QC environments.
Experience with multiple analytical technologies, modalities, product types, and/or global QC laboratories.
Experience supporting regulatory submissions, health-authority responses, regulatory inspections, or analytical-method-related commitments.
Demonstrated experience with complex analytical method validation, transfer, investigations, remediation, and lifecycle management.
Experience establishing platform approaches, global standards, technical governance models, or laboratory capability strategies.
Demonstrated scientific leadership through mentoring, capability building, knowledge sharing, and continuous improvement.

description:
About AbbVie
AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. AbbVie Analytical Research & Development (Analytical R&D) is a global analytical scientific organization responsible for all CMC analytical activities related to the development of AbbVie's pharmaceutical products.  Our scope includes AbbVie's diverse pipeline of innovative small molecule medicines and spans from the selection of Discovery candidate molecules through Early-Stage Clinical Development.  We are building a world-class team of scientists and leaders who will drive the advancement of industry-leading analytical capabilities and make meaningful contributions to advance AbbVie's pipeline of innovative medicines.  Careers in AbbVie Analytical R&D provide unique opportunities to work with global and cross-functional teams to drive exceptional science and innovative product development strategies.  We are looking for diverse candidates with strong scientific and leadership experience to join the AbbVie Analytical R&D team and can offer exciting and rewarding career opportunities for these candidates.
Position Description:
For the Principal Research Scientist I position, we are seeking a highly motivated and experienced data scientist to provide scientific and technical leadership for analytical data science, artificial intelligence/machine learning (AI/ML), advanced analytics, and data automation within Analytical R&D. The successful candidate will partner closely with analytical scientists to frame high-value scientific questions, engineer and integrate complex analytical data, and develop fit-for-purpose models, visualizations, and digital solutions that accelerate data-driven decisions across pharmaceutical development.
The candidate will perform and direct data science and application-development activities, mentor and develop scientists, and provide leadership across multiple projects and initiatives. They will conceive, execute, and communicate multidisciplinary strategies; translate between analytical scientists, statisticians, data engineers, software and IT partners; and convert innovative concepts into sustainable, adopted solutions with measurable scientific and business impact.
This role requires a strong combination of data science depth, pharmaceutical or scientific domain awareness, product-oriented solution development, and collaborative leadership. The scientist will help shape the Analytical R&D data science strategy, establish reusable standards and best practices, coordinate initiatives across a global network, and foster productive partnerships with internal data science, statistics, information technology, and R&D organizations.
Responsibilities:
Provide scientific and technical leadership for analytical data science, AI/ML, advanced analytics, visualization, and data automation initiatives supporting pharmaceutical development.
Consult with analytical scientists and project teams to define the scientific or business question, assess data readiness, select appropriate analytical approaches, and translate results into clear recommendations and decisions.
Lead the end-to-end delivery of data products and analytical solutions, including problem framing, data acquisition and integration, exploratory analysis, feature engineering, model development and validation, visualization, deployment, documentation, user adoption, and lifecycle support.
Develop and apply statistical, machine-learning, chemometric, and/or generative-AI methods to complex analytical data while ensuring approaches are scientifically sound, interpretable, reproducible, and fit for intended use.
Engineer, curate, and analyze structured and unstructured data from laboratory instruments, scientific systems, documents, and development workflows; improve data quality, traceability, accessibility, and reuse.
Design and deliver intuitive applications, dashboards, reports, and automated workflows that reduce manual effort, improve consistency, and enable scientists to obtain timely insights from their data.
Mentor, guide, and develop data scientists and scientific colleagues; provide technical coaching, peer review, and hands-on support, and create learning opportunities that strengthen data literacy and analytical capability across the organization.
Lead or coordinate a portfolio of data science initiatives, establish priorities and delivery plans, manage risks and dependencies, and communicate progress, value, and recommendations to project teams and senior stakeholders.
Establish and promote standards for analytical data assessment, model validation, software development, documentation, version control, testing, data governance, and sustainable solution support.
Build and foster a global network with Analytical R&D, Development Sciences, statistics, enterprise data science, IT, and external partners; connect teams to the appropriate expertise and facilitate effective cross-functional execution.
Identify high-value opportunities, generate new scientific proposals, evaluate emerging AI/ML and digital technologies, and champion responsible innovation that advances scientific understanding, development speed, quality, and operational efficiency.
Communicate complex methods and findings clearly to technical and nontechnical audiences through decision-focused presentations, reports, visualizations, and scientific publications where appropriate.
Ensure solutions and activities comply with applicable safety, quality, regulatory, data-integrity, privacy, security, and AbbVie requirements.
Bachelor’s, Master’s, or Ph.D. in Data Science, Computer Science, Statistics, Applied Mathematics, Engineering, Chemometrics, Computational Science, Analytical Chemistry, Pharmaceutical Sciences, or a closely related discipline, typically with a minimum of 14 years (BS), 12 years (MS), or 6 years (Ph.D.) of relevant industry experience.
Demonstrated experience applying data science, AI/ML, statistics, or advanced analytics to scientific, pharmaceutical, biotechnology, chemical, or other complex R&D problems.
Advanced proficiency in Python and/or R and strong working knowledge of relevant data-science libraries, statistical modeling, machine learning, data visualization, and reproducible analytical workflows.
Experience integrating, cleaning, transforming, and analyzing complex and heterogeneous data; working knowledge of SQL, relational data concepts, APIs, and modern data-management practices.
Demonstrated ability to build and deliver production-quality analytical applications, dashboards, automated workflows, or reusable data products. Experience with tools such as Streamlit, Shiny, cloud platforms, workflow automation, or equivalent technologies is desirable.
Strong understanding of model development and evaluation, experimental design, uncertainty, validation, interpretability, and the limitations and appropriate use of AI/ML methods.
Demonstrated leadership through mentoring, technical direction, project or portfolio leadership, influence across functions, and delivery of complex initiatives. Prior direct people-management experience is beneficial but not required.
Proven ability to partner with domain scientists, quickly learn scientific workflows, translate ambiguous needs into tractable analytical problems, and balance technical rigor with practical, fit-for-purpose delivery.
Experience with software-development practices such as Git/version control, modular coding, testing, documentation, code review, deployment, and lifecycle management.
Excellent analytical problem-solving, project-management, written and oral communication, and stakeholder-management skills, including the ability to explain complex concepts to diverse audiences.
Self-motivated, collaborative, and adaptable, with demonstrated scientific curiosity, creativity, sound judgment, and the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced R&D environment.
Knowledge of pharmaceutical development, CMC, analytical laboratory workflows, regulated environments, data integrity, or scientific data standards is strongly preferred.

Lead and develop a team of architects responsible for architectural oversight of COTS applications, integrations, and the technology roadmap within the group; set direction, coach on architectural rigor, and manage performance, growth, and staffing.
Define and advance the group's COTS application and integration strategies, translating long-term business and technology goals into actionable, multi-year architectural roadmaps.
Provide architectural leadership and oversight across major programs and initiatives — from vendor selection and COTS implementation through configuration, extension, integration, and lifecycle management — ensuring designs are cohesive, future-ready, and aligned to enterprise standards.

Serve as a senior architectural authority in governance and design forums, clearly framing trade-offs, risks, and recommendations across vendor capabilities, integration approaches, build-vs-buy-vs-configure decisions, and roadmap sequencing.
Guide the evolution of the group's COTS and integration landscape, balancing modernization, resilience, security, compliance, total cost of ownership, and vendor roadmap alignment in complex, regulated environments.
Partner closely with infrastructure, data, security, DevOps, and enterprise architecture teams to ensure the COTS application strategy is tightly integrated with broader platform and delivery ecosystems.
Mentor and develop architects and senior technologists, raising overall architectural maturity, integration/platform thinking, and modern application practices across the group.

Prior experience leading or managing a team of architects or senior technologists, including coaching, performance management, and capacity/demand planning across a portfolio.

Strong enterprise influence skills, with demonstrated comfort operating in governance forums, architectural review boards, vendor negotiations, and ambiguous problem spaces.

Experience with campus utilities, building systems, site infrastructure, or support facilities, including interfaces with cGMP manufacturing operations.
Hands-on experience managing scope, budgets, forecasts, schedules, risk, contractor performance, procurement activities, contract administration, and change control.
Experience leading multidisciplinary project teams and coordinating designers, contractors, vendors, Engineering, Construction, Commissioning, Operations, Procurement, EHS, and Quality in a matrixed organization.

Project execution and accountability: Converts portfolio priorities into practical package plans and drives deliverables to completion within delegated authority.
Technical and design integration: Understands utilities, infrastructure, building systems, and applicable cGMP design principles; integrates operational requirements, vendor inputs, and project interfaces.
Financial and schedule management: Uses budgets, forecasts, integrated schedules, milestones, and performance measures to identify variances and drive corrective action.
Commercial and contract management: Develops clear scopes, evaluates bids, administers approved contracts, monitors contractor obligations, and applies disciplined change control.
Risk management and problem-solving: Anticipates constraints, evaluates options and delivery impacts, implements mitigation, and escalates decisions with clear recommendations.

The Special Events Manager supports the planning and delivery of safe, secure, and well-coordinated events for a pharmaceutical manufacturing company. The role partners with internal stakeholders, event organizers, site leadership, and external service providers to identify risks and implement appropriate protective-services plans.
Events may take place at manufacturing sites, corporate offices, off-site venues, or other locations. The manager helps ensure that event plans align with company policies, site access and safety requirements, applicable regulations, and the needs of employees, visitors, executives, and other attendees.
Key Responsibilities
Develop and coordinate protective-services plans for company events, including meetings, conferences, executive engagements, employee events, and visits by external stakeholders.
Conduct or coordinate comprehensive event-specific threat and vulnerability assessments, incorporating available intelligence, threat indicators, historical incidents, attendee profiles, venue vulnerabilities, and operational considerations.
Develop risk-based mitigation strategies and provide actionable security recommendations to inform leadership decisions and protective-services planning.
Monitor and evaluate relevant security threats and emerging risks that could affect company events, personnel, facilities, or operations.
Translate intelligence and threat information into actionable recommendations, communicate changes in the threat environment to appropriate stakeholders, and adjust event security plans as necessary.
Assess event-related risks, locations, attendance, schedules, and operating conditions; recommend proportionate security measures.
Coordinate with event owners and business partners to incorporate security considerations early in the planning process.
Work with site Protective Services, facilities, environmental health and safety, emergency management, communications, legal, human resources, and other relevant teams.
Coordinate event access controls, credentialing, visitor screening, staffing, traffic and parking plans, venue security, and incident-response procedures, as appropriate.
Support protective-services planning for executive and other high-profile attendees in coordination with the appropriate internal teams.
Prepare event security briefs, staffing plans, contact lists, post orders, contingency plans, and other operational documents.
Oversee contracted security and event-service providers; communicate expectations and monitor performance.
Ensure event teams understand applicable site procedures, including visitor management, restricted-area controls, emergency procedures, and relevant manufacturing-site requirements.
Monitor event conditions and adjust plans in response to changing risks, schedules, attendance, or operational needs.
Document incidents, observations, and after-action findings; recommend improvements for future events.
Maintain appropriate confidentiality when handling sensitive event, personnel, operational, or security information.
Track event-related resources and expenses and contribute to planning, reporting, and continuous improvement.
Perform other related duties as assigned.
Bachelor’s degree in security management, emergency management, criminal justice, business, hospitality, or a related field; or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
Experience coordinating security, protective services, emergency management, or operational planning for events or complex facilities.
Experience working with cross-functional teams and external service providers.
Strong written and verbal communication, organization, and problem-solving skills.
Ability to handle confidential information with discretion.
Ability to manage multiple priorities and respond calmly to changing conditions.
Proficiency with standard business software and tools used for planning, communication, and documentation.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience in pharmaceutical, life-sciences, healthcare, manufacturing, law enforcement, or another regulated operating environment.
Experience with program development, development of policy and protocols, and scenario-based planning for operational readiness.
Experience planning events at facilities with controlled access, restricted areas, or sensitive operations.
Relevant professional training or certifications in security, emergency management, event safety, or project management.
Experience supporting executive events, VIP visits, or events involving external stakeholders.
Familiarity with incident command, business continuity, emergency response, and risk-assessment practices.

This position may require work at manufacturing sites, offices, and off-site venues. Event schedules may include occasional early mornings, evenings, weekends, or holidays. Success in this role means event organizers and Protective Services partners receive timely, practical guidance; event plans address foreseeable risks and operational requirements; providers understand their responsibilities; and lessons from events are used to strengthen future planning.

This position will serve as a technical lead across expression-system and strain development, fermentation, recovery, purification, and scale-up.
Recombinant production of short peptides can be challenging due to intracellular degradation, low expression, aggregation, and limited solubility. The successful candidate will develop and optimize practical strategies to address these challenges and advance robust, scalable processes for therapeutic peptide production. Lead recombinant peptide process-development activities, including expression strategy, host and clone screening, process optimization, and scale-up.
Design and evaluate expression constructs and microbial hosts, including  Escherichia coli  and yeast, for peptide production.
Develop and assess fusion-tag and carrier-protein strategies—including His-tag, GST, SUMO, and inclusion-body expression—to improve peptide stability, expression, host tolerance, and recovery.
Design and conduct clone-screening studies using microscale cultivation, parallel bioreactors, and other appropriate scale-down or high-throughput approaches.
Develop and optimize peptide recovery processes, including cell harvest and lysis, inclusion-body isolation and processing, and chemical or enzymatic cleavage of fusion partners.
Troubleshoot peptide-specific process challenges, such as aggregation, low solubility, degradation, incomplete cleavage, and co-eluting impurities; recommend and pursue appropriate solutions.
Interpret analytical results, including HPLC, UPLC, and LC-MS data, to assess peptide identity, mass accuracy, purity, and process-related impurities; partner with analytical teams to address characterization needs.
Evaluate emerging technologies and process approaches for recombinant peptide production, including genetic code expansion when relevant to program needs.
Apply AI/ML approaches, where appropriate, to analyze peptide sequence, structure, and experimental data in support of design, optimization, and candidate prioritization.
Communicate scientific plans, progress, challenges, conclusions, and recommendations clearly to project teams and other stakeholders.
Mentor junior scientists and provide technical direction in recombinant peptide bioprocessing.

Maintain a high level of productivity while managing priorities and timelines; follow applicable corporate standards for safety, quality, and compliance.
PhD with typically 4+ years of relevant experience, master’s degree or equivalent education with 10+  years of relevant experience or Bachelor’s degree or equivalent education with typically 12+ years of relevant experience is required.
Thorough theoretical and practical understanding of relevant scientific disciplines, with hands-on experience in microbial physiology and recombinant expression systems, particularly  E. coli  and/or yeast.
Demonstrated ability to independently design, execute, and interpret critical experiments to address scientific or development questions.
Experience developing or optimizing expression processes for peptides, small proteins, or other products susceptible to degradation, or instability.
Experience with strain or clone screening, fermentation, and process optimization; familiarity with bioreactors and scale-down or parallel cultivation approaches.
Demonstrated experience with preparative chromatography and peptide or protein purification, as well as peptide recovery and fusion-partner cleavage strategies.
Strong experimental design, data interpretation, troubleshooting, scientific writing, and oral communication skills.
Ability to manage multiple priorities and timelines and work effectively in a matrixed, cross-functional environment.

Experience developing or manufacturing complex therapeutic peptides, particularly GLP-1 or related incretin peptides, in a pharmaceutical or biotechnology company or start-up environment.
Experience applying genetic code expansion to incorporate non-canonical amino acids at defined positions using engineered orthogonal aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase/tRNA pairs and codon reassignment.

Adobe is seeking a leader to join our Public Policy Team and lead Adobe’s cybersecurity and fraud public policy engagement. The position will be based in Washington, DC, and will report to the Vice President Public Policy. They will partner closely with Adobe’s Chief Security Officer, as well as Adobe’s Vice President for Fraud.
What you'll Do
• Advance Adobe’s global cyber policy objectives in key markets around the world.
• Develop and implement strategic public policy outreach initiatives and advocacy campaigns to engage with key partners and government officials.
• Build and maintain positive relationships with government officials and influencers to promote Adobe’s interests.
• Keep informed of cyber-related policy developments and trends; coordinate with key collaborators to assess impact and provide updates.

• A distinguished track record of success.

Adobe Commerce powers storefronts for merchants and brands worldwide, making security, reliability, and scalability critical.

title: Senior Software Development Engineer
description:
The Opportunity
Typography is central to how ideas are communicated. If you're passionate about beautifully created design, have deep curiosity about what AI can do, and take personal responsibility for creating products that people love; then this may be the role for you. Adobe Fonts supports millions of creatives in choosing and using typefaces across fonts.adobe.com, Express, Photoshop, Illustrator, Acrobat, and more Creative Cloud platforms. Our Internal Services team provides the platform engineering and deployment backbone for all of these. We manage CI/CD, deployment approaches, the services and data layers our engineers depend on, our observability and security stance, and increasingly the agentic tools that transform how our entire organization delivers software.
We're seeking a Senior Software Development Engineer to lead this exciting journey in our San Francisco location.
What you'll do
Own and evolve our deployment platform. Lead strategy for CI/CD, PR environments, and release safety across a mixed fleet that includes containerized services, serverless services, and static front ends.
Build the foundation for AI-accelerated development. Help build our agent factory and grow our internal agentic toolkit and skill library.
Ship inference applications at scale. Take greenfield services from spec to production and standardize our ML/inference footprint.
Modernize our services for the AI era. Identify where an existing service is held back by its current build and lead the fix.
Rethink our security posture for agentic threats. Lead how we secure autonomous agents and their tool use.
Expose Adobe Fonts to the agentic ecosystem. Extend our Model Context Protocol (MCP) surface and conversational, intent-based font discovery.
Work higher up the stack, too. Contribute directly to search, browse, discovery, and the customer-facing experiences our platform powers.
Hold ownership over what you deliver to production, encompassing on-call support, incident management, and the reliability of the services and pipelines that the entire organization depends upon.
Set technical direction and multiply the team. Write the development docs, run the technical reviews, and mentor engineers.
What we're looking for
Software engineering
Deep full-stack fundamentals and craft — build, testing, code quality, code review — plus system development and production maturity: latency, scale, reliability, observability, and on-call ownership.
Ships and owns services end to end, and reasons fluently across the whole stack: front end (JavaScript/TypeScript, React or Web Components), application services (Ruby/Rails, Python, Go, and comfort picking up others), and the SRE/config/hardware layer beneath (Terraform, Chef, Kubernetes/Helm, AWS).

We are looking for a Senior Manager to lead BizTech Enablement and Innovation (BEI), BizTech's solutions partner to the rest of the company. BEI works with Finance, Legal, People, Marketing, Global Operations, Policy and Communications, Design, and other non-technical functions to understand how they work, turn their problems into working solutions, and make sure employees know about and adopt the technology BizTech provides. The team also brings what it learns back to BizTech product teams and vendors to shape their roadmaps. You will report to the Director, Tech Foundations.
The Difference You Will Make:
This is a strategic leadership role within a large business unit. For the next 18 months, the team's focus is AI. You will own the company's approach to AI adoption and impact outside of Engineering, set the vision for AI-enabled work, hold functions accountable to measurable outcomes, and serve as BizTech's primary partner to E-Team leaders on AI transformation.
More broadly, you will lead how Airbnb's non-technical functions discover, adopt, and get value from business technology. That covers quick consultations and fast-track solutions, go-to-market for new BizTech services, and building or buying new solutions where existing tools fall short. In the near term, you will define where Airbnb should be on AI-enabled work in two years, build the team and partnerships to get there, and make the trade-offs required to deliver it.
Success in this role is measured in business outcomes, not tool rollouts: functions that have redesigned their work around technology and AI, defined their own impact metrics, and can show the efficiency and quality gains, supported by a simpler tool landscape with fewer duplicate and unsupported tools.
A Typical Day:
Help define and own the multi-year strategy for AI adoption and impact across Airbnb's non-technical functions, aligned with company and Tech priorities.
Assess current gaps, existing capabilities, and emerging AI trends to anticipate how functions will need to work 18 to 24 months out, and translate that into a roadmap and investment.
Simplify the tools business teams use by steering them to supported solutions and closing the gaps that lead them to find their own.
Set organizational OKRs and success criteria for near and long-term initiatives, and hold teams and partners accountable for delivery.
Make and communicate hard trade-offs across competing functional demands, platform constraints, and budget.
Serve as the senior BizTech partner to leadership teams on AI transformation, including regular readouts to executives and senior Tech leadership.
Establish the framework by which each function defines, measures, and reports the business impact of AI, and drive adoption of that framework as a standard.
Build a metric-driven accountability culture: clear baselines, targets, and ownership for every function, with a single trusted source of truth for adoption and impact data.

Listen actively and anticipate where change will meet resistance.
Design and continuously refine the operating model that connects different technical functions and networks into one coordinated enablement system.

Partner with platform and product teams to influence the AI tooling roadmap based on the needs of non-technical users.
Direct external partner and consulting engagements, including scope, governance, and return on investment.
Set quality, reliability, and security standards for the AI solutions the team and functions build; own operational issues in production and drive the fixes that prevent repeats.
Make sure tech debt and the long-term upkeep of shipped solutions are prioritized across the team's roadmap.
Lead a multi-disciplinary, globally distributed organization including managers, Business Solutions Engineers, Systems Architects, and Program Managers.
Create a team environment that values constructive debate, risk-taking, and learning from experiments, and that fosters belonging across regions.
Build an 18+ month talent plan and a succession pipeline, including hiring at L10 and above.
Coach, mentor, and grow the team to communicate clearly, resolve conflict early, and build inclusive teams.
Pilot new technologies, including AI, with business teams, and hand proven solutions to product owners for long-term support.
Coach leaders across functions to connect AI capabilities to business value.
Establish mechanisms that turn learnings from individual functions into reusable patterns across the company.

Role model Airbnb's core values and strengthen the company's mission through the way AI is introduced to employees.

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Business, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
Demonstrated track record setting and delivering multi-year strategy for a company-wide technology or transformation program with executive visibility.

Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.
The Community You Will Join:
Airbnb, a leader in travel and hospitality, is on a mission to create a world where anyone can belong anywhere. We offer unique accommodations and experiences, crafted and curated by locals. As we expand into new marketplaces for in-person experiences and services, we are on the lookout for driven and innovative individuals to help shape our growth trajectory.
The Difference You Will Make:
Airbnb is seeking a Staff, Advanced Analytics, to support our Host Incentives team. This individual will play a pivotal role in supporting strategic business and product initiatives through detailed data analysis, experimentation, statistical modeling, and the development of reporting tools and metrics. The individual will be instrumental in building and scaling an efficient, effective incentive program for our hosts.
A Typical Day:
Own the measurement strategy for host incentives end to end, and drive the roadmap with limited direction.
Set the analytical standard for how host incentive programs are evaluated and act as the senior thought partner to Operations, Data Science, Finance, and Product leadership.
Work with large and complex data sets to solve a wide array of challenging problems using different analytical and statistical approaches.
Apply technical expertise with quantitative analysis, experimentation, data mining, forecasting and the presentation of data to identify trends and patterns that can inform decision-making.
Collaborate closely with Operations, Data Science, Finance, Product and other cross-functional teams to provide actionable insights.
Design, execute, and analyze experiments to measure impact and guide incentive iterations. Leverage causal methods when traditional randomized trials aren’t available.
Design and build metrics / dimensions to monitor product and business performance.
Build sophisticated reporting and analytical tools that empower stakeholders to make data-driven decisions.
Present findings and recommendations to stakeholders, including senior leadership, in a clear and concise manner.
Stay up-to-date with the latest industry trends and advancements in quantitative and qualitative data analysis techniques.
Leverage AI to automate repetitive tasks and empower stakeholders.
Your Expertise:
10+ years of industry experience with a degree (Masters or PhD is a plus) in a quantitative field (e.g., Statistics, Econometrics, Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, Data Science, Operations Research).
Prior experience in an advanced analytics or data science role.
Experience measuring incentive, promotion, pricing or marketing-spend programs, including incrementality and ROI, strongly preferred.
Exceptional business acumen, strategic thinking skills, and the ability to conduct rigorous analysis and make informed judgments.
Excellent communication skills, capable of engaging with a variety of stakeholders and conveying complex concepts in an accessible manner.
Proven stakeholder management skills, with the ability to collaborate and influence across functions.
Experience partnering with Operations and Finance teams to drive action and provide expertise and direction on analytics, experimental design, and measurement.
Experience in analysis of A|B experiments and statistical data analysis.
Experience designing and building metrics, from conception to building prototypes with data pipelines.
Strong expertise in at least one programming language (Python or R) and SQL.
An agile, growth-minded approach, demonstrated through a history of driving projects from ideation to impact.
Experience with AI-assisted analytics (Claude, ChatGPT, etc).

This position is US - Remote Eligible. The role may include occasional work at an Airbnb office or attendance at offsites, as agreed to with your manager. While the position is Remote Eligible, you must live in a state where Airbnb, Inc. has a registered entity. Click here for the up-to-date list of excluded states. This list is continuously evolving, so please check back with us if the state you live in is on the exclusion list  If your position is employed by another Airbnb entity, your recruiter will inform you what states you are eligible to work from.
Our Commitment To Inclusion & Belonging:
Airbnb is committed to working with the broadest talent pool possible. We believe diverse ideas foster innovation and engagement, and allow us to attract creatively-led people, and to develop the best products, services and solutions. All qualified individuals are encouraged to apply.

We ask that you only reach out to us if you are a candidate whose disability prevents you from being able to complete our online application.

Airbnb values diversity & belonging and is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity employer. title: Product Manager, NAS Ship Cost Optimization, NAS Ship Cost Optimization
description:
At Amazon, we're working to be the Earth’s most customer-centric company. To get there, we need exceptionally talented, bright, and driven people. This Product managers will be responsible for driving optimization efforts across various organizations and processes to improve shipping costs at Amazon. This includes defining the right set of metrics and processes, establishing ambitious goals and driving towards them, working with technology and operations partners to design, develop and deploy intelligent processes and improvements.
The North American Stores (NAS) organization is focused on continuously optimizing its P&L to drive long-term profitability. One of the most significant levers? Outbound fulfillment costs. The NAS Ship Cost Optimization (SCO) team tackles this head-on—leveraging technology for scale and launching innovative products that optimize costs systematically and with measurable impact.
This team has delivered over $1 billion+ in cumulative bottom-line improvements over the past four years by reducing packaging waste, correcting dimensional defects, optimizing regional fulfillment, and building Gen-AI products that reimagine how Amazon collaborates with selling partners. In 2026, the team is targeting significant savings through initiatives spanning cube reduction, AI-powered vendor outreach, regionalization strategies, sortability defect reduction, and improved placement—against a total addressable opportunity of $1.5B+.
As a Sr Product Manager on this team, you will own products and initiatives that directly improve the profitability of one of Amazon's largest businesses. You will develop a deep understanding of the inputs driving ship costs—placement, regional fulfillment, sortability, ship method choices, and dimensions—and translate that knowledge into products, policies, and partnerships that deliver hundreds of millions in savings. You will work across partner teams spanning Supply Chain Technology, Operations, Transportation, Finance, and Category Management, and you will leverage AI and automation to build the next generation of cost optimization products.
This is a role for someone who thinks in systems, communicates with precision, and thrives at the intersection of data, product strategy, and cross-organizational influence.
Key job responsibilities
- Own and drive the end-to-end product roadmap for one or more SCO initiatives (e.g., Cube Reduction, CRISP Gen-AI service, regional fulfillment strategies, or Sortability Overrides), from opportunity sizing through execution and measurement.
- Develop deep subject matter expertise in the inputs that drive outbound ship costs—placement, regional fulfillment, sortability tier economics, dimensional accuracy, and ship method choices—to identify high-impact opportunities others miss.
- Build and scale AI-powered products such as CRISP (Cube Reduction, Improving Sizing and Product Design), a Gen-AI LLM service that delivers automated packaging and product redesign recommendations to 20,000+ selling partners.
- Influence and align cross-functional stakeholders across VP-level organizations including Supply Chain Technology (SCOT), Transportation, Fulfillment Tech, Finance, Category teams, and Retail Business Services (RBS) to secure resources, resolve dependencies, and drive shared goals.
- Design and run controlled experiments to validate hypotheses, which enable product feature decisions and deliver results at scale.
- Define success metrics and tracking mechanisms (e.g., monthly flash reporting, ASIN-level cost attribution, vendor response rates) that create transparency and accountability for initiatives targeting $200MM+ in annual savings.
- Partner with Science and Engineering teams to improve targeting methodologies (dynamic ship cost impact models, out-of-stock probability signals, ASIN similarity algorithms) and automate manual workflows.
- Represent the team in leadership forums, crafting data-driven narratives that communicate progress, risks, and trade-offs to senior leaders with clarity and confidence.
A day in the life
You start the morning reviewing product metrics and triaging customer feedback to decide where to focus. Mid-morning, you are in a design review with your engineering and design partners, working through tradeoffs on a feature approaching launch. After lunch, you draft a working-backwards document for a new initiative, pulling in input from finance and marketing stakeholders. Later in the afternoon, you sit in on a customer research session to pressure-test assumptions before finalizing roadmap priorities. You close the day by updating your team on progress and aligning on next steps.
About the team
The NAS Ship Cost Optimization team is a small, high-impact product team that punches well above its weight. Over the past four years, the team has delivered $1B+ in cumulative bottom-line improvements to the Stores P&L by building innovative products—including the Gen-AI powered CRISP service—and championing cost-smart policies across the fulfillment network.
The team operates with strong leadership visibility at all levels, given the scale of results delivered and the innovative, AI-forward approach to problem solving. You will join a closely knit group that Thinks Big, earns trust through results, and works collaboratively across some of Amazon's most complex operational systems.
If you want to own products that move a multi-billion dollar P&L—and do it by combining analytical rigor, creative product thinking, technology-driven scale, and genuine cross-functional partnership—this is the team.

The Prime Video Global Beta Team makes sure pre-release products, features and services meet a high quality bar before they go live. We put new experiences in front of real users on real devices around the world, collect their feedback on design, function and usability, and give product teams the confidence to launch.
As a Senior Program Manager on this team, you will own betas from intake to final report-out. You will work with product, engineering, UX, QA and launch teams to define what each beta needs to prove, figure out how to run it, and translate participant feedback into clear launch recommendations. You will also help the program itself grow by using data and technology to make betas faster and less manual. If you are a program manager who is comfortable bringing many teams to a single decision, we would like to hear from you.
Key job responsibilities
- Own each beta from start to finish: set objectives, define entry and exit criteria, run the beta, and deliver measurable results back to the product team.
- Run the intake and prioritization process, working with stakeholders across product, engineering, UX and QA to sort competing requests and make clear go/no-go calls.
- Dig into participant feedback and program data, spot trends and risks early, and present launch-readiness recommendations to product owners and senior leaders.
- Design the participant experience, covering sample size, surveys, communications, device setup and support, while keeping the participant pool healthy for future betas.
- Improve the program's day-to-day operations, from intake workflows and survey templates to dashboards and reporting, and explore where generative AI tools can save time without sacrificing quality.

In the afternoon you might work out how to split participants between two overlapping betas, then write up a report that gives leaders what they need to greenlight a launch.

The Beta team is part of Prime Video's Automation and AI organization. We are program managers and technical program managers who each own betas end to end, partnering with product, engineering and business teams across organizational lines. Over the next year we are focused on automating more of our beta operations and using generative AI to turn participant feedback into insights faster, so product teams can get answers in days rather than weeks. If you want a role where your work directly shapes the quality of what hundreds of millions of viewers see, this is a great place to be.
