title: Sr. Principal/Director PMT, Secure Work Enablement
description:
About Amazon Web Services
Amazon Web Services (AWS) offers a broad set of global compute, storage, database, analytics, application, and deployment services that help organizations move faster, lower IT costs, and scale applications. These services are trusted by the largest enterprises and the hottest start-ups to power a wide variety of workloads — including web and mobile applications, data processing and warehousing, storage, archive, and many others.
AWS Applied AI Solutions (AAIS) is building toward a future where every business innovates with Amazon AI teammates. To get there, we build AI solutions that improve human capabilities and transform entire business functions. We create end-to-end products that surprise and delight out-of-the-box, making complex things easy and hard things possible, with no cloud experience required. We start with customers who embrace the future and build bridges to meet the rest where they are. We pursue ambitious opportunities with conviction, and we are looking for builders who share that mindset.
The Opportunity
For a decade, WorkSpaces has been exceptional at what it was designed to do: securely deliver a virtual desktop where a user logs in, applications load, work happens, the session ends. It is reactive by design—with no memory of what occurred, no understanding of intent, and no ability to act on the user's behalf. But work has changed. The modern enterprise now runs on three workforces: humans who set direction, AI agents that execute delegated work, and the systems that run the business. Non-human identities already outnumber human ones, yet no infrastructure layer governs all three within a single trust boundary. Whoever solves this—making the secure, governed path the fastest path—will define how the world works for the next decade.
Amazon WorkSpaces is uniquely positioned to lead this transformation. We are extending its trust boundary from humans to humans and AI agents working together, governed by default. This is not an incremental improvement but a reimagining of the workspace itself—from a platform that delivers applications and compute into one that actively partners with users: understanding intent, orchestrating workflows across systems, anticipating needs, and reducing friction at every step.
We are looking for a seasoned product leader to own the end-to-end product strategy for Amazon WorkSpaces and define the future of work at the intersection of human talent and agentic AI. You will treat the workspace not as a container for compute but as the orchestration layer where humans and AI collaborate—reimagining every surface through the lens of human-AI partnership, and making AI adoption effortless for enterprises that have rightly prioritized security, governance, and compliance above all else.
Key job responsibilities
Product Vision & Strategy - Human-AI Collaboration
- Define and evangelize the product vision for Agentic WorkSpaces—the enterprise platform where humans and AI agents work as one team across modalities—and drive the strategy to deliver it within AWS and across Amazon.
- Lead the strategic narrative with AWS leadership, enterprise customers, analysts, and the market, articulating why Agentic WorkSpaces is the control plane for the future of work.
- Own the product strategy for the organizational knowledge layer—a permission-aware shared intelligence that compounds over time, survives attrition, and gives every team member, human or AI, accumulated organizational context from day one.
- Design products that make security the accelerant, not the obstacle, ensuring the governed path is always the fastest path to business outcomes.
Business & Portfolio Leadership
- Lead pricing, packaging, and go-to-market strategy to accelerate adoption.
- Partner cross-functionally with engineering, design, sales, marketing, solutions architecture, and professional services to bring products to market at scale.
- Recruit, develop, and inspire product leaders who combine deep technical insight with the product judgment to build experiences that delight enterprise customers.
Cross-AWS Influence
- Collaborate with Amazon Bedrock, Quick, Alexa and Kiro teams to shape how AWS AI services are integrated and experienced within governed enterprise workspaces.
- Partner with AWS Identity, Networking, and Security teams to co-develop the trust boundary model that extends enterprise governance from humans to AI agents.
- Represent WorkSpaces in AWS-wide strategic forums, influencing how Amazon approaches the enterprise future-of-work opportunity.
A day in the life
Ideal Candidate Profile
You are a builder-operator who has shipped transformative products at scale and run them in production at enterprise grade. You make bold bets and validate them with data. You see AI not as a feature to bolt on but as a fundamental shift in how work gets done—and you have the product judgment to make that shift tangible, trustworthy, and irresistible to the most demanding enterprise customers. Energized by ambiguity, you have defined new product categories where no playbook exists, and you think in systems: the workspace, the agent, the identity boundary, the governance model, and the user experience are all facets of a single product thesis.
About the team
Secure Work Enablement (SWE), within the AWS Applied AI team, aims to empower millions of businesses to innovate and collaborate through AI-powered experiences where security is invisible but omnipresent. Our flagship WorkSpaces service has delivered secure cloud-based virtual desktops for over a decade—trusted today by over one million daily users in hospitals, financial institutions, government agencies, and some of the most security-sensitive environments on earth. title: Sr. Product Manager – Technical, Leo Futures, Leo Connectivity
description:
Amazon Leo is building a constellation of 3,000+ Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites to deliver fast, affordable broadband connectivity to customers around the world. The Leo Connectivity Product team is responsible for defining and delivering the end-to-end networking and service experiences that connect customers — consumers, enterprises, and the public sector — to the Leo network.
We are seeking a highly technical Sr. Product Manager to own product definition for future generations of Leo’s satellite connectivity system. This is a strategic, cross-functional role focused on identifying the customer problems we will solve with next-generation architectures. You will work at the intersection of vehicle engineering, software engineering, modeling and simulation, and the PMT teams building our first-generation network, constellation and customer devices — synthesizing insights across all of them to define what comes next.
This role requires someone who thrives in ambiguity. The problems are not yet well-defined, the solution space is wide open, and the timelines may be long. You will frame ill-defined challenges into actionable product strategies, drive system-level trade studies with modeling and simulation teams and translate technical possibilities into customer-centric product direction. This is a high-visibility individual contributor role based in Redmond, WA.
*** Export Control Requirement***
- Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.
Key job responsibilities
- Define the product vision and requirements for future-generation satellite connectivity systems, grounded in deep understanding of customer problems across consumer, enterprise, and public sector segments.
- Drive system-level trade studies in partnership with modeling and simulation teams — translating simulation outputs into product requirements and investment recommendations.
- Partner deeply with vehicle engineering and software engineering to understand technical constraints and opportunities that inform future system architectures.
- Collaborate with PMTs owning first-generation constellation systems and customer antenna products to identify gaps, lessons learned, and opportunities that shape future generations.
- Frame ambiguous, long-horizon problems into structured product strategies with clear hypotheses, evaluation criteria, and decision frameworks.
- Write PRFAQs, technical narratives, and investment proposals that articulate the customer need, technical approach, and business case for future system capabilities.
- Represent the futures roadmap in leadership reviews, clearly communicating trade-offs, dependencies, and strategic rationale to senior technical and business stakeholders.
A day in the life
Your morning might begin with a review of simulation results from the modeling team — a new trade study has landed overnight comparing architectural approaches for a capability that could unlock performance improvements for enterprise customers. You dig into the data, identify the assumptions that need stress-testing, and draft follow-up questions for the simulation engineers.
Mid-morning, you’re in a working session with vehicle engineering, walking through how a proposed design change to the satellite bus impacts the connectivity services you’re defining. You push on the customer experience implications and propose a set of requirements that preserve flexibility for future service evolution.
After lunch, you sit down with a PMT colleague who owns our payload software. Together you review field data and customer feedback, looking for patterns that signal where the current architecture falls short and where the next generation needs to leap forward. You capture three hypotheses to validate with simulation runs.
The afternoon is heads-down writing time. You’re drafting a narrative that frames a customer problem — one that doesn’t have an obvious solution yet — and propose an evaluation framework for the engineering team to assess multiple architectural paths. You end the day in a cross-functional sync, aligning vehicle, software, and simulation teams on priorities for the next sprint of trade studies.
About the team
You’ll be part of the Leo Connectivity Product team — a group of product and technology leaders responsible for defining the end-to-end connectivity experience for Leo’s customers. Our team spans device products, networking services, enterprise solutions, and future systems.
We value deep technical curiosity, comfort with ambiguity, and a relentless focus on the customer problems worth solving. We operate with a builder’s mentality — moving fast on the things we understand and moving deliberately on the things that require getting it right. We are a team that debates rigorously, decides clearly, and supports each other once a direction is set.
We are committed to building a diverse and inclusive team. We believe the best products come from teams with varied perspectives and experiences.
Basic qualifications: - Experience owning/driving roadmap strategy and definition
- Experience with feature delivery and tradeoffs of a product
- Experience contributing to engineering discussions around technology decisions and strategy related to a product
- Experience managing technical products or online services
- Experience in representing and advocating for a variety of critical customers and stakeholders during executive-level prioritization and planning
- Working knowledge of RF systems, propagation physics, spectrum allocation, and the physical-layer constraints that govern satellite connectivity performance.
- 5+ years of experience in aerospace, satellite communications, or telecommunications systems.
Preferred qualifications: - Background in satellite communications, space systems, or LEO constellation architectures.
- Experience defining products that span multiple customer segments (consumer, enterprise, public sector).
- Experience working with large-scale simulation and modeling systems to inform product decisions and system architecture trade-offs.
- Demonstrated ability to thrive in ambiguity — defining 0→1 product strategies where the problem space is undefined and the solution set is wide open.
- Proven ability to influence without authority across multiple engineering disciplines (hardware, software, systems).
- Experience with Amazon’s product development mechanisms (PRFAQs, narratives, working backwards).

description:
If you are interested in this position, please apply on Twitch's Career site https://www.twitch.tv/jobs/en/

Twitch is the world’s biggest live streaming service, with global communities built around gaming, entertainment, music, sports, cooking, and more. It is where thousands of communities come together for whatever, every day.
We’re about community, inside and out. You’ll find coworkers who are eager to team up, collaborate, and smash (or elegantly solve) problems together. title: Cellular ASIC Design Engineer
description:
Apple is where individual imaginations gather together, committing to the values that lead to great work. That happens because every one of us shares a belief that we can make something wonderful and share it with the world, changing lives for the better. Do you excel at crafting elegant solutions to complex challenges? Do you naturally prioritize the significance of every detail? As a member of our Hardware Technologies group, you'll contribute to designing, optimizing, and manufacturing our next-generation, high-performance, power-efficient cellular chips and system-on-chips (SoC). Your role will be pivotal in ensuring that Apple products and services can seamlessly and efficiently handle the tasks that make them beloved by millions. By joining this group, you'll be responsible for developing and building the technology that powers Apple's devices. We invite you to join us in delivering the next groundbreaking Apple products!
As a Cellular ASIC Design Engineer, you'll develop and optimize design and implementation methodology for integrated circuits across multiple focus areas including area efficiency, power optimization, and design technology co-optimization. You'll design innovative products at the block/IP-level and system-level in advanced process technologies (3nm, 2nm and beyond).
Your primary responsibilities will involve developing best-in-methodologies for optimizing Power, Performance, Area, and Cost efficiency metrics through various approaches:
DESIGN FLOW & METHODOLOGY DEVELOPMENT:
- Establish design guidelines, methodologies, and standards for synthesis, place-and-route, timing closure, and signoff processes
- Develop and optimize EDA tool flows including synthesis tools (DC/DCT/DCG/Genus/Oasis), P&R tools (ICC2/Fusion/Innovus/Aprisa), and signoff tools (PT/PT-SI/Tempus)
- Drive timing convergence process improvements across design teams to enhance design PPA and yield
- Create and maintain comprehensive design flows, scripts, and automation tools to improve design productivity and reduce turnaround time
PHYSICAL DESIGN & IMPLEMENTATION:
- Identify utilization bottlenecks in physical design and develop architectural, design, and implementation-level solutions to improve utilizations
- Work with physical design teams on timing closure, collaborating with CAD teams, IP teams and Design Technology teams for flow scripts/tools development and validation
- Understand RTL to GDS digital flow and provide hands-on contribution for timing signoff of complex SOCs
ANALYSIS & VALIDATION:
- Perform design technology co-optimization analysis, including optimal operating point analysis for performance/power curves and identification of scaling trends and bottlenecks in advanced technology nodes
- Conduct Spice simulations (Hspice/Finesim/AFS/Spectre/Infinisim) for PVT corners validation and STA vs spice correlation
- Perform timing package validation across advanced process technologies and timing signoff specification development
- Conduct in-depth analysis of design databases and silicon validation data to identify critical issues and improve overall design metrics
- Understand intricate timing paths (digital, analog, mixed signal) and timing constraints, providing solutions as required
POWER & PERFORMANCE OPTIMIZATION:
- Develop and implement voltage scaling and power optimization methodologies including clock gating, power gating, and dynamic voltage/frequency scaling techniques
- Use power analysis tools (RedHawk/SeaHawk/Voltus) for comprehensive power signoff and optimization
- Facilitate and drive STA methodology improvements using industry-leading timing tools and ECO methodologies
MULTI-FUNCTIONAL COLLABORATION:
- Collaborate closely with technology and IP teams to enhance efficiency through custom and semi-custom IP development
- Work closely with process technology, front-end design, physical implementation, CAD, and multi-functional teams to develop innovative solutions
- Support advanced process technology bring-up from PDK to VLSI design production
- Drive DFT (Design for Test) methodology improvements including scan insertion, ATPG, and built-in self-test strategies
TECHNICAL LEADERSHIP:
- Stay ahead of industry trends and emerging technologies to continuously improve design methodologies
- Apply strong programming skills (Python, Perl, TCL, Unix shell, C/C++) for methodology automation and enhancement
- Apply ML modeling experience for advanced design optimization and predictive analysis
Minimum qualifications: Minimum BS and 10+ years of relevant industry experience.
VLSI background with hands-on experience in RTL to GDSII flows.
Prior experience in doing Power, Performance, Area and Cost optimizations for SoCs.
Experience with SoC power flows & Vmin optimization.
Experience with Design Technology Co-optimization, identifying and solving scaling bottlenecks in new technology nodes.
Rapid prototyping and scripting of methodologies and test chip block implementation.
Preferred qualifications: Solid understanding of Physical Design challenges, proficiency with synthesis, place and route tools, and implementation exploration.
Experience with Metal stack optimizations.
Experience performing Early Tech node analysis to identify implementation bottlenecks.
Design Technology Co-optimization expertise.
Strong analytical skills and ability to identify and communicate high return on investment opportunities.
Ability to apply data science and ML analytics for Frontend and Backend databases, as well as post-silicon data, to identify trends & patterns and fine-tune implementation methodologies.

We are tasked with driving cellular radio technologies addressing GSM, UMTS, LTE, 5G NR and upcoming 6G standards. You will work closely with Platform Architecture, RFIC and PMU design teams, and suppliers to assess, scope, and ultimately drive Cellular RF technology innovation to meet the challenges of next generation wireless products. You have strong Technical Writing Skills.

title: Forward Deployed Software Engineer - Platforms Engineering, Enterprise Technology Services
description:
Do you want to help build some of the largest and most consequential enterprise and customer technology systems in the world? Join Apple’s Information Systems and Technology (IS&T) organization. IS&T is the engine behind everything Apple does for customers and for the people who build for them. It’s Apple’s central nervous system. Supporting 2.5 billion active Apple devices, processing billions of secure transactions, and keeping the technology that defines modern life running flawlessly, IS&T makes the impossible feel effortless.Do you love building solutions to handle global complexity and immense scale? Imagine what you could do here.
At Apple, new ideas have a way of becoming extraordinary products, services, and customer experiences. Bring passion and dedication to your job and there's no telling what you could accomplish. That same passion for innovation that goes into our products also applies to our practices, strengthening our dedication to leave the world better than we found it!
Most software engineering roles hand off testing to one team and operations to another. Here you own all of it. As a Software Engineer on Forge, you'll design, build, test, ship, and run the platform Apple's engineering teams build on, working closely with those teams to find where the infrastructure beneath them gets in the way and fixing it.
Forge is part of Enterprise Technology Services (ETS), within Apple's Information Systems and Technology (IS&T) organization, the engine behind everything Apple does for customers and for the people who build for them. Forge is building the platform Apple's engineering organizations can use to take a service from code to running in production. That path has traditionally run through a series of separate specialist systems. We are bringing it together on a common platform with a shared core, so a team goes from allocated capacity to a live production service without assembling the pieces themselves. Our job is to get teams to production quickly, on a platform that stays secure and reliable without them having to think about it.
Our charter is deliberately wide and still growing, reaching from the physical fleet in the data center to the surfaces engineering teams build against, and extending into new environments and new classes of infrastructure as Apple's needs evolve. We are a small team with outsized reach, bringing an AI-first mindset to how the platform operates and improves itself, and the best work we do takes one team's hardest problem and turns it into a capability every team inherits.
As a Forward Deployed Software Engineer, you will embed with the engineering teams who use our platforms, then build the software that solves their problems. This is a software engineering-first role that goes well beyond feature development: you will sit with a customer team to understand their applications and workflows, translate ambiguous requirements into a technical design, write the production code, integrate it with existing systems, and stay with it through deployment and operational readiness. We run what we build, so you will also share an on-call rotation for the services the team owns — which is the fastest way to learn where the platform still falls short.
The work spans Go backend services, React and TypeScript applications, REST and gRPC APIs, distributed systems, and automation that reaches into public cloud, private cloud, Kubernetes, virtual machines, and bare-metal environments. You will also build AI-assisted capabilities — LLM integrations, and agentic workflows — along with the evaluations and quality controls that make those capabilities measurable and trustworthy enough to run in production.
You will move comfortably from a technical discussion with an engineering customer to designing a solution, writing the code, and validating that it works reliably at scale. You will approach loosely defined problems with curiosity and sound judgement, and you will know when a recurring customer request should become a reusable platform capability rather than another one-off integration. You care about clean, maintainable code, thoughtful architecture, and operational reliability, and you are as motivated by simplifying an existing system as by building a new one.
In a team with daring goals and real autonomy, you will take utmost ownership of what you ship — and measure your success by the engineering problems you solve and the lasting improvements you leave behind in the platforms other teams build on.

Strong backend development skills in Go, or in a comparable language such as Rust, C++, or Python with the ability to become productive in Go
Solid understanding of software architecture, REST and gRPC APIs, distributed applications, and relational data modelling

At Apple we work every single day to craft products that enrich people’s lives. Do you love working on challenges that no one has solved yet? Do you like changing the game? We have an opportunity for a forward-thinking and unusually hardworking Physical Design Engineer. As a member of our wide-ranging group, you will have the rare and great opportunity to craft upcoming products that will delight and encourage millions of Apple’s customers every single day. In this role, we will be at the center of a PHY design effort working with architecture, CAD, timing and logic design teams, with a critical impact on delivering outstanding PHY designs. You will be required to do physical designs of outstanding PHY design.
As a Physical Design engineer you will contribute to all phases of physical design of high performance PHY design from RTL to delivery of our final GDSII.
Minimum qualifications: Bachelor's of Science in Electrical Engineering and a minimum of 10 years of relevant industry experience or equivalent.
Preferred qualifications: The ideal candidate will have deep design experience in high PHY and/or SOC designs.
Deep Knowledge about industry standards and practices in Physical Design, including Physically aware synthesis, Floor-planning, and Place & Route.
Experience in developing and implementing Power-grid and Clock specifications.
Strong understanding of all aspects of Physical construction, Integration and Physical Verification.
Shown Knowledge of Basic SoC Architecture and HDL languages like Verilog to be able with logic design team for timing fixes Power user of industry standard Physical Design & Synthesis tools.
Deep Understanding of scripting languages such as Perl/Tcl, solid understanding of Extraction and STA methodology and tools.
Deep Understanding of Physical Design Verification methodology to debug LVS/DRC issues at chip/block level.

title: Principal Digital Forensic Investigator
description:

In this role as a Principal Digital Forensic Investigator, you will serve as both a senior technical authority and trusted advisor to executive and legal team and you will craft investigative strategies to address some of Apple’s most critical legal matters. You will lead high-consequence forensic investigations into insider threats, data theft, media leaks, cybercrime, complex frauds and a variety of other concerns. The successful candidate will develop bespoke forensics solutions to address the rapidly changing world of forensics, foster strong partnerships across Apple’s businesses, identify security loopholes and develop risk remediations.
Minimum qualifications: Principal-level career experience (25+ years) leading complex digital forensic investigations for law enforcement (federal/state/local/international) and in the private sector.
Extensive experience performing digital forensics for high-tech crimes, including: trade secret misappropriation, insider threats, data exfiltration, media leaks, cyber incidents, internal fraud and national-security-grade matters.
Demonstrated expertise in developing bespoke data acquisition and digital forensic solutions. Scripting proficiency in Python and Bash.
Mastery of Apple operating systems (macOS, iOS, iPadOS, WatchOS) and corresponding core artifacts (e.g., Plists, SQLite databases, file system structures), as well as cloud forensics (iCloud, AWS, GCP).
Prior qualification as an expert witness in state, federal, or international courts, specifically regarding Apple forensics and digital evidence integrity. Extensive testimonial experience in civil and/or criminal legal proceedings.
Prior experience developing and delivering trainings on MacOS forensics to law enforcement and the private sector.
Deep knowledge of secure handling and storage for physical and electronic evidence in alignment with criminal/civil chain of custody procedures and industry best practices.
Prior employment as police officer, investigator or equivalent with US or international law enforcement agency.
Extensive experience interviewing witnesses and subjects of investigation.
Strong background eDiscovery collections, processing and data review tools.
Certification in DFIR, SANS, and/or relevant industry education.
Ability to deliver accurate, impartial findings with consistent attention to detail.
Strong verbal and written communication.
Commitment to integrity and confidentiality.
Preferred qualifications: Experience working with Fortune 500 companies.
Degree in Computer Science, Digital Forensics, Information Systems or equivalent.

Do you want to help build some of the largest and most consequential enterprise and customer technology systems in the world? Join Apple’s Information Systems and Technology (IS&T) organization.
IS&T is the engine behind everything Apple does for customers and for the people who build for them. It’s Apple’s central nervous system. Supporting 2.5 billion active Apple devices, processing billions of secure transactions, and keeping the technology that defines modern life running flawlessly, IS&T makes the impossible feel effortless.”
Do you love building solutions to handle global complexity and immense scale? Imagine what you could do here.
Infrastructure Services is part of IS&T and the foundation of Apple's global network operations — managing data center equipment and systems to deliver compute, storage, and networking services for teams across Apple, including its internal developer community. From individual facilities to a worldwide network, Infrastructure Services ensures the technology underneath everything works without question.
The Retail Compute Release Engineering team is looking for a detail-oriented and self-motivated Release Engineer with a passion for automation. The team owns the end-to-end software delivery lifecycle, driving release quality, process improvement, and optimization for the platforms and services that power Apple Retail Stores worldwide. As a release engineer on this team, you will be directly responsible for upholding the retail store experience for more than one million visitors to our 540+ Apple Retail Stores worldwide, as well as store employees.
In this role, you will work within a highly collaborative environment ensuring software releases are tested and validated prior to being released. You will help maintain, develop, and establish a solid and low-friction testing environment, providing a safe space where engineers can iterate and ultimately ship their code with confidence. We are looking for someone who is curious, has a passion for automation, and is eager to learn new things.
Your primary responsibilities include managing our code releases, maintaining a lab environment to validate changes across our codebase, and developing tools and automation workflows that contribute to this end. A core goal is to shift testing left, catching issues as early in the development cycle as possible rather than at the release gate. You'll participate in weekly code release reviews, dig into the details of proposed changes, and help surface downstream impact, including implications for vulnerability exposure, patch cadence, and release integrity, before changes are shipped. Knowledge of Linux OS's and software development practices will allow you to understand at a foundational level what a software change will actually affect.
Minimum qualifications: 5+ years of experience in release engineering, configuration management, or software engineering discipline (DevOps, SRE, Release Engineer, Site Reliability Engineer, Systems Administrator, or in a closely related role).
Proficiency with git and modern SCM practices, including branching strategies, pull requests, and common git workflows.
Experience designing, maintaining, or troubleshooting CI/CD pipelines (Jenkins).
Scripting and automation experience in one or more of: Python, Ruby, Go, bash.
Strong hands-on experience with Linux (RHEL or equivalent) at the command line.
Preferred qualifications: Hands-on work with configuration management and infrastructure-as-code tooling such as Puppet and Ansible.
Background operating software across geographically distributed environments.
History of implementing release strategies such like code freezes and canary/pilot rollouts.
Track record of producing clear technical documentation.
Proven success building or improving hot-fix and emergency patch workflows.
Comfort building and managing lab and testing environments.
Familiarity with artifact creation, code signing, and software supply chain practices.
Curiosity and a bias toward automating repetitive processes rather than tolerating them.
Comfort collaborating with multiple development teams.
Familiarity with GitOps tooling (Argo CD, Flux) and Kubernetes distributions such as K8s or K3s.

title: Reliability Engineer
description:
Imagine what you can do here. Apple is a place where extraordinary people gather to do their lives best work. Together we create products and experiences people once couldn't have imagined, and now, can't imagine living without. It's the diversity of those people and their ideas that inspires the innovation that runs through everything we do.
APPLE INC has the following available in Cupertino, California and various unanticipated locations throughout the USA. Develop new reliability tests procedures and specifications by performing failure modes effects and analysis (FMEA) to identify design and process specific failures and their corresponding use cases, detection methods, and performance evaluation criteria. Design of experiments to characterize user behavior to inform test spec development. Analyze instrumented study data to quantify subjective user experience. Prepare concise and detailed test plans and analyzing test reports. Weibull statistical analysis of data to provide quantitative risk assessments of anticipated exposure in the field by considering stress-strength analysis, acceleration factors, user perception/behavior, and test-to-field correlation. Present tests, test results, and risk assessments in a confident and positive manner to the cross-functional and leadership teams. Research new technologies to understand unique failure mechanisms by driving quantification of subjective user perception such as using machine learning image processing techniques. Guide design and interact with diverse groups to improve product reliability. Investigate failures during reliability testing to determine root cause and drive mitigations. Guide failure analysis to determine root cause through familiarity with characterization techniques such as SEM, TEM, FTIR, CT, etc. Collaborate with design teams to develop mitigations for failures in Reliability testing by leveraging expertise in mechanical engineering/materials science to inform solution space and scope feasibility of fixes prior to implementation. 40 hours/week. At Apple, base pay is one part of our total compensation package and is determined within a range. This provides the opportunity to progress as you grow and develop within a role. The base pay range for this role is between $150,400 - $225,300/yr and your base pay will depend on your skills, qualifications, experience, and location.
PAY & BENEFITS: Apple employees also have the opportunity to become an Apple shareholder through participation in Apple’s discretionary employee stock programs. Apple employees are eligible for discretionary restricted stock unit awards, and can purchase Apple stock at a discount if voluntarily participating in Apple’s Employee Stock Purchase Plan. You’ll also receive benefits including: Comprehensive medical and dental coverage, retirement benefits, a range of discounted products and free services, and for formal education related to advancing your career at Apple, reimbursement for certain educational expenses — including tuition. Additionally, this role might be eligible for discretionary bonuses or commission payments as well as relocation. Learn more about Apple Benefits: https://www.apple.com/careers/us/benefits.html.
Note: Apple benefit, compensation and employee stock programs are subject to eligibility requirements and other terms of the applicable plan or program.
Minimum qualifications: Bachelor's degree or foreign equivalent in Mechanical Engineering, Reliability Engineering, or a related field and 2 years of experience in the job offered or related occupation.
Experience and/or education must include:
Utilizing Failure, Mode, Effect, and Analysis (FMEA) to prevent reliability failures via design
Using reliability statistical analysis to predict field DPPM (defective parts per million)
Conducting risk assessments using field data and DPPM calculations to contextualize risk for reliability failures
Collecting field data and comparing to reliability test results to ensure correlation
Collaborating cross functionally to mitigate reliability failures
Creating Keynotes or PowerPoints to present key information for reliabilty issues to the cross functional team
Identifying root cause of reliability failures via failure analysis e.g. CT, SEM, x-ray
Preferred qualifications: N/A

Excellent problem-solving, critical-thinking, and communication skills.
Strong theoretical and practical knowledge of machine learning and deep learning.
Experience building and evaluating LLM/VLM-powered agents, including tool use, multi-step reasoning, planning, and context management.
Strong programming skills in Python and/or C++, and experience with a deep learning framework such as PyTorch or JAX.

title: Senior Engineering Manager, Multilingual AI - Siri
description:
Siri is used by people all over the world, in their own languages on billions of Apple devices. Global Siri makes that possible, working across engineering teams to bring Siri and the Apple Intelligence experiences built around it to users in every supported language and region.
This is a pivotal moment. Siri is evolving from a voice assistant into a deeply personal, agentic AI that understands your personal context, reasons on what's on your screen, and takes action across your apps, all built on Apple's foundation of privacy. Bringing that experience to every language and every culture is one of the hardest and most consequential problems in applied AI today: it requires close integration across large language models, speech technologies, multimodal understanding, agentic evaluation, and the large-scale data and platform systems that tie them together.
We're looking for a Senior Engineering Manager to lead a multi-team AI engineering organization, at the intersection of feature development, engineering architecture, and global language readiness. You'll define the strategy and execution for how Siri's next-generation intelligence reaches international users, set the technical direction, grow an exceptional group of managers and engineers, and partner with global regional teams to bring these experiences to users worldwide. If you want deep technical challenges, global product impact, and the satisfaction of seeing your work reach people in their own language across the world, this is the right role.
As Senior Engineering Manager for Global Siri, you will lead a group of engineering and machine learning teams, responsible for internationalization architecture, cross-functional integration, and engineering readiness of next-generation Siri and Apple Intelligence features. You'll be accountable for end-to-end outcomes: from defining the technical strategy and scalable ML architecture, through model development, data, and evaluation, to shipping production systems that run on-device and in Apple's Private Cloud Compute.
Your organization's scope will cover the full stack of international language technologies including:
- Language understanding and LLMs: establish multilingual and locale-specific scaling technologies. Work with foundation model and features teams on architecture, model behavior, adaptation, evaluation of intentional experiences, reasoning, and generation, including personal context and on-screen awareness.
- Speech and multimodal input: automatic speech recognition (ASR), text-to-speech (TTS), speaker understanding, and fusion of voice, vision, and text input across languages, accents, and dialects.
- Agentic capabilities: ensuring Siri can reliably take action across apps and services for users worldwide, accounting for regional apps, conventions, and expectations.
- Evaluation and data science: building state-of-the-art multilingual and agentic evaluation that tells us, with rigor, how good Siri is in each market and where to invest next.
- Data and platform: scalable systems for data collection, annotation, synthetic data generation, and language-specific representations and conventions, plus the tooling and pipelines that make launching a new language faster with each release.
You'll partner closely with Siri's Speech, Experience, Platform, and Foundation Model teams, as well as product, design, research, data science, and regional engineering organizations, to turn ambitious goals into shipped products. You'll be a visible leader across Siri and Apple Intelligence, providing regular updates to senior leadership and influencing roadmaps well beyond your own organization.
What you'll do
- Lead and grow a multi-team organization of ML engineers and software engineers, including managing first-line managers and senior technical leaders.
- Set the technical strategy and multi-year engineering plan for bringing Siri and Apple Intelligence capabilities to international markets, and translate it into clear priorities, milestones, and owners.
- Own key decisions on ML architecture and language technologies across Siri products and technologies; shape model and platform requirements through partnership with the teams that own those systems.
- Build scalable, repeatable systems and processes that reduce the cost and time of adding and improving each language, so quality scales with the number of markets rather than against it.
- Establish rigorous, data-driven evaluation for each locale, including agentic and end-to-end evaluation, and use it to guide investment and launch decisions.
- Lead data strategy, including annotation programs, data quality, and the definition of language-specific representations, conventions, and guidelines.
- Partner across Siri and Apple Intelligence, influencing teams throughout the stack so that international is designed in from the start rather than added later.
- Champion modern engineering practices and reusable GenAI-assisted workflows, to accelerate delivery while maintaining high quality and reliability.
- Attract, hire, develop, and retain outstanding talent, and build a team culture of technical excellence, ownership, inclusion, and care.
- Communicate the team’s strategy, engineering decisions, delivery progress, and cross-functional risks clearly to senior leadership and partner organizations.
Minimum qualifications: 10+ years of experience building software and/or machine learning systems, including 5+ years managing engineering teams.
Experience managing managers or leading a multi-team organization, with a track record of developing first-line managers and senior engineers.
Hands-on technical background in software and/or ML engineering, with depth in at least one of: LLM-based products, language technologies, speech systems, or multimodal AI products.
Proven track record of shipping ML-powered products at scale, with a detailed understanding of development, evaluation, integration, and release readiness.
Strong leadership, planning, and prioritization skills, with demonstrated ability to deliver complex, cross-functional programs.
Excellent written and verbal communication, including presenting to executive leadership and working effectively with people across a wide range of backgrounds and technical depth.
B.S. in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Machine Learning, Linguistics, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
Preferred qualifications: M.S. or Ph.D. in Machine Learning, Speech and Language Technologies, Computational Linguistics, or a closely related field.
Experience building multilingual or international AI systems, especially across multiple markets, languages, or low-resource settings.
Experience developing, training, or fine-tuning LLMs, speech models, or multimodal models, including on-device or efficiency-constrained deployment.
Experience with conversational AI, agentic systems, and evaluation of agentic or generative AI products.
Strong background in experimental design and data science, with experience building evaluation frameworks that drive product decisions.
Demonstrated expertise using AI-assisted software development workflows to accelerate engineering while maintaining code quality.
Excellent strategic vision, with the ability to set direction in ambiguous, fast-moving technical areas.
Working proficiency in more than one language, or experience collaborating closely with linguists and in-market teams.

title: Sr. Optical Safety Engineer
description:
At Apple, great ideas become great products, services, and customer experiences, faster than anywhere else. The Product Safety Engineering group within Apple's Product Integrity organization ensures that every Apple product meets the highest global safety standards while enabling the kind of innovation our customers trust and expect.
We are seeking a technically rigorous and collaborative optical safety engineer to serve as the Directly Responsible Individual (DRI) for laser and LED product safety. This role sits at the intersection of cutting-edge photonics engineering and global regulatory compliance — you will own the safety strategy for optical systems across Apple's consumer and professional product lines, from early-stage design review through certification and mass production. If you have deep expertise in IEC 60825-1 and IEC 60825-2, a passion for building safety into products rather than checking boxes at the end, and the communication skills to lead cross-functional alignment at every level of the organization, this role was built for you.
Apple's optical systems, spanning lasers, LEDs, structured light, time-of-flight sensors, and fiber-optic communication components, are among the most technically sophisticated in the consumer electronics industry. As the optical safety DRI, you will be the authoritative voice on laser and LED safety within Apple's Product Safety Engineering team, working alongside hardware, optical, firmware, regulatory, and operations engineers to embed safety requirements at every stage of the product lifecycle.
You will lead compliance efforts to IEC 60825-1/IEC 60825-2 and IEC 62471, conduct and oversee optical hazard analysis, drive certification, and own the technical relationship with external test laboratories and certification bodies. You will apply rigorous engineering methods, including FMEA, Fault Tree Analysis, and Design of Experiments, to characterize risk, drive root-cause resolution, and prevent recurrence across product families.
Beyond the technical work, this role requires someone who can communicate complex optical safety requirements clearly to non-specialists, write reports suitable for submission to global regulatory authorities, and present findings and recommendations confidently to both engineering and executive audiences. You will also work closely with suppliers and contract manufacturers to ensure optical safety requirements are correctly implemented and sustained through production.
Experience with ICT product certification frameworks, particularly where optical subsystems interface with server or communications infrastructure (IEC 62368-1, IECEE CB Scheme, CISPR), is a meaningful advantage in this role, as Apple's optical safety scope continues to expand into other product categories.
This is a high-visibility, high-ownership position for an engineer who brings both technical depth and the maturity to serve as a trusted partner across one of Apple's most cross-functional organizations.
Minimum qualifications: MS in Physics, Optical Physics, Electro-Optics, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a closely related field, plus 2 to 8 years of directly relevant experience in optical safety or photonics engineering
2+ years of hands-on experience characterizing optical and optoelectronic devices, including laser sources, LEDs, photodetectors, and fiber-optic components
Experience performing optical hazard analysis, accessible emission limit (AEL) calculations, and optical power/irradiance measurements
Experience conducting FMEA and Fault Tree Analysis in the context of product safety
Experience managing technical relationships with external test labs, vendors, and certification bodies to develop and qualify product designs
Excellent written and verbal communication skills; able to translate complex optical safety requirements into clear guidance for non-specialists, and to write technical reports suitable for submission to regulatory bodies
Strong cross-functional collaboration skills; comfortable working across hardware engineering, legal, regulatory affairs, and operations teams with competing priorities
Confident working independently while also being a reliable, engaged team contributor
Organized and detail-oriented, with the ability to manage multiple concurrent workstreams without losing accuracy
Comfortable presenting technical findings and recommendations to engineering and executive audiences
Preferred qualifications: PhD in Physics, Optical Physics, Electro-Optics, or Electrical Engineering - new grad to 1 year of industry experience or PhD with 2 to 4 years of industry experience in optical safety, laser systems, or related photonics applications
Working knowledge of IEC 60825-1 (laser safety), IEC 62741 (LED safety), and IEC 60825-2 (safety of optical fiber communication systems); ability to apply these standards to real product architectures without supervision
Familiarity with ICT product certification frameworks (IEC 62368-1, CB Scheme, FCC Part 15/18, CISPR 32/35) as they intersect with optical safety, particularly for data center or server products
Proficiency with data analysis, optical modeling, and automation tools such as MATLAB, Python, COMSOL, or Zemax
Experience with manufacturing process audits and supplier quality in the context of photonic or electro-optic assemblies
Familiarity with IEC TR 60825-14 (user guide for IEC 60825-1) or IEC 60825-12 (safety of free-space optical communication systems)

title: Video Processing Engineer
description:
Do you love problem solving in a collaborative environment and then having the results of your efforts benefitting millions around the world? At Apple, our Architecture group is responsible for connecting our hardware and software into one unified system. Join this team, and you’ll collaborate with engineers across Apple to design how all of our technologies work in unison! You’ll drive development of our renowned system-on-a-chip architecture and develop algorithms to improve image quality and enable new use cases. You’ll develop forward-looking prototype systems as well as build and deploy software development tools that will be distributed to the Apple engineering community and help build the seamless technology experiences we’re known for worldwide.
This role will be responsible for investigating techniques for improving video processing solutions along the quality vs. power axes. State-of-the-art video processing solutions often involve the use of Machine Learning, but this can be computationally intensive and not practical. There exists a computational gap between Machine Learning techniques and traditional methods. The goal is to find operating points in between that can leverage the improved quality due to Machine Learning when needed and fall back to traditional, low-compute methods when not needed. Examples of video processing solutions that can benefit from using a hybrid solution comprised of traditional techniques and Machine Learning based techniques include (but not limited to) 1) Under Display Camera enhancement 2) Motion Estimation for Codec, GGM and MCTF 3) Face ID processing. The result of finding hybrid solutions is better video quality and/or longer battery life on the Phone, Pad and Mac. You will be responsible for investigating hybrid video processing techniques that can be translated into efficient SoC architectures. You will be expected to be able to translate architectures into specifications and C-models. You will also be expected to work cross-functionally with other Architects as well as Design and DV.

• Generate architecture test vectors for quality validation.
• Write bit exact C-models of defined architectures.
• Support Design and Verification teams when verifying designs against bit exact C-models.

Then this is the opportunity of a lifetime! Cox Fleet, a national leader in mobile onsite fleet maintenance, is proud to announce open enrollment into our next FleeTec Academy class. 10 weeks paid classroom training; all travel expenses paid.

Further hands-on training by one of our technicians and a full-time job with us as a Mobile Diesel Mechanic in your market.

Real pay rates that you can afford to pay rent with and a predefined pathway for raises.

$19/h after that for 6 weeks

Then $21/h upon graduation.
Sounds like something you might be interested in. Apply now! Our class size is kept extremely small to ensure we can dedicate the time teaching our future technicians properly. We only have one spot in each geographical market we hire, so it will be competitive. Could that next hire, be you?

Desire to start a career as a Diesel Technician and become one of our Mobile Mechanics.
Bring a willingness and ability to study hard.
Dedicate 10 weeks away from home to be with us.
Maturity level to focus on the task at hand. This is not a summer camp, but a start of your career path.

Job Description
As a Product Manager for the Recon Solutions and Services release train within Cox Automotive, you will be responsible for the One Recon platform — a modern, unified technology hub designed to consolidate fragmented legacy recon tools and manual processes into a single, seamless experience for Manheim auction sites and their reconditioning operations.
In this role, you will translate business strategy and stakeholder insights into actionable product plans, define and prioritize requirements at the epic and feature level, and maintain a well-groomed product roadmap. You will collaborate closely with release train leaders and team members across product, engineering, UX, and operations to ensure timely, high-quality delivery of platform capabilities that maximize value for auction operators and support teams. Your responsibilities will span product discovery, roadmap definition in partnership with product leadership, stakeholder engagement, go-to-market planning, and identification of future platform opportunities based on organizational objectives and operational needs.
This role requires strong platform thinking, a working understanding of APIs and integrations, and the ability to balance strategic vision with hands-on product execution — ensuring the One Recon platform continues to drive measurable operational improvements and supports Cox Automotive’s leadership in auction reconditioning services.
Primary Duties & Key Responsibilities
Product Strategy & Roadmap
Partner closely with product leadership to ensure alignment on priorities, strategic direction, and planned work across the team.
Define and maintain the One Recon platform roadmap in alignment with organizational objectives and the operational needs of Manheim auction sites.
Drive innovation in platform capabilities, recon workflow tooling, and integration with vendor and auction systems.
Collaborate with product leadership to prioritize strategic initiatives and quarterly planning, with a focus on replacing legacy tools and eliminating manual processes.
Stakeholder & Market Insight
Conduct product discovery to deeply understand the problems and workflows of auction site operators before defining solutions.
Gather feedback from auction operators, operations partners, and internal teams to create clear plans for new features or enhancements that balance individual site needs with enterprise-wide platform value.
Analyze platform usage patterns, research operational trends, and identify opportunities to improve recon efficiency across Manheim’s auction network.
Serve as subject matter expert on recon workflows, auction operations, and the underlying systems and integrations that support them.
Execution & Delivery
Partner with engineering, UX, and architecture teams to deliver high-quality platform features and integrations on time.
Define epics and features that translate operational requirements and stakeholder needs into actionable development work.
Own product backlog definition and maintenance at the epic and feature level in close partnership with product leadership, ensuring clear requirements and delivery accountability.
Cross-Functional Leadership & Go-To-Market Execution
Drive stakeholder alignment through clear, consistent communication of platform strategy and release updates.
Support product marketing efforts including release communications, documentation, and enablement for auction operators and operations partners.
Build and maintain effective working relationships with auction site operators, operations partners, engineering, UX, and product teams across Cox Automotive.
Performance & Optimization
Monitor platform KPIs, feature adoption metrics, and operational efficiency indicators.
Identify opportunities for workflow automation, process improvement, and platform consolidation.
Support product issue resolution and continuously optimize the One Recon platform based on stakeholder feedback and usage data.

Bachelor’s degree and 2 years’ experience in a related field. The right candidate could also have a different combination, such as a master’s degree and up to 2 years’ experience; or 6 years’ experience in a related field

Job Description:
Forensic Accounting Managing Director - Litigation Support & Economic Damages
Essential Job Functions:
Economic Damages, Litigation & Forensic Analysis:
Lead complex economic damages and financial analyses in commercial disputes, including lost profits, breach of contract, intellectual property, business interruption, shareholder and other business disputes.
Develop, review, and defend sophisticated damages, valuation, and financial models using financial statements, transaction-level data, forecasts, market information, and other relevant evidence.
Evaluate opposing expert analyses, damages theories, assumptions, and methodologies; identify strengths, weaknesses, and alternative approaches.
Lead litigation support engagements from early case assessment through expert reports, depositions, arbitration, and trial, including preparation of expert exhibits and demonstratives.
Apply forensic accounting and investigative techniques where disputes involve allegations of fraud, accounting irregularities, asset tracing, or other complex financial issues.
Use quantitative analysis and data analytics to support damages calculations, forensic investigations, post-acquisition disputes, and other litigation-related inquiries.
Client & Engagement Management:
Conduct engagements in compliance with applicable professional, legal, regulatory, and firm requirements.
Manage a broad spectrum of matters involving investigations, litigation support, post-acquisition disputes, and insurance claims.
Lead a broad spectrum of matters involving economic damages, litigation support, forensic accounting investigations, post-acquisition disputes, and other complex financial disputes.
Position the team for successful engagement execution, quality results, and client satisfaction by clearly working within project parameters, managing resources and processes, and anticipating/resolving issues.
Serve as a senior advisor to clients and counsel, translating complex financial and accounting issues into clear, defensible analyses and practical litigation strategies.
Lead engagement execution, including scope, workplan, staffing, budgets, quality, risk management, expert-report development, and client satisfaction.
Manage engagement setup and completion activities, including conflicts, engagement letters, billing, collections, and other engagement administration.
Develop and maintain trusted relationships with outside counsel, in-house legal teams, executives, and other senior client stakeholders.
Recruit, mentor, and develop professionals across the damages and broader Disputes & Investigations team, including development of future expert witnesses.
Business Development:
Originate and expand economic damages and litigation support engagements through an established network of law firms, corporate clients, and referral relationships.
Build Crowe’s market position in economic damages and litigation support, with an expectation of developing into or continuing as a recognized testifying expert.
Identify opportunities to expand existing client relationships and cross-sell Crowe capabilities across forensic accounting, investigations, digital forensics, post-acquisition disputes, and other Advisory services.
Collaborate with Crowe partners and leaders across Advisory to identify disputes, litigation, and expert-services opportunities within existing client relationships.
Maintain and expand an external network of attorneys, experts, corporate decision-makers, and industry contacts to generate opportunities and strengthen Crowe’s brand in the disputes market.
Represent Crowe through relevant legal, accounting, damages, and industry organizations, conferences, CLE/CPE programs, publications, and other thought-leadership activities.
Develop a recognized area of expertise within economic damages and litigation support and contribute to Crowe industry and market initiatives.
Reporting & Communication:
Draft, review, and support expert reports, rebuttal reports, declarations, presentations, and trial demonstratives that clearly communicate complex damages and financial analyses.
Present complex financial concepts and conclusions to attorneys, executives, boards, arbitrators, judges, and juries in a clear and credible manner.
Serve as a senior client and counsel contact and, based on experience, provide deposition, arbitration, and trial testimony as an expert witness.
Basic Qualifications:
Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Economics, Business, or a related quantitative field required; advanced degree is a plus.
CPA, CFA, CFF, ABV, CVA, CFE, or other relevant professional credential strongly preferred. A CPA is preferred for candidates whose expert work is primarily accounting-based.
Minimum of ten (10) years of progressive experience in economic damages, litigation support, forensic accounting, valuation, dispute advisory, or related professional services, including significant responsibility for complex matters.
Significant professional-services experience with demonstrated responsibility for law-firm and client relationships, engagement leadership, team development, and financial performance.
Deep knowledge of economic damages methodologies and financial analysis, with experience in areas such as lost profits, breach of contract, intellectual property, business valuation, business interruption, shareholder disputes, or other complex commercial litigation.
Demonstrated experience developing or managing complex damages models and contributing substantially to expert reports, rebuttal analyses, deposition preparation, arbitration, and trial. Prior expert testimony is strongly preferred, but candidates with substantial second-chair or supporting-expert experience and a clear trajectory toward testimony will be considered.
Proven ability to manage multiple complex engagements simultaneously, including scope, budgets, staffing, deliverables, expert deadlines, risk management, and client/counsel expectations.
Demonstrated business development success, including an established network of attorneys and/or corporate relationships, a track record of originating or expanding engagements, and the ability to build a sustainable book of business at Crowe.
Strong leadership and people-management experience, including supervising, mentoring, developing, and evaluating professionals and building teams capable of supporting complex expert matters.
Exceptional analytical, problem-solving, organizational, and critical-thinking skills, with the ability to evaluate incomplete or conflicting financial evidence and develop independent, defensible conclusions.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including experience communicating complex damages and financial analyses to legal counsel, senior executives, and other sophisticated stakeholders.
Experience analyzing large and complex financial and transactional data sets and using those analyses to support damages opinions, forensic conclusions, or litigation strategy.
Advanced proficiency with Microsoft Excel, Word, and PowerPoint; experience with financial modeling, data analytics, and litigation-support tools is preferred.
Ability to travel and work additional hours as required by client needs, expert-report deadlines, depositions, arbitrations, and trials.

title: Associate, Enterprise Strategy & Planning
description:
About the Team
Our sales and partner management teams are the heart and soul of DoorDash, enabling us to sign and partner with top restaurants and New Verticals merchants to drive revenue and help our partners operate and grow their businesses. As DoorDash grows both in scale and breadth of offering, the strength of our sales engine and organizational structure must grow with it. Our Enterprise sales organization partners with the largest national and regional restaurant and New Verticals brands across the US and Canada, from signing new partners to growing and retaining our most strategic accounts.
About the Role
DoorDash is looking for a strong individual contributor on our Enterprise Planning & Strategy team to execute top company business objectives and help define the sales planning roadmap for our Enterprise sales organization, spanning restaurants and New Verticals.
Your responsibilities will range from strategic (designing quotas and incentives aligned to the company's goals and strategy, integrating new products into sales GTM strategy and building consensus among sales leadership) to operational (forecasting, designing compensation plans, driving plan implementation and ensuring key metrics can be communicated, tracked and commissions calculated). You’ll bring a strategic mindset and strong analytics to the design and administration of sales incentive programs, while building trusted partnerships with Sales leadership. This role supports our US and Canada Enterprise sales organization across multiple sales motions and role types. You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…
Own quarterly goaling and quota setting for Enterprise Sales teams across restaurants and New Verticals
Design, document, and administer sales compensation plans and SPIFFs
Track attainment and calculate payouts accurately and on time
Build forecast and target models that support the Annual Operating Plan (AOP)
Partner with Sales leadership, Finance, and Product to ladder sales goals into company goals and bring new products into sales GTM

New Verticals is an exciting team at DoorDash that is building and scaling new ways to delight our customers beyond restaurant delivery.
Our Central Operations team, part of New Verticals Strategy & Operations, is re-inventing how consumers shop grocery, convenience, alcohol and retail by making every store’s digital shelf match the physical shelf. We do this by onboarding new data sources that improve selection coverage, price accuracy, inventory accuracy, and the location data that helps Dashers find the store and the item. When these get better, consumers see what they want at the right price and receive it with fewer substitutions and refunds, Dashers shop and navigate faster, and merchants sell more. We are looking to hire a Manager to own how we onboard new data sources, external and internal, onto our ecosystem. title: Manufacturing Test Engineer - Dot
description:
About the Team
DoorDash is seeking a Staff Manufacturing Test Engineer to lead production testing for Dot, our autonomous road-going delivery robot. You will be the directly responsible individual for manufacturing test strategy, equipment, software, and fixturing at our final assembly site. You will also help define test requirements and acceptance criteria for subassembly lines and suppliers in coordination with our Manufacturing Quality team, and work with our Manufacturing Integration Engineer to productionize internal tooling. This is a hands-on role spanning prototype builds through production ramp. You will commission test stations, troubleshoot failures on the line, improve test coverage and yield, and ensure manufacturing processes consistently produce reliable robots. This role requires regular hands-on work in lab and production environments, occasional off-shift support during builds, and travel to supplier and manufacturing locations as needed.
You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…
Define the manufacturing test strategy and coverage for Dot components, subassemblies, and final robot assembly.
Design, procure, build, commission, and sustain test equipment, fixtures, electrical test beds, and production tooling.
Travel to supplier sites to deploy, audit, and repair test equipment.
Work with Integration engineers to specify & deploy automated test, calibration, flashing, and data-collection tools.
Work with Quality engineers to establish test requirements and acceptance criteria for contract manufacturers and component suppliers.
Partner with design, firmware, systems, quality, and manufacturing teams on Design for Manufacturing and Design for Test improvements.
Diagnose production failures across hardware, firmware, test software, fixtures, processes, and operator execution.
Track production test performance, including first-pass yield, false positives, cycle time, capacity, and equipment uptime.
We’re excited about you because…
Bachelor's degree in electrical, mechanical, mechatronics, manufacturing engineering, or a related field, plus 7+ years of relevant experience
Hands-on experience delivering and sustaining manufacturing test equipment for complex electromechanical products.
Experience scaling hardware from prototype builds through production launch and ramp.
Strong electrical and mechanical troubleshooting skills, including familiarity with debugging PCBAs, motors, lithium-ion batteries, and wire harnesses.
Experience managing equipment from requirements and supplier selection through commissioning, qualification, and production support.

title: Mechanical Engineer - Structural Simulation
description:
About the Team
DoorDash Labs is the hardware and autonomy innovation engine at DoorDash. We design, build, and deploy custom robotics and autonomous delivery systems designed to operate safely, efficiently, and reliably in urban environments. We are currently kicking off development on our clean-sheet, next-generation robot platform—rethinking the mobility foundation from first principles to dramatically improve efficiency, payload dynamics, and service lifetime.
About the Role
As a Senior Structural Simulation Engineer (Level IC5) , you will be the foundational structural analysis authority for DoorDash Labs. You will own structural finite element analysis (FEA) across our next-generation robotic platform, working directly on core vehicle architecture—including chassis systems, suspension, closures, and sensor enclosures.
This role will be heavily focused on  future-forward designs starting from the early concept phase. In your first 90 days, you will drive our architectural exploration, define early vehicle load cases, and make strategic software ecosystem decisions (including standardizing and driving our commercial commitments around simulation tools). As development advances, you will shift from rapid concept modeling to production-intent structural refinement and physical test-to-simulation correlation.
You’re excited about this opportunity because you will:
Build From Day Zero: Lead structural concept validation for a ground-up robotic platform, running high-velocity trade studies alongside chassis, suspension, and closures engineers.
Define Our Tooling & Workflows: Evaluate, select, and operationalize our primary CAE/FEA software tech stack (with an emphasis on ANSYS-based suites), negotiating capabilities and technical fit directly with vendors.
Establish Load Cases & Criteria: Formulate first-principles structural load cases, fatigue histories, stiffness benchmarks, and failure criteria for dynamic ground vehicle environments where little historical data exists.
Simulate Critical Vehicle Subsystems: Execute complex static, dynamic, modal, durability, and fatigue analyses on structural enclosures, cast and sheet-metal subframes, linkages, and moving mechanisms.
Drive Test-Simulation Correlation: Partner with physical test teams to correlate strain gauge, modal shaker, and dynamic field testing data back into simulation models to maximize predictive accuracy.
Influence Primary Architecture: Act as the math-first checkpoint for mechanical design decisions, steering CAD geometry toward optimized strength-to-weight ratios before parts hit prototype tooling.
We’re excited about you because:
Deep Structural Domain Expertise: You bring 7+ years of hands-on structural FEA and mechanical simulation experience (or an advanced degree—MS/PhD—with 4+ years) focused on structural integrity, stiffness, fatigue life, and dynamic loading.
Vehicle & Robotics Systems Background: You have a demonstrated track record analyzing moving vehicle architectures—such as automotive body-in-white (BIW), chassis frames, suspensions, structural battery enclosures, robotics, drones, or high-performance mobility platforms.
Software Mastery (ANSYS Preferred): You are an advanced user of industry-standard finite element solvers (ANSYS Mechanical/Workbench strongly preferred; Abaqus, OptiStruct/HyperMesh, or LS-DYNA considered) and understand solver theory, element formulations, and convergence troubleshooting.
First-Principles Mechanical Rigor: You possess strong mathematical and classical mechanics fundamentals; you don’t just hit "solve," but can gut-check stress distributions and shear loads with hand calculations.
Ambiguity & Green-Field Ownership: You thrive in early-stage product definitions where requirements are fluid, documentation is sparse, and decisions must be made quickly with high technical conviction.
Cross-Functional Communication: You clearly translate complex FEA stress tensors, fatigue curves, and deflection limits into actionable design guidance for mechanical design engineers and leadership.
Nice to Haves:
Prior experience establishing or transitioning a company’s CAE software stack from scratch.
Background in topology optimization, lightweighting cast/extruded aluminum structures, or composite material modeling.
Direct experience running durability and fatigue analysis on systems subject to rough-road, curb-strike, or cyclic vibrational abuse.
Working familiarity with CAD tools (e.g., NX, SolidWorks, or Creo) for rapid geometry defeature and design iteration.

DoorDash’s mission is to grow and empower local economies. By building intelligent, last-mile delivery technology for local cities, DoorDash connects people with the local businesses they care about — helping grow businesses and the communities that support those businesses. At DoorDash, there are three audiences that are at the core of every decision we make - our Consumers, Merchants, and Couriers. We bring their voices into the business in order to help set the strategic vision for all of DoorDash’s current and future products.

We're looking for a Research Operations Manager to be the operational backbone of our research team, and a driving force behind DoorDash's commitment to customer obsession. Every great product decision starts with a real voice: a Dasher, a merchant, a customer. You'll own the systems, tools, vendors, and AI-powered processes that get those voices in front of the people building for them, faster and at greater scale. You'll also champion a culture of experimentation and continuous improvement, so the research practice keeps getting better along with our understanding of the people we serve.
