location: Seattle, WA; New York, NY; San Francisco, CA; Los Angeles, CA
description:
About the Team
DoorDash for Business is building the premier corporate dining and benefits platform—helping companies of all sizes feed their teams through industry-leading products and meal programs. Our mission is to become the go-to solution for executives, administrators, and employees who need seamless, high-quality food programs at work. We move fast, operate with an ownership mindset, and are growing new product lines to better serve our corporate customers.
About the Role
As a Senior Associate on the DoorDash for Business Strategy & Operations team, you will help grow and run Self-Serve Meal Manager, our free, self-serve product that automates recurring meals for teams and offices. Because the product is self-serve, growth is product-led: customers find us, sign up, set up a calendar, and decide whether to stay without a sales rep in the loop. Your job is to make every stage of that funnel work better.
Acquire: Bring new teams in at the top of the funnel, both on the DoorDash platform (merchandising, in-app placements, lifecycle messaging) and off platform (paid, email, and organic channels).
Activate: Turn sign-ups into first orders through strong onboarding, and find and fix where customers drop off.
Retain: Keep teams ordering through a reliable, high-quality product experience, and catch the issues that cause churn before customers leave.
This is a role for someone versatile who will wear many hats: analyst, growth operator, customer-facing problem solver, and product partner. You will be expected to find a problem in the data, work out why it is happening, and drive the fix yourself. The role is built to grow. As the product scales, so will your scope and ownership.
You will report to the Manager, Strategy & Operations for DoorDash for Business and can work remotely or hybrid depending on preference.
You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…
Own the funnel: Analyze the self-serve funnel end to end, from visitor to sign-up to activation to repeat ordering. Find where customers drop off and run experiments on acquisition channels, onboarding, selection, and promotions to lift conversion and retention.
Go deep on the data: Write SQL daily to size problems, segment customers, measure lift, and tell a real result from noise. Build the dashboards and automated checks that let a small team support a growing customer base.
Work directly with customers: Email customers, resolve issues, and run proactive outreach to teams that are stuck, at risk, or churned. Hear first-hand why people stay and why they leave.
Turn issues into patterns: Translate individual customer problems into trends, then flag them to product and engineering with a clear call on severity: urgent and big, or real but minor, backed by the metric impact.
Improve reliability: Root cause order defects such as late deliveries, point of sale issues, and failed drop-offs. Work with merchants, Dashers, and support partners on fixes and track the impact on quality metrics.
Use AI to scale: Build AI-assisted workflows that flag at-risk customers, orders, and merchants, and replace slow manual analysis and one-off fixes with repeatable processes the team can maintain.
Influence the roadmap: Bring customer, merchant, and order data to product, engineering, and operations partners as clear recommendations.
We're excited about you because…
You have 2–5 years of experience in strategy and operations or growth, ideally at a marketplace company, a high-growth B2B startup, or an early-stage AI company.
You are deeply analytical. You write SQL fluently, are comfortable with large datasets, and can get to a root cause and turn complexity into a clear recommendation.
You have run growth or conversion experiments and can tell a real lift from noise.
You are hungry to learn and quick to pick up new domains, tools, and skills. You are versatile, happy to switch between analysis, customer conversations, and process building, and you want a role you can grow into.
You are comfortable in customer-facing work: writing clear emails, handling frustrated customers, and resolving issues with empathy and ownership.
You have a product mindset. You can spot patterns across customer issues and judge what is urgent and what is not, and you can make that case to product partners.
You are extremely comfortable using AI (e.g., Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, or similar) in your daily work to automate workflows, analyze data, and make faster, better decisions.
You own problems end to end, from diagnosis to testing to rollout, and are comfortable building processes in ambiguous, early-stage environments.
You communicate with clarity and influence, tailoring your message for customers, merchants, cross-functional partners, and senior leadership.

title: Executive Director, MISUMI Imprint Foundation
description:
About MISUMI Americas
MISUMI Americas, a division of MISUMI Group, is a leading provider of standard, configurable, and custom manufacturing solutions. By integrating a vast catalog of components with a world-class digital manufacturing platform, MISUMI Americas empowers engineers and procurement teams to accelerate innovation across the entire product lifecycle. With operations in the San Francisco Bay Area and Chicago, the company serves as a vital partner for the most innovative companies in the Americas.
About the Foundation
MISUMI Imprint Foundation is the first corporate giving organization in MISUMI Group 's history. It launched in October 2026 with a $2 million seed investment from MISUMI Americas and a mandate to fund the people who will build the physical world.
The reasoning is straightforward. MISUMI supplies the components that engineers design into machines, and as AI moves out of software and into factories, vehicles, operating rooms, and orbit, demand is rising for engineers, machinists, and technicians who can build hardware that works safely and reliably in the real world. The United States is not producing enough of them. The Foundation exists to widen that pipeline.
We make grants in three areas:
Scholarships & Access — need-based support for first-generation and underrepresented students in engineering, manufacturing, and supply chain, at four-year universities and community colleges alike
Maker Programs — equipment grants for manufacturing labs, engineering team sponsorships, maker spaces, and student hackathons
Industry–Academia Bridges — curricula built around real manufacturing problems, internship and apprenticeship pathways, mentorship and career support
The Foundation launched under the fiscal sponsorship of the SME Education Foundation and has filed for independent 501(c)(3) public charity status. Its defining structural feature is partner co-investment: MISUMI's global supplier partners are invited to contribute annually and join the Foundation Advisory Board, with seats at three tiers — Founding, Growth, and Community Partner.
About the role
This is a founding role. The mission is set, the seed capital is committed, and the board is in place. Almost everything else is yours to build: the first grant cycle, the review criteria, the partner program, the measurement framework, and the independent organization itself.
You will be the Foundation's first full-time employee and its public face — to universities and community colleges, to K–12 and robotics programs, to MISUMI's supplier partners, and to the press. You will report to the Board Chair and work closely with MISUMI Americas leadership, but the Foundation's day-to-day direction will be set by you.
We are looking for someone who wants the version of this job where the answers do not exist yet.
What you'll do
Build and run the grantmaking. Design the application, review, and award process across all three program areas. Source and evaluate grantees. Set award sizes and durations. Make the hard calls about what we fund and what we decline, and be able to explain both.
Grow the partner co-investment program. Recruit supplier partners into the Founding, Growth, and Community tiers. Run the Advisory Board, which convenes twice yearly to set grant priorities and announce awards jointly. Manage relationships with senior executives at some of the world's largest component manufacturers.
Complete the transition to an independent 501(c)(3). Work with counsel and the board to move the Foundation out of fiscal sponsorship into standalone operation — governance, policies, financial controls, audit readiness, and state charitable registrations.
Measure and report honestly. Define what success looks like beyond dollars granted, build the data to track it, and publish results — including the parts that did not work. Produce the Foundation's annual report.
Represent the Foundation externally. Speak at conferences and on campuses. Work with MISUMI Americas marketing on announcements and storytelling. Build relationships with industry bodies, workforce coalitions, and peer funders.
Build the team. Scope and hire the Foundation's next one to three roles as grant volume justifies them.
First-year priorities
Open and close the inaugural grant cycle, with a defensible process and a portfolio you can stand behind
Secure the first cohort of Founding Partners and hold two Advisory Board meetings
Complete the 501(c)(3) determination and operational transition from fiscal sponsorship
Publish a measurement framework and the Foundation's first annual report
Establish institutional relationships with a target set of universities, community colleges, and K–12 programs
Desired Traits
Seven or more years in philanthropy, workforce development, education, or a closely adjacent field, including direct ownership of a grantmaking or scholarship program — you have made funding decisions, not only administered them
Experience building something from the beginning. A founding role, a new program inside a larger institution, or an organization you took from idea to operating. Comfort with ambiguity is not a nice-to-have here
Credible with two very different audiences. You can hold a room of community college deans and a room of manufacturing executives, and you do not change your argument between them
Fundraising or partner development track record. You have asked people for significant money and been told yes
Working knowledge of nonprofit governance and compliance — 501(c)(3) requirements, fiscal sponsorship, board management, charitable registration. You do not need to be a lawyer, but you need to know what you are looking at
Clear writing. Grant guidelines, board materials, annual reports, and declines all live or die on it
Genuine interest in manufacturing and engineering education. You do not need an engineering degree. You do need to find this industry interesting enough to learn it properly
Helpful, not required
Background in engineering, manufacturing, or the skilled trades, or lived experience of a technical education pathway
Familiarity with community college and technical program funding, CTE, or registered apprenticeships
Relationships with FIRST, VEX, SkillsUSA, SME, NAM, the Manufacturing Institute, or similar
Experience inside a corporate foundation, or navigating the relationship between a foundation and its corporate parent
Japanese language ability or experience working across U.S. and Japanese organizations
What we offer
The chance to build a foundation from its first grant, with committed capital and a board that wants it to be independent
Competitive salary, health coverage, retirement contribution, and paid time off
Remote-first, with travel to campuses, partner sites, MISUMI Americas offices, and the Advisory Board convenings
A mandate that is deliberately broad, because the talent pipeline will change and we intend to change with it
Physical Demands
The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Ability to travel 25–30% annually within the United States for campus and grantee site visits, partner site visits, Advisory Board convenings (twice yearly), MISUMI Americas offices in the San Francisco Bay Area and Chicago, and industry conferences.
Occasional international travel as the Foundation's work extends beyond the U.S.
Salary Range: $215,000 to $250,000 per year, based on experience and location

We’re actively seeking teammates who:
Bring diverse perspectives and experience to our culture and company.
Excel at being part of a strong, empathetic team.
Thrive in an environment emphasizing respect, honesty, collaboration, and growth.
Have an ‘always learning’ mindset that celebrates learning, not just wins.
Help us continue to build a world-class organization that values the contributions of all of our teammates

Today, companies of all sizes—from emerging brands to Fortune 500s—use Flexport technology to move more than $19B of merchandise across 112 countries a year.
The recent global supply chain crisis has put Flexport center stage as we continue to play a pivotal role in how goods move around the world. We are proud to have the support of the best investors in the game who believe in our mission, solutions and people. Ready to tackle global challenges that impact business, society, and the environment? Come join us.
Build the operational and technical skill set that runs global trade
At Flexport, we believe global trade can move the human race forward. We're shaping the future of a $10T industry with technology and people who understand it end to end. The Rotational Development Program (RDP) exists because that combination — real supply chain fluency plus the ability to build and automate — doesn't exist at scale in the market today. So we're building it ourselves.
This is an 18-month program, not a rotation for rotation's sake. Every assignment is live, revenue-generating work. Every participant leaves with a certification in AI and low-code tooling running alongside their operational and commercial training. And every graduate places into a role with real scope: primarily Account Management, with paths into Automation Engineering, Forward Deployed Engineering/Consulting, Sales Engineering, or a traditional Ops/Sales/Customs track.
What you'll do
You'll rotate through three functions, six months each, with AI/low-code curriculum running continuously across all three:
Gateway Ops (Air or Ocean). Own the shipment lifecycle. Execute bookings, manage exceptions, and hold data integrity to Flexport's standard. Build your first automation and reporting skills through structured coursework running in parallel.
Customs. Become a global trade expert by navigating the complex world of customs regulations to ensure goods comply with international laws. Simultaneously, move into applied technical work: SQL, workflow automation, Lean process improvement, etc.
Sales / Account Management. Take on go-to-market work and build client-facing skills, operating with more independence. Your capstone: identify a real business problem in the function you're sitting in and build the tooling or process fix that solves it. You'll present it to leadership at graduation.
Throughout the program, you'll get:
A day-to-day manager in your current rotation and a Rotation Program Manager tracking your development, with mid-point and end-of-rotation evaluations at every stage.
Certifications in AI/low-code tooling, from foundational bootcamp through applied builds to a capstone project.
Bi-weekly cohort touchpoints and a standing alumni mentor community.
Increased earning potential as you clear program benchmarks
This role is for you if you
Are on track to graduate, or recently graduated, and want to build a career at the intersection of supply chain operations and technology — not just run one or the other.
Are genuinely curious about AI and low-code tooling and want to build real fluency, not just check a resume box.
Can operate with minimal supervision, prioritize a high volume of work, and communicate clearly under pressure.
Want real ownership fast? This program hands you live client and business work from the very beginning — it is not a shadowing or classroom based program.
Have a "compliance-first" mindset. We operate in a heavily regulated industry, and that matters in every rotation.
Ready to build the future of global trade — and the skill set to run it?
Apply now.

description:
Fortune Brands Innovations (NYSE: FBIN) is an industry-leading home, security and digital products company with a portfolio of trusted brands, including Moen, House of Rohl, Therma-Tru, Larson, Master Lock, Yale residential, and Sentry Safe.
We are building a company that is determined to win, and we are clear about how: strong brands, great people, and disciplined execution.

Fortune Brands Innovations is hiring a Manager, Product Integrity to join our Connected Products team .  Product Integrity is the team that confirms our connected products — Flo by Moen water devices, Yale and August smart locks, and Master Lock connected padlocks — do what their requirements say they do before they reach a customer. This role leads that team and owns the bridge between requirements and proof: taking what Product, Systems Architecture, and Compliance ask for and turning it into tests with a method, a sample size, and a pass/fail criterion.
The role also owns 100% end-of-line testing at the factory, including test fixture design and test software. Depending on test complexity, fixtures are built fully in-house or developed with a supplier.
We are looking for a systems architect who leads a test team . The right person understands the whole product — electrical, mechanical, firmware, and how they interact — well enough to argue a requirement with Product, an interface with Architecture, and the statistics with Reliability, and then run the lab that proves it.
Position location: this position is eligible to work in a hybrid environment out of our North Olmsted, OH or San Francisco, CA locations.
What you will own

The Maintenance Technician at Alpine, a division of ITW, plays a critical role in keeping production, warehouse, and facility equipment operating safely, reliably, and efficiently. Perform electro-mechanical, hydraulic, and pneumatic troubleshooting, repairs, and preventive maintenance on production, warehouse, facility, and plant equipment.

Program and support PLCs and VFD-controlled equipment as needed to maintain reliable operations.
Rebuild equipment, fabricate replacement parts using machine shop equipment, and maintain MRO inventory levels.

Strong electro-mechanical aptitude with working knowledge of electrical systems, motors, PLCs, VFDs, hydraulics, and pneumatics.
Ability to read and interpret schematics, maintenance documentation, and technical instructions.
Experience using machine shop equipment, hand tools, forklifts, and material handling equipment.
Ability to troubleshoot complex equipment issues, analyze data, and work independently in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.

Join a collaborative manufacturing team where your technical expertise directly impacts operational success. Job Description:
SUMMARY
Responsible for supplying raw materials and supplies to production lines using very methods and tools.
ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Follows all company safety rules and policies.
Orders and releases raw materials.
Liaises between production and purchasing.
Conducts inventory and cycle counts and investigations.
Reads work orders, production schedules or follows visual and oral instructions to determine materials to be moved, what parts are to be retrieved from receiving and where on the production line to position the specific parts for use by production employees.
Knows, or can learn, manufacturing processes, receiving and production floor parts inventory procedures.
Owns the kanban replenishment process, including maintenance of kanban bins/locations, visual parts, setup, and proper replenishment requests.
Removes and delivers damaged parts off the production floor to the proper site.
Operates forklift in a safe productive manner.
Works cooperatively and congenially with co-workers to achieve cohesive and productive work processes and work environment.
Performs additional tasks as assigned by management or as the situation requires.
QUALIFICATIONS
Ability to follow verbal and written instructions.
Ability to read and follow work orders.
Ability to perform basic computer operation tasks and capable of learning programs used in kanban and production areas of the company including ERP Software, spreadsheets, and email.
Possess a certified forklift operator license and a minimum of one-year experience. OSHA trained.
Familiarity or ability to learn lean flow manufacturing concepts.
PHYSICAL DEMANDS & WORK ENVIRONMENT
Attend work regularly and report promptly for duty on the days and at the times scheduled by the supervisor.
Schedule changes occur and should be handled in a productive manner
Working temperatures vary with seasonal changes and climate control is limited. The environment is one in which noise exists.
Sit on a forklift, stand, and/or walk for a combined minimum of eight (8) hours per day on a concrete surface.
Lift and carry components, tools, or other items weighing more than 35 pounds. Any item over 35 pounds, is to be done with assistance
May perform combination of physical movements to reach areas difficult to access including bending, stooping, squatting, reaching, twisting and rotation motions using head/neck, arms, wrists, waist, knees and arms while performing duties.
Pull and push up to 100 pounds.
Handle small hand tools and power tools. Handling may be done unilaterally (one-handed) or bilaterally (two-handed) depending on size and shape of object and task being performed.
Need corrected vision to be aware of surroundings and location of items needed and perform various other job duties.
Need corrected hearing to identify conditions in the environment (i.e. forklift horns, fire alarms).
Need mental alertness to identify, avoid, or resolve safety hazards.
Ability to communicate with supervisors and co-workers.
Ability to wear designated personal protective equipment for the work assignment (i.e. safety glasses, safety shoes, hearing protection, cut-resistant gloves, cut resistant sleeves, dust masks).
Hours of Work
Monday – Friday – 6:00am to 2:30pm and OT when required

title: Production Team Lead
description:
Job Description:
Loma Systems® is a premier manufacturer of inspection equipment used to identify contaminants and product defects in the food and pharmaceutical industries. Established in the UK in the 1960’s, Loma Systems is today one of the leading global companies involved in production line safety systems, boasting an impressive installed base of over 125,000 machines in over 100 countries. Our talented team of people work across the world in a friendly, supportive work environment and with a no politics culture, there is nothing to stop you reaching your full potential.
We are part of Illinois Tool Works (ITW), a global Fortune 250 diversified industrial manufacturer of value-added consumables and speciality equipment with related service businesses. Operating under the core philosophies of 80/20 business processes, customer-back innovation and a decentralized entrepreneurial culture, the company focuses on solid growth, improving profitability and strong returns across its worldwide platforms and divisions. These divisions serve customers and markets around the globe, with significant presence in developed and emerging markets. ITW’s revenue totaled US$14.5 billion in 2021, with nearly 45,000 employees worldwide.
Production Team Leader
Location: Carol Stream, IL
The Production Team Leader is responsible for the day-to-day leadership, planning and execution of North American production. The role has full line-management responsibility for the production team and ensures equipment is built safely, meets quality requirements and is completed in line with agreed delivery commitments.
Combining visible shop-floor leadership with practical operational coordination, the position owns production scheduling, capacity planning, Kanban execution and daily production performance. The role works closely with Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering / Quality, Supply Chain, Logistics and Customer Experience to maintain material and technical readiness, resolve constraints and improve production processes.
Responsibilities:
Team leadership and development
Lead, coach and develop the production team, setting clear expectations for safety, quality, delivery, productivity and workplace standards.
Manage daily work allocation, attendance, leave planning and performance reviews; address performance concerns with support from Human Resources and the Operations & Engineering Director.
Maintain regular shop-floor presence, build effective working relationships and involve employees in identifying and implementing improvements.
Maintain a team skills matrix and coordinate training and cross-training with Manufacturing Engineering and Engineering to improve capability, flexibility and coverage.
Production scheduling and capacity planning
Own and maintain a documented production schedule showing job priorities, assigned resources, expected effort, key milestones and completion dates.
Review available capacity against workload, employee skills, planned absence and material and engineering constraints; identify risks and propose practical recovery actions.
Assess requests to bring forward, defer or add orders, communicating achievable dates and the impact on existing commitments to Regional Sales Managers and Customer Experience.
Coordinate engineering release and technical readiness with the Engineering Team Leader and material availability with the Senior Buyer before confirming production plans.
Daily production flow and material readiness
Lead daily production meetings, to review progress, shortages, quality concerns, shipping priorities and actions with clear owners and due dates.
Manage daily production flow, work in progress and line clearance, keeping job status and operational records accurate and accessible.
Manage shop-floor Kanban execution, monitor stockouts and trigger replenishment in line with agreed processes; work with the Senior Buyer to review replenishment levels and support assigned purchasing activities.
Identify material shortages and overdue items early, communicate required dates and production impact to the Senior Buyer, and agree follow-up actions; monitor commitments for directly assigned purchase orders and escalate delivery risks promptly.
Coordinate production-team participation in cycle counts, the annual inventory count and inventory reconciliation, supporting the Senior Buyer, Logistics and Accounting.
Support cycle counts, the annual inventory count and inventory reconciliation in coordination with Supply Chain, Logistics and Accounting.
Safety quality and workplace standards
Maintain a safe, clean and organised production environment through daily housekeeping, 5S routines, clear work areas and appropriate part presentation.
Reinforce safe working practices, report hazards and near misses, and follow through on assigned corrective actions with the relevant safety and functional owners.
Ensure production follows approved drawings, work instructions, inspection and test requirements, and applicable quality and compliance procedures.
Contain and escalate production non-conformances promptly; work with Manufacturing Engineering / Quality and Engineering on investigation and corrective action.
Partner with the Manufacturing Engineer to improve assembly methods, layouts, standard work and production readiness for new or changed products; ensure agreed changes are implemented, understood and sustained.
Performance management and continuous improvement
Maintain and communicate production KPIs, including on-time delivery, lead time, assembly efficiency and stockouts, using accurate and consistent data.
Analyse performance gaps, identify contributing causes and implement or coordinate actions to improve results, escalating constraints outside the role’s authority.
Identify and deliver practical improvements using ITW principles, including 80/20, Front-to-Back and In-lining, with support from Manufacturing Engineering and the Business Improvement Coordinator.
Document key operating routines and improvement outcomes, establish backup coverage and demonstrate sustained benefits to safety, quality, delivery, cost or capacity.
In addition to the responsibilities listed above, the position holder is expected to support related business, operational, and continuous improvement activities as reasonably directed by leadership.
Key Interfaces:
Operations & Engineering Director: operational priorities, performance, resource needs and escalation.
Engineering Team Leader and Engineering team: engineering release, technical queries, design changes and production readiness.
Manufacturing Engineer / Quality: assembly methods, standard work, training, quality controls, non-conformances and improvement implementation.
Senior Buyer / Supply Chain: material readiness, production requirements, Kanban replenishment, shortage resolution and coordination of assigned purchasing activities.
Logistics, Customer Experience, Regional Sales Managers and Accounting: order priorities, delivery feasibility, shipping, receiving and invoicing coordination.
Human Resources and Business Improvement Coordinator: people processes, training, work instructions, process flows and improvement support.
External: suppliers, vendors and global Loma production teams, as required.
Requirements:
Essential:
·         Demonstrated experience supervising or directly leading a manufacturing or assembly team, including work allocation, coaching and performance management.
·         Practical experience in production scheduling, capacity planning and coordinating material availability in a varied manufacturing environment.
·         Technical aptitude and ability to interpret engineering drawings, bills of materials and assembly documentation.
·         Experience using ERP / MRP systems and Microsoft Excel to maintain accurate operational records, schedules and performance information.
·         Ability to prioritise competing demands, identify delivery risks and communicate clear actions across functions.
·         A hands-on, organised and analytical approach, with evidence of implementing and sustaining improvements.
·         Working knowledge of manufacturing safety practices, quality controls and 5S principles.
Desirable:
Experience in capital equipment or mechanical / electrical equipment assembly, particularly for food, packaging or pharmaceutical applications.
Experience with Kanban, inventory control, shipping / receiving or production-related purchasing.
Familiarity with Microsoft Dynamics 365, ISO 9001 quality systems and ITW operating principles.
Relevant qualification in manufacturing, engineering or operations, or equivalent practical experience.
Benefits:
Along with opportunities for career growth and development, Loma Systems provides a comprehensive benefits package, in conjunction with ITW, which supports our employees’ educational endeavors, wellness and financial security. Here are some of the features our comprehensive package has to offer:
Medical, dental and vision benefits
Flexible Spending and Health Saver Accounts
401(k) retirement savings program
Paid vacation, sick days and holidays
Wellness and fitness program
Advancement opportunities
Educational assistance
Volunteer and matching charitable gifts programs

title: QA/QC Lab Inspector - 2nd shift with 10% shift premium
description:
Job Description:
ITW Shakeproof is a division of Illinois Tool Works (ITW) which supplies cold headed & metal stamped fasteners totaling approximately $200M in revenue annually. Manufacturing/Warehouse locations include Watertown, WI, Milwaukee, WI, Broadview, IL, Elgin, IL, Machesney Park, IL, and Iron Ridge, WI, with a Sales, and Innovation / Strategic Marketing team primarily in Troy, Michigan. We serve major OEMs and their tier suppliers direct and through distribution channels in the automotive and industrial markets.  ITW Shakeproof Fasteners drives profitability by leveraging its innovative solutions and application engineering, allowing us to enhance our customers’ competitive advantage. Known for innovation, diversification, and excellent financial performance.   We are never, whether we know it or not, more than a few steps from an innovative ITW solution.
This position is a divisional resource responsible for ensuring exemplary support of quality complaints at our automotive and industrial customers. The Quality Engineer is instrumental in ensuring product quality for customers and investigating and remediating potential issues. As a customer facing role, the individual should expect frequent travel to our customer locations (primarily in the Midwest).
ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:
The QA/QC Lab Inspector performs and assists in the physical and metallurgical tests on start-up and in-process production parts in a metal fastener facility. Perform tasks associated with the verification and validation of part quality.
Performs preparation techniques of Metallurgical mounts such as grinding, cutting, polishing, etching products.
Operate and interpret findings from Micro-Hardness testing equipment on prepared mounts.
Performs Start-up and in-process tests on production parts. Have the ability to stop production if parts do not pass.
Reads and understands print drawings and specifications for correct test requirements, procedures, and sampling plans.
Verify calibration on all equipment within the lab and from the factory floor prior to use.
Reports any safety violations, test equipment misuse and/or improper work to the Supervisor.
Verifies and ensures that all jobs and materials have accurate information on the Manufacturing Order Route Packet prior to release to the production floor.
Receive and document sample parts into the Quality Lab tracking system.
Review the lab test results to ensure all operations have been properly performed and recorded.
Conducts lab sampling as needed.
Issue and track production gages to the manufacturing floor.
Proper handling and use of low-level acids as part of the metal etching process.
Attend the Material Review Board meetings when required.
Sort parts in the lab if required.
Supports and maintains waste elimination initiatives at the facility.
Continually seeks opportunities to improve by taking advantage of available training.
Attend all Company and department meetings are required
Inspects fasteners for conformance to specifications by performing a variety of testing.
Compares product with parts list or sample model to ensure completion of assembly.
Completes final inspection reports for each lot of parts.
Examines material or product for surface defects such as cracks, or obvious plating defects.
Verifies specified dimensions of product or material.
Rejects defective parts and marks type of defect on part, container of parts, or inspection tag.
Verifies that all required operations are complete and correct; ensure that lot integrity is maintained.
Operates comparator as required to inspect parts for dimensional requirements.
Completes final inspection reports for each lot of parts.
Ensures compliance with all company safety rules and procedures.
Performs other duties as assigned.
MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS :
High School Diploma or equivalent education.
Prefer minimum of 1-2 years of Metallurgical or physical laboratory experience.
Understanding of test equipment and procedures to include various hand gaging equipment and desk top test equipment.
Basic Microsoft Office understanding and usage.
Ability and wiliness to learn new techniques and procedures.
Compensation Information:
$22.40 per hour plus 10% shift premium
A full range of medical, dental, vision, 401K plus up-to-six percent (6%) match, wellness program, short- and long-term disability, education assistance, and gift & volunteer matching program are also available.

title: Quality Engineer
description:
Job Description:
Job Description
Brooks Instrument ( www.brooksinstrument.com ), an industry leader in flow and pressure instrumentation for critical applications, is seeking candidates for a   Quality Engineer position that will be based at the company headquarters in Hatfield, Pennsylvania (suburban Philadelphia). The company has manufacturing locations in Pennsylvania, Hungary, Malaysia, and Korea, and also maintains sales and service offices throughout the world. Our high-tech products are used in laboratory and process applications in end markets such as: oil & gas, petrochemical, medical devices, waste water, life sciences, and analytical instruments.
Brooks is a division of ITW (Illinois Tool Works), a fortune 200 company. ITW is one of the world’s leading diversified manufacturers of specialized industrial equipment, consumables, and related service businesses. The company has operations in 56 countries and employs over 50,000 employees. These talented employees, many of whom have specialized engineering or scientific expertise, contribute to ITW’s global leadership in innovation. The company is proud of its broad portfolio of nearly 10,000 active patents, and is focused on fully leveraging its highly differentiated business model to deliver solid growth with consistent best-in-class margins and return on capital.
Basic Functions
Serve as the point of contact for quality control planning, development, application, and maintenance of quality standards for processing materials into finished product.  Receive only broad supervision from the department manager and must be capable of advanced decision-making in the manager’s absence.  Product/industry knowledge is broad and support is often given to other departments as needed.  Major challenges include support of the division quality function concurrent with:
Business growth
Best business practices
Introduction of new products and processes
Meeting division continuous improvement goals
Achieving customer satisfaction
Essential Duties and Responsibility
Performs basic quality engineering functions, quality audits and sets quality standards for both in-process and finished products and materials.
Reports on quality analyses, product or process non-conformance issues, and recommends necessary corrective actions and procedure changes.
Interface with the plant management staff to ensure that quality improvement activities are in sync with plant quality and operational objectives.
Interface with all hourly employees, supervisors, department managers and division personnel while leading and coordinating improvement activities.
Coordinate the resolution of product quality concerns (process/customer) and facilitate responsiveness to customers.
Participate in the review of customer documentation to identify and ensure fulfillment of copy exact requirements.
Coordinate and evaluate annual product validations.
Support and promote Continuous Improvement Process (CIP) activities.
Verify and approve all department operation instructions and provide the necessary support for a complete understanding of the operation instructions and their application.
Support customer in 8D responses and regular quality resolution update meetings.
Develop/monitor first pass yield reports, scrap reports, and process audit reports.
Initiate engineering deviation requests and product change notices.
Determine that manufacturing processes and equipment have sufficient capability to meet customer quality requirements by analyzing capability studies, control charts, and other statistical data.
Employ statistical process controls and techniques to reduce scrap/rework and to drive continuous improvement.
Participate in the review of design, manufacturing, and test documentation to ensure that applicable system and contract quality requirements are met.
Develop sampling plans, design forms for recording, evaluating, and reporting quality data, and write instructions on the use of such forms.
Initiate plans, procedures, and/or actions to prevent/eliminate product and systemic quality problems.
Prepare slides for regular Quality review meetings. Participate in regular quality improvement meetings.
Write problem investigation reports and complete customer corrective action requests (eg 8D).
Ensure quality cost concepts are understood and executed.
Develop and administer department quality information, including the auditing of quality plans to permit identification and correction of deficiencies.
Participate in customer visits, surveys, and audits.
Analyze customer complaints and field failures.  Coordinate corrective action, follow-up and reporting.
Assist in the resolution of supplier quality problems as needed.
Participate in the development and implementation of ISO 9001 level II documentation and internal quality system audits.
Disposition discrepant material in a manner that ensures product quality and adherence to system requirements.
Perform project-specific tasks as required (e.g., customer required first article inspection, qualification test failure analysis, etc.) to ensure compliance to individual project requirements.
Maintain and collect data for tracking various Operational performance and Quality trends.
Perform analysis of data, using SPC techniques, charts, pareto, histograms, etc.
Prepare and present analysis results/charts in Power-point/presentation format.
Write queries and prepare reports from Trackwise data.
Track and follow-up corrective and preventive action (CAPA), customer complaint (CC), failure analysis (FA) and similar cases in Trackwise.
Support resolution of Quality issues both internal/external working with production and engineering teams.
Audit processes to identify and correct deficiencies or non-conformances
Complete customer responses, CAPA forms for quality issue resolution
Coordinate and perform internal audits as needed.
Provide Quality Certificate support as needed.
Support CIP teams when requested.

description:

Why This Role
Miller is building a new software-as-a-service business from the ground up: cloud software for the welding and fabrication industry, backed by nearly a century of industry leadership and the resources of ITW. You’ll be one of the first engineers on a small, senior internal team, helping set how we build, ship, and run software, including how we adopt AI-assisted engineering as those practices take shape, and you’ll see your work used by real customers on real shop floors.
Location: Remote -Occasional travel to our Appleton, WI facility.
Job Description
The Senior Software Engineer owns delivery of features and projects end to end on Miller’s cloud SaaS platform, from refining requirements with Product, through design and code, to operating what they build in production. Working alongside our Software Architect, product leaders, and contract development partners, you’ll raise the bar for quality and speed, mentor others, and help establish the engineering practices a modern SaaS business runs on.
Key Responsibilities
Own delivery of projects end to end
Take high-level, often ambiguous problems, break them into well-defined work, and deliver independently.
Design and build cloud services, APIs, and web applications on Microsoft Azure using C#/.NET and modern front-end frameworks.
Partner with Product to refine requirements and propose simpler alternatives that deliver the same value faster.
Engage directly with customers, support, and design partners to understand how our software is used, and ship features with the telemetry needed to show usage and value.
Review code and designs from contract development partners, raising quality and velocity concerns with data.
Define monitoring, alerting, and runbooks for what you own; take part in on-call and incident response and contribute to blameless postmortems.
Build with infrastructure as code and CI/CD, and apply security and compliance controls (e.g., SOC 2, ISO 27001) in day-to-day work.
Use time-boxed spikes and prototypes to test ideas and make deliberate calls on when to throw a prototype away versus harden it.
Mentor other engineers through code review, pairing, and knowledge sharing.
Use AI-assisted development tools (e.g., GitHub Copilot, Claude) to speed up design, coding, testing, and documentation, while reviewing AI-generated output critically and following ITW AI usage policy.
Stay current as AI tools evolve, understand their trade-offs and risks, and share what works with the team.
Deliver software enhancements
Reviewing code from external development partners
Improve software development, testing, and deployment processes.

4+ years of professional software development experience.
Hands-on experience building and operating cloud-hosted web applications or services in production (Azure preferred).
Strong proficiency in C#/.NET or a comparable modern language, including REST APIs and relational databases.
Experience with CI/CD pipelines, automated testing, and monitoring production systems.
Demonstrated ability to own delivery end to end, work through ambiguity, and debug and improve code written by others, including AI-generated and partner code.
Experience using AI-assisted development tools in professional work, with a clear view of where they help and where they don’t.
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

Experience at a SaaS product company (multi-tenant architecture, subscription products).
Infrastructure as code (e.g., Bicep, Terraform) and containers (e.g., Docker, Kubernetes, Azure Container Apps).
Experience working with or reviewing the work of contract or outsourced development teams.
Exposure to SOC 2, ISO 27001, or secure software development practices.
IoT, connected equipment, or industrial and manufacturing data experience.
Modern front-end frameworks (e.g., React, Angular, Blazor).
Experience building AI or LLM-powered features into products.
Agile/Scrum experience and familiarity with delivery metrics such as DORA.
Curiosity about welding, fabrication, and the people who do the work.

Join a collaborative and growth-focused team where your expertise will directly impact the company’s financial health and operational success. We value innovation, accountability, and continuous improvement.

Job Description:
ITW Food Equipment Group LLC designs and manufactures commercial food equipment for food service and retail customers through its subsidiaries. The company’s products include ware washing equipment; cooking equipment, including ovens, ranges, and broilers; refrigeration equipment, including refrigerators, freezers, and prep tables; food processing equipment, including slicers, mixers, and scales; and kitchen exhaust, ventilation, and pollution control systems. ITW FEG has the largest service network in this industry to support our global customers, with highly specialized technicians and best-in-class supply chain procedures. The company was incorporated in 2001 and is based in Troy, Ohio. ITW Food Equipment Group LLC is an Illinois Tool Works Inc. subsidiary.
SUMMARY
Service/Repair Technician 1 is entry level in the service technician occupation requiring fundamental knowledge of mechanical and/or electrical aptitude with some troubleshooting experience. Responsible for providing on-site support to Hobart Service customers that includes but is not limited to: installation and/ or service of commercial food equipment. Routine work schedule including on-call, after-hours, holiday, and weekend on-site repair support.
ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
These are the most significant job duties performed. The size, scope and complexity of assigned duties and responsibilities are dependent on the level and experience of the incumbent. To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each assigned essential duty satisfactorily. Other responsibilities or special projects not specifically listed below may also be assigned.
Installs basic mechanical commercial food equipment and assists in more advanced installs as needed.
Maintain, diagnose, and repair basic mechanical commercial food equipment for customers on contract and/or on time and material (i.e., T&M) basis.
Completes and documents preventative maintenance on basic mechanical commercial food equipment.
Implements and supports standard operating procedures outlined in Hobart Service safety manuals and programs.
Supports branch and organization financial objectives by providing a quality customer experience.
Maintains current organization, industry, and equipment knowledge.
Responsible for assigned company assets including vehicle, tools, and inventory.
Follows the company's safe driving and other applicable policies.
Supervisory Responsibilities
This position has no direct or indirect supervisory responsibilities.
QUALIFICATIONS
The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required to perform this job successfully. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Required Education and Work Experience
High school diploma or GED and,
0-2 years of electrical/mechanical experience
Desired Education/Experience
Associates Degree or Vocational Certificate is preferred.
Mechanical or electrical experience is preferred.
Experience installing, maintaining, troubleshooting, and repairing commercial cooking and/or refrigeration equipment is preferred.
Certificates and Licenses
Position/Location dependent.
Job Specific Knowledge
To perform this job successfully, the individual needs to demonstrate knowledge of these areas as they relate to the primary functions of the job.
Mechanical Aptitude – demonstrates mechanical aptitude to operate and troubleshoot equipment. Skilled in use of various tools and equipment (e.g. basic hand tools, reading and following service manuals, gauges, meters, etc.)
Customer Service - highly professional demeanor with excellent telephone skills and etiquette. Utilizes various interpersonal styles and communication methods to positively assist and influence customers.
Problem Solving - fundamental role in finding ways to address all types of problems by having a good approach to a problem without being ineffective, favoring or causing painful consequences.
Safety at Work - learns to keep the organization safe from different risks by developing a high sense of alertness that detects danger from afar and stops it before it causes risk, danger or injury to themselves, or others.

description:
It started with a simple idea: what if surgery could be less invasive and recovery less painful? Nearly 30 years later, that question still fuels everything we do at Intuitive . As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care , our technologies—like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion —have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide.
We’re a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.
The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful—because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.
Primary Function of Position:
The Business Process Lead, FP&A Transformation is the enterprise process owner for how forecasting is designed, executed, and continuously improved at Intuitive. This high-impact individual contributor will lead the transformation of legacy, manual, and fragmented workflows into a simpler, faster, and more accurate forecasting operating model. Working with FP&A leadership across the organization, this role translates business needs into scalable processes, aligns stakeholders, pilots improvements, and drives sustained adoption.
The successful candidate is a systems thinker, process architect, and change leader who creates clarity in ambiguity, challenges unnecessary complexity, and connects process design to measurable outcomes. Success will be reflected in a forecasting model that is faster, simpler, more accurate, well governed, and consistently adopted across FP&A. Innovative thinking to challenge the current state to fully transform the forecast process.
Role and Responsibilities:
Diagnose and Design: Map end-to-end forecasting workflows, handoffs, decision points, rework loops, and elapsed-time gaps.
Identify root causes related to ownership, decision rights, data readiness, calendar design, and manual workarounds.
Design the future-state operating model, including workflow sequencing, inputs and outputs, decision gates, escalation paths, and integration points.
Prioritize, Pilot, and Scale: Build a transformation roadmap that sequences process, data, and automation opportunities by value, feasibility, risk, readiness, and dependencies.
Facilitate prioritization decisions with Finance leadership and clearly communicate trade-offs.
Design and lead pilots with defined scope, success measures, timelines, and learning objectives.
Measure outcomes, refine the approach, and scale proven changes while maintaining process integrity.
Track adoption and outcomes using measures such as cycle time, rework, compliance, engagement, and forecast accuracy trends.
Establish feedback loops and governance to sustain improvements.
Required Skills and Experience:
8+ years of progressive experience in business process excellence, finance transformation, FP&A operations, or a related discipline.
Experience partnering with Data, Systems, or Technology teams without directly owning technical delivery.
Success leading enterprise-scale process redesign from diagnosis through future-state design, pilot, rollout, and adoption.
Expertise with AI/ML-enabled forecasting and responsible integration of model outputs into financial processes.
Experience translating ambiguous problems into process blueprints, RACIs, decision gates, requirements, and prioritized roadmaps.
Lean Six Sigma, BPM, Design Thinking, or formal change management training or certification.
Proficiency with process-mapping tools such as Visio, Lucidchart, or Miro.
Hands-on experience facilitating process mapping and cross-functional working sessions.
Executive communication skills for VP- and C-suite audiences.
This role requires working onsite in our Sunnyvale, CA office Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday every week.
Required Education and Training:
Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Business, Operations, Data Analytics, Information Systems or a related field.
Preferred Skills and Experience:
FP&A transformation experience, including forecasting operating model redesign, planning-cycle optimization, or driver-based planning.
Ability to influence without authority across senior leaders, business owners, and technical teams.
Strong analytical capabilities and experience evaluating transformation outcomes.
Experience in a publicly traded technology or medical-device company and a SOX-compliant environment.

The Human Factors Manager works closely with fellow Human Factors managers and engineers and collaborates with other cross-functional managers of clinical engineering, system and software engineering, product managers, and program managers among other important functional teams in the development of novel technologies and devices.
The Human Factors Manager's primary role is to support, inform and guide development of Human Factors team members and represent the Human Factors function within and across business units, ensuring the successful execution of Human Factors Usability Engineering Initiatives, process activities and deliverables, while keeping a patient-first mindset, acting as an advocate for the clinical caregiver end-users regarding safety and usability, and as representative for medical device regulatory compliance.

Support the execution of, and report to leadership on, usability research and evaluations at various stages of product development.
The Human Factors Manger will balance testing efforts across multiple projects from early prototypes to formal External Standards-mandated validation testing in US and OUS market environments.
Advocate strongly and consistently for the clinical caregiver experience for safety and usability, with understanding of the nuance and balance of user/customer needs and business needs.
Interface and associate with end-user customers in multiple international markets to gather design insights in a highly professional manner, during complex workflow-oriented usability formative study and user research activities.
Write and revise highly accurate, clear, and concise usability engineering documents in a timely manner for multiple projects.
Synthesize complex information into internal communications and presentations for product teams and broader organization leadership audiences.
Prepare and review documentation for submission to regulatory agencies and notified bodies, including supporting the response to questions for additional justification and rationale

human factors (e.g. IEC 62366, AAMI HE75, FDA Applying Human Factors and Usability Engineering to Medical Devices) and advise management regarding potential improvements to internal processes and regulatory issues related to usability engineering.

The Team
The Incubator within Future Forward at Intuitive is a cross-functional innovation group focused on identifying, evaluating, and developing new clinical opportunities and technology platforms. The team operates at the earliest stages of innovation, working from unmet clinical needs through concept generation, derisking, and early development. By partnering closely with engineering, clinical, and business leaders, the Incubator helps shape Intuitive’s long-term growth by advancing transformational technologies that improve patient outcomes and expand access to care.
Primary Function of the Position
The Physician, Corporate Strategy is an MD physician innovator embedded within Intuitive’s Future Forward Incubator. This role translates clinical insight and early-market understanding into new growth opportunities, helping identify unmet clinical needs, evaluate strategic fit, and shape technology concepts from initial hypothesis through early de-risking. We are open to candidates who bring one of two complementary profiles: (1) strong clinical practice experience with exposure to innovation, venture, startups, business development, Biodesign, or product development; or (2) deep venture, startup, business development, Biodesign, or corporate strategy experience with an MD background and enough medical/clinical fluency to credibly assess patient care, procedure workflows, and clinician needs. The successful candidate will work closely with engineering, clinical, product, regulatory, reimbursement, and strategy partners to determine which opportunities should advance and how they should be clinically and commercially framed.
Essential Job Duties
Identify, frame, and prioritize unmet clinical needs using clinical immersion, literature review, market sensing, and voice-of-customer input.
Translate physician and patient insights into concise need statements, opportunity hypotheses, clinical workflows, requirements, and early de-risking plans.
Evaluate early-stage opportunities for clinical importance, feasibility, strategic fit, adoption barriers, competitive landscape, and potential business impact.
Partner with engineering and design teams to define clinical use cases, procedural workflows, performance goals, and prototype feedback loops for new platforms.
Lead or support early clinical de-risking activities, including preclinical studies, simulated use, workflow validation, and early feasibility planning where appropriate.
Develop point-of-view assessments on emerging technologies, startups, venture-backed innovation, adjacent markets, and external partnership opportunities.
Collaborate with regulatory, reimbursement, health economics, product, and commercial strategy partners to shape indication strategy and development pathways.
Engage KOLs, clinicians, entrepreneurs, academic innovators, and external partners to validate concepts and inform investment decisions.
Communicate findings to senior stakeholders through clear written recommendations, executive presentations, and data-driven opportunity narratives.
Experience and Qualifications

Position Summary
The Quality Assurance Manager, Audits & Inspections is responsible for the planning, execution, management, and continuous improvement of the company’s GxP audit and regulatory inspection readiness programs supporting late-stage pharmaceutical development.
The role provides hands-on leadership for internal, external, vendor, and study-related audits and establishes a sustainable inspection-readiness program as the organization progresses through Phase 3 clinical development toward regulatory submission, pre-approval inspection, and commercialization readiness.
Working under the direction of the Head of Quality Assurance, the Manager partners with Clinical Operations, CMC, Regulatory Affairs, Pharmacovigilance, Nonclinical, and other functional teams to identify compliance risks, assess inspection readiness, manage audit observations and corrective actions, and ensure the organization and its critical service providers remain prepared for regulatory inspection.
This is a hands-on individual-contributor role requiring demonstrated experience conducting GxP audits and supporting FDA and/or other health-authority inspections.
Key Responsibilities
Audit Program Management
Develop and maintain a risk-based annual and multi-year GxP audit program covering internal functions, clinical studies, CROs, CDMOs, laboratories, pharmacovigilance providers, and other critical GxP vendors.
Plan, schedule, conduct, document, and close GxP audits in accordance with approved procedures and applicable regulatory requirements.
Develop audit plans, agendas, checklists, reports, observations, and follow-up documentation.
Evaluate audit observations for regulatory significance, systemic risk, and potential impact on product quality, subject protection, data integrity, and regulatory submissions.
Track audit findings, commitments, CAPAs, and effectiveness activities through closure.
Perform audit trending and provide periodic reporting of significant findings and emerging compliance risks to QA leadership.
Regulatory Inspection Readiness
Develop and maintain the company’s inspection-readiness program for FDA and other applicable health authorities.
Support readiness for BIMO, GCP, GMP, GLP, GVP and, as applicable, Pre-Approval Inspections (PAI).
Conduct inspection-readiness assessments, mock inspections, document reviews, interview preparation, and functional readiness exercises.
Identify potential inspection vulnerabilities and coordinate remediation activities with responsible functional owners.
Maintain inspection-readiness tools, procedures, playbooks, request-management processes, and supporting documentation.
Support development and maintenance of inspection war-room, document-request, response-review, escalation, and communication processes.
Regulatory Inspection Management
Support the Head of Quality Assurance in coordinating and managing regulatory inspections.
Facilitate inspection logistics, document requests, SME preparation, inspection-room activities, and real-time issue escalation.
Review proposed responses and supporting evidence for accuracy, completeness, consistency, and regulatory defensibility.
Support evaluation and response to inspection observations, including FDA Form 483 observations and comparable health-authority findings.
Track post-inspection commitments and associated CAPAs through completion and effectiveness verification.
Vendor and Partner Quality Oversight
Conduct qualification, routine, for-cause, and risk-based audits of CROs, CDMOs, laboratories, and other GxP service providers.
Evaluate vendor audit findings in the context of sponsor oversight responsibilities and program risk.
Partner with functional owners to establish appropriate remediation and escalation plans.
Support vendor qualification and ongoing performance monitoring based on audit results, quality events, compliance history, and risk.
Compliance Risk & CAPA
Identify emerging or systemic compliance risks through audit findings, inspection trends, quality events, and other quality intelligence.
Support or lead root-cause investigations associated with significant audit and inspection findings.
Review CAPAs for adequacy, proportionality, sustainability, and regulatory defensibility.
Perform or coordinate CAPA effectiveness verification associated with audit and inspection observations.
Escalate significant compliance risks promptly to the Head of Quality Assurance.
Cross-Functional Quality Partnership
Serve as a hands-on QA resource to functional teams preparing for audits and regulatory inspections.
Provide training and coaching to employees and SMEs regarding inspector interactions, documentation practices, inspection conduct, and response expectations.
Collaborate with QMS and GxP QA program functions to translate audit and inspection findings into sustainable improvements to the Quality Management System.
Maintain appropriate independence and objectivity when conducting audits and evaluating compliance.
Promptly escalate requests requiring significant regulatory interpretation, acceptance of material compliance risk, or final compliance disposition to the Head of Quality Assurance before communicating a final QA position.
Required Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree in life sciences, pharmacy, chemistry, engineering, or another relevant discipline.
Minimum of 7 years of progressive pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or regulated life-sciences Quality Assurance experience.
Demonstrated hands-on experience planning, conducting, documenting, and closing GxP audits.
Experience conducting audits of CROs, CDMOs, laboratories, clinical sites, or other regulated service providers.
Demonstrated experience supporting FDA or other health-authority regulatory inspections.
Strong working knowledge of applicable FDA regulations, ICH guidance, and GxP requirements.
Experience with audit observations, investigations, CAPA development, remediation, and effectiveness verification.
Strong technical writing skills and ability to produce clear, evidence-based audit reports and compliance assessments.
Ability to independently evaluate complex compliance issues and appropriately escalate significant risks.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience supporting Phase 3 and late-stage pharmaceutical development.
Experience preparing for or supporting FDA BIMO and/or Pre-Approval Inspections (PAI).
Cross-functional auditing experience spanning GCP, GMP, GLP, and/or GVP.
Experience with clinical-stage organizations operating through outsourced CRO/CDMO models.
Experience developing or implementing formal inspection-readiness programs.
Lead Auditor certification, ASQ certification, RQAP, or comparable professional credential is desirable but not required.
Key Competencies
The successful candidate should demonstrate strong auditor judgment and independence, exceptional attention to detail, regulatory and compliance acumen, concise technical writing, effective interviewing skills, and the ability to distinguish between isolated procedural deficiencies and systemic compliance risk. The individual must be comfortable challenging conclusions when warranted while maintaining productive working relationships with operational teams.

Responsible for independently conducting clinical studies on schedule and within budget while ensuring high quality and compliance

Ability to lead project team consisting of CRAs and CTAs and support management with relevant study updates

performance, safety and user-facing features of the da Vinci™ Surgical System, Intuitive’s flagship product.

across our embedded platform software stack.

Own development and drive the technical direction of embedded software for video networking, UI display, and machine learning applications on Linux-based systems – including architectural decisions, code review and performance optimization.
Design and own comprehensive test strategies to validate board functionality, peripheral interfaces, and system performance metrics – including defining acceptance criteria and driving resolution of complex hardware-software integration issues.
Partner with and technically guide hardware engineers to identify, root-cause and resolve board-level issues during early development phases – serving as the primary software interface for cross-functional hardware bring-up
Architect and lead the development of automated test frameworks for board validation and regression testing – establishing scalable infrastructure usable across multiple platform variants.
Mentor junior and mid-level engineers through code reviews, technical guidance, and hands-on debugging support – actively contributing to the growth of the team.
Author and maintain technical documentation including design specifications, bring-up procedures, and failure analysis reports in compliance with FDA-regulated development processes.

Expert-level proficiency in C and C++ for embedded systems development, including memory management, real-time constraints, and performance-critical code
Deep expertise in embedded Linux, including kernel internals, custom device driver development, BSP bring-up, and user space application development

Effective written and verbal communication skills for technical documentation and cross- functional team collaboration

Hands-on experience with GPU acceleration (CUDA) and hardware-accelerated inference frameworks (TensorRT) in production embedded systems
Experience with QNX RTOS or other real-time operating systems in safety-critical applications.

title: Senior Human Factors Engineer
description:

As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care , our technologies—like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion —have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide.
We’re a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.
The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful—because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.
Primary Function
The Senior Human Factors Engineer works closely with designers, clinical engineers, and technical product managers to inform and guide the development of new products and ensure that those products are safe and easy to use. As part of new product development projects, they conduct user research, analyze and characterize use-related risks, and conduct usability testing of products prior to launch. They have primary responsibility for creating usability risk analyses and conducting final usability validation studies. The Senior Human Factors Engineer also works closely with the regulatory group to create the usability engineering documentation
required for submission to medical device regulatory agencies.
Roles & Responsibilities:
Collect and synthesize detailed information on how users interact with Intuitive products through various techniques including interviews, simulations, direct observations, task analyses, and persona development.
Present results of field observations, research, and usability testing.
Contribute to user interface designs by negotiating design recommendations to mitigate use errors and improve usability. Assist creation and revision of user-interface requirements documents.
Analyze complaints from on-market products and update usability risk assessment and escalate usability-related issues as necessary.
Design, execute, and report on usability (human factors) tests at various stages of product development from early prototypes all the way through formal FDA-mandated validation testing.
Write and execute usability test protocols. Analyze test data and write test reports.
Develop validation strategies for projects involving updates to existing products.
Lead the efforts required to create and update usability risk analyses for Intuitive products
Maintain traces between use risks, mitigations, and validation test cases.
Reinforce a human centered design approach across the organization.
Represent the Human Factors function on core teams for large projects.
Coordinate human factors efforts across projects involving several sub-systems.
Manage usability engineering activities within development projects and provide schedules and status to technical product managers and engineering project managers.
Mentor junior human factors engineers (e.g. interns) and others in organization in usability engineering methods and best practices, as well as Intuitive product development processes.
Prepare and review documentation for submission to regulatory agencies and notified bodies.
Answer questions and provide additional justification and rationale to any questions received.
Keep abreast of regulations and best practices for medical device human factors (e.g. IEC 62366, AAMI HE75, FDA Applying Human Factors and Usability Engineering to Medical Devices) and advise management regarding potential improvements to internal processes and regulatory issues related to usability engineering.
Qualifications
Skills, Experience, Education, & Training:
Minimum BS in Human Factors Engineering, Cognitive Psychology, Computer Science with human-computer interface (HCI) emphasis, Human Centered Design, or related field. MS strongly preferred.
Minimum 8+ years relevant Human Factors/Usability Engineering experience in hardware product development industry
Experience in medical device, or similar regulated industry, a significant plus
Ability to lead usability engineering activities (i.e. establishing usability requirements; creating usability risk analyses, test protocols, and test reports) for a complex, software-controlled electro-mechanical medical device
Ability to interface with customers in a highly professional manner
Ability to analyze and synthesize large quantities of information into usable communications
Superior ability to write accurate, clear, and concise protocols, reports, operating procedures, etc. in a timely manner
Excellent verbal communication and presentation skills
Ability to work with and across various groups and levels of management within the organization, including other engineering groups, marketing, clinical engineering, and regulatory. Excellent collaboration skills.
Ability to apply user-centered design and usability engineering principles to product research, development, and design
Ability to travel internationally as well as domestically (up to 25%)

Robotics Algorithms and Controls engineers (Systems Analysts) perform a central role in the design, development, and support of new products in the daVinci product line. They are responsible for developing the surgical teleoperation, motion control, and safety algorithms. This responsibility crosses into electrical, mechanical, software, control, user interface, and safety engineering. Systems Analysts strive to provide early design input, prove out new designs, and seek out solutions to challenging problems.
As a Systems Analyst, you will work with a small, multidisciplinary team of talented and dedicated engineers. This role demands in-depth collaboration with cross-functional teams, utilizing technical and interpersonal skills to develop a shared understanding of new product requirements. Systems Analysts maintain awareness and interest in developing research and technologies related to medical devices and safety-critical systems and actively apply this knowledge to system design.

Contribute to the development of new robotic systems through analysis and characterization.
Analyze complex electro-mechanical devices for dynamic safety and clinical risk.
Apply control theory to the design and verification of mechatronic and tele-robotic systems.
Integrate prototype hardware with existing systems.
Develop and implement motion control and safety algorithms, including documentation of risks, requirements, and test protocols.
Develop cartesian controls for manipulator robotics to design and implement precise and efficient robotic movements.
Participate in clinical observations and experiments to ensure that performance requirements are relevant and realistic.
Communicate system performance to the organization.
Support and track system performance as it evolves from design engineering to manufacturing.
Provide analytical assistance and tool building for other engineering issues.
Act as an interface between various technical specialties. Take ownership of issues that cross disciplinary boundaries and use a broad skillset to ensure the success of the project.
Document and communicate intellectual property.
Skill/Job Requirements:
Minimum MS degree in CS, ME, EE, or similar with 4–5+ years of industrial experience or PhD with 1–3+ years of experience.
Experience designing and implementing servo control systems.
Possess strong embedded development skills including intimate knowledge of C and modern C++.
Possess MATLAB and Python programming capabilities, as well as hardware and software integration skills.
Be detail-oriented and able to develop and drive a single solution to completion.
Comfort with concepts of design input, design output, traceability, and risk analysis.
Hands-on engineering experience with proven ability to work well in a team environment.

description:

As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care, our technologies like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide.
