The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
The Future Forward organization is Intuitive’s advanced concepts group. We explore emerging technologies, prototype next-generation solutions, and build software experiences that shape the future of robotic-assisted surgery.
If you're ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare, you'll find your purpose here.
The Future Forward group within Intuitive Surgical is searching for a Sr. Electrical and Electronic Design Engineer to architect, design, and bring up the electronic hardware behind next-generation robotic and vision systems. This role is an exciting opportunity to join a small and innovative team in the early phases of product development, where design decisions made at the schematic and architecture level shape the performance of the entire system.
Joining Intuitive Surgical means joining a team dedicated to using technology to benefit patients by improving surgical efficacy and decreasing surgical invasiveness, with patient outcomes as our highest priority. The Sr. Electrical and Electronic Design Engineer owns analog, digital, and mixed-signal circuit design from concept through schematic capture, layout direction, prototype bring-up, design verification, and transfer to manufacturing. The ideal candidate designs for electromagnetic compatibility and signal integrity from the first block diagram rather than after the first chamber failure, and can isolate the most difficult board-level and system-level failures on the bench. A strong sense of integrity, care, and attention to detail is required, together with a commitment to developing products of the highest quality.
Roles and Responsibilities:
Design analog, digital, and mixed-signal circuits from concept through schematic capture, layout direction, prototype bring-up, and transfer to manufacturing.
Lead schematic and design reviews, and guide PCB layout for signal integrity, power integrity, and manufacturability.
Design for EMC and EMI from the start through grounding, shielding, filtering, isolation, and ESD protection, and support pre-compliance and compliance testing.
Bring up and debug prototypes in the lab, and drive hardware issues to root cause and a verified fix.
Integrate sensors, cameras, illumination, motor drives, and compute platforms in partnership with Mechanical, Firmware, Software, Vision, and Test teams.
Document designs, verification protocols, and results under Intuitive design controls.
Mentor engineers and help shape design practices, reference designs, and the technology roadmap for future products.
Drive external suppliers and design partners for camera, sensor, optics, and PCBA subsystems, setting technical direction and holding builds to schedule and quality targets.
Skills/Job Requirements:
Minimum 8 years' experience designing production electronics in the medical device, automotive, or robotics industry, including at least one product taken from concept to production.
Bachelor of Science degree in Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Computer Engineering, or Computer Science; a Master of Science degree preferred.
Strong schematic design, review, and debug skills across analog, digital, and mixed-signal circuits, using Altium Designer, Cadence OrCAD/Allegro, or Siemens Xpedition.
Practical EMC and EMI design and troubleshooting experience, with working knowledge of standards such as IEC 60601-1-2, CISPR 11/32, or the IEC 61000-4 immunity series.
Solid signal integrity and power integrity fundamentals for high-speed interfaces such as MIPI CSI-2, LVDS, PCIe, USB, DDR, or Ethernet, including impedance control, return paths, crosstalk, and decoupling.
Direct experience with imaging and vision hardware, motor drive electronics, or precision sensing, and with transferring designs into manufacturing and production test.
Confident in the lab with oscilloscopes, spectrum analyzers, near-field probes, and logic or protocol analyzers, working with embedded interfaces such as I2C, SPI, UART, CAN, USB, and Ethernet, and using Python or MATLAB for test automation and data analysis.
Experience under a regulated quality system such as ISO 13485, FDA 21 CFR Part 820, IEC 60601-1, and ISO 14971, or automotive functional safety such as ISO 26262, is desired; FPGA design experience with VHDL or SystemVerilog is a plus.
Clear communication, strong documentation habits, and the ability to lead technical decisions, work independently, and mentor others.

title: Sr. Simulation & Synthetic Data Engineer - Remote
description:
It started with a simple idea: what if surgery could be less invasive and recovery less painful? Nearly 30 years later, that question still fuels everything we do at Intuitive . As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care , our technologies—like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion —have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide.
We’re a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.
The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful—because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.
About the Team
Future Forward Research — Synthetic Data, builds the simulation and data infrastructure that powers Intuitive's autonomous surgical capabilities.
The Role
You'll build the virtual surgical worlds and the data pipelines that train our perception and policy models. Day to day, that means designing simulation environments, generating large volumes of labeled synthetic data, and working with ML engineers to close the sim-to-real gap for robotic surgery. It's a hands-on engineering role at the intersection of 3D simulation, machine learning, and robotics.
What You'll Do
Design and build high-fidelity simulation environments for surgical tasks.
Generate scalable synthetic datasets including photo realistic imagery, segmentation masks, depth, optical flow, and kinematic state — and own their quality, versioning, and delivery.
Implement domain randomization and procedural scene generation to maximize sim-to-real transfer.
Model deformable soft-tissue physics, tool-tissue contact, and instrument kinematics that match Intuitive's platforms.
Partner with ML engineers to define task curricula, reward functions, and evaluation benchmarks.
Develop and refine sim-to-real transfer strategies, and validate simulated behaviors against benchtop phantoms and real systems.
Build reusable tools, APIs, and documentation so the broader team can spin up new tasks without deep simulation expertise.
What You Bring
We care more about real depth in a few of these than shallow coverage of all of them.
Strong software engineering. You write maintainable, tested code in Python, C++ and/or C#, and you're comfortable in a Linux / Git / Docker / GPU workflow.
Hands-on simulation or graphics experience. You've built things in a physics simulator, game engine, or rendering/VFX pipeline — robotics simulators, real-time engines, and offline graphics pipelines all count.
A feel for data and models. You've produced data that trained an ML model (or worked closely alongside that), and you understand how data quality and distribution show up in model behavior.
Working knowledge of 3D and physics fundamentals — coordinate frames, rendering, rigid-body and contact dynamics — enough to reason about why a simulated scene does or doesn't look and behave correctly.
You've likely spent several years building games, simulation, graphics, robotics, or data systems — but we're far more interested in what you've built than in a specific number on your résumé. If you don't check every box, we still want to hear from you. Strong candidates often come from autonomous driving, humanoid robotics, gaming, or VFX rather than surgical robotics specifically.
Education
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Graphics, Robotics, Electrical or Mechanical Engineering, Physics, or a related technical field — or equivalent practical experience.
An advanced degree (MS or PhD) in a related area is a plus, not a requirement. We've hired strong engineers from all paths, including self-taught backgrounds and industry work in games, VFX, or robotics.
Bonus Points
None of these are required — they're signals, not gates. Any one of them is a nice plus.
Deformable-object simulation: FEM, position-based dynamics, or differentiable physics
NVIDIA Isaac Sim/Lab
Surgical robotics simulation: ORBIT-Surgical, dVRK-based environments
Sim-to-real techniques: domain randomization, system identification, privileged learning, residual policies
Vision-language or vision-language-action models, and how simulation data supports them
Procedural/generative asset creation: NeRFs, Gaussian Splatting, or diffusion models
Distributed compute at scale: Ray, Kubernetes, Slurm, multi-GPU/multi-node
Medical imaging or surgical video pipelines
Publications or open-source work in simulation, graphics, robotics, or AI
Tools You Might Use
You won't touch all of these, and we don't expect you to walk in knowing them.
Category
Examples
Simulation engines
Unity, NVIDIA Isaac Sim/Lab, MuJoCo
Deformable physics
PhysX FEM, SOFA, DiSECt, NVIDIA Warp/Newton, PBD
Rendering & data
USD, Omniverse Replicator, Blender
Infrastructure
Docker, Kubernetes, Ray, Airflow, CUDA
What Success Looks Like in Your First Year
Simulation environments for several core surgical tasks are operational and integrated with the ML training pipeline.
Synthetic data delivers measurable model lift on targeted perception or policy metrics.
A quantitative sim-to-real correlation is established on benchtop phantoms.
Parallelized infrastructure reliably generates thousands of training episodes per hour with automated dataset delivery.
A reusable task-creation framework lets ML engineers define new surgical skills without deep simulation expertise.

Day

description:

Primary Function of Position
The Staff Supplier Quality Engineer operates with a high degree of independence to determine methodologies, audit frameworks, quality systems, and procedural controls across the global supply chain ecosystem, reporting to the Director, Global Supply Chain Audits.
This role is responsible for the technical execution, continuous improvement, strategic projects, and global harmonization of Third-Party Logistics (3PL) quality management, distribution center controls, and service supplier qualification processes worldwide. The Staff SQE leads risk-based lead audit programs, ensures conformance to applicable global regulatory standards (21 CFR Part 820, ISO 13485, EU MDR 2017/745, Good Distribution Practice / GDP), and serves as a subject matter expert (SME) in regulatory body inspections. S/he partners with cross-functional global operations, logistics, and regional RAQA organizations to drive critical process improvement projects, resolve systemic quality issues, ensure CAPA effectiveness, and advance 3PL supply chain compliance maturity.
Essential Job Duties
·         3PL Quality Management & Worldwide Oversight
·         Design, own, and continuously improve a global 3PL Quality Management Program encompassing third-party logistics providers, global distribution hubs, forward stocking locations, cold chain/temperature-controlled storage facilities, and fulfillment partners across all global regions.
·         Establish and maintain qualification frameworks, quality agreements (QAs), and re-evaluation controls specific to 3PL providers and logistics vendors supporting GxP-regulated distribution processes in alignment with 21 CFR Part 820, ISO 13485 (Clause 7.5.5), EU MDR, and GDP requirements.
·         Drive global harmonization of 3PL quality controls, distribution oversight, and logistics quality standards across regional entities: ISJ, ISK, IS India, IS Aubonne, ISE, ISB, and IST.
·         Maintain quality oversight of 3PL operational execution, including ambient/cold-chain storage validation, environmental monitoring, product handling, serialized inventory controls, localized labeling/repackaging, and transportation controls.
·         Lead Audits & Supplier / Service Qualification
·         Lead and execute comprehensive risk-based audits as Lead Auditor for worldwide 3PL providers, distribution hubs, and service suppliers (sterilization, calibration, test laboratories, software/IT GxP service vendors).
·         Design, own, and update 3PL audit master schedules, audit risk models, protocols, checklists, and reporting templates tailored to third-party logistics and service supplier activities.
·         Conduct Lead Audits against applicable global regulatory standards including Good Distribution Practice (GDP), ISO 13485, ISO 17025, ISO 11135/11137, and 21 CFR Part 820 subpart requirements.
·         Evaluate audit findings, issue formal audit reports, drive root cause analysis rigor with 3PL leadership, and manage SCAR / CAPA phase gate reviews and effectiveness verifications.
·         Projects & Process Improvements
·         Lead strategic quality engineering projects and continuous process improvement initiatives to optimize supply chain workflows, streamline 3PL quality oversight, and elevate supplier scorecards.
·         Partner with IT and Supply Chain teams to drive continuous improvement of QMS software platforms (Trackwise, SAP, Agile) supporting 3PL quality workflows, audit scheduling, and SCAR tracking.
·         Establish and analyze quality metrics, trends, and KPIs regarding 3PL performance, supplier corrective actions, and audit program effectiveness.
·         Own Process Nonconformances (NCs) and CAPAs related to 3PL, logistics, and supply chain audit processes, ensuring root cause rigor (6M / 5-Why) and sustainable corrective actions.
·         Supplier Controls & QMS Administration
·         Manage 3PL Supplier Corrective Action Requests (SCARs) end-to-end: issuance, aging tracking, phase gate reviews, effectiveness verification, and closure.
·         Support Approved Supplier List (ASL) governance regarding 3PL status maintenance, including promotions, conditional approvals, and demotions.
·         Administer and maintain 3PL and service supplier records in Trackwise, SAP, and Agile, including audit files, ISO/GDP certifications, quality agreements, and ARFs.
·         Regulatory Audit Support & Leadership
·         Serve as SME during FDA inspections, Notified Body audits (e.g., BSI, TÜV), and internal QMS audits for all matters related to 3PL Controls, GDP compliance, Service Supplier qualification, and Supply Chain Audits.
·         Operate independently to determine methods and procedures on new, complex, or special assignments with minimal supervision.
·         Mentor, coach, and guide junior compliance and supplier quality engineering staff.
·         May supervise or mentor the activities of junior compliance and supplier quality staff.
Required Skills and Experience
ISO 13485 Lead Auditor with demonstrated experience leading multi-site external audits worldwide.
Expert-level knowledge of 21 CFR Part 820, ISO 13485:2016, EU MDR 2017/745, and Good Distribution Practice (GDP / GMP) requirements applicable to 3PL, logistics, and service supplier controls.
Proven experience leading quality oversight and audits of global 3PLs, cold chain storage, distribution networks, and service suppliers.
Expert proficiency with QMS platforms including Trackwise, SAP, and Agile for supplier file management, SCAR tracking, and audit scheduling.
Strong understanding of risk management principles (ISO 14971) as applied to 3PL risk stratification, logistics risk assessments, and audit frequency determination.
Required Education and Training
Education: BS/BA degree in Engineering, Life Sciences, Supply Chain Management, or a related technical discipline preferred.
Experience Level: Typically requires a minimum of 12 years of related experience with a Bachelor's degree; or 8 years with a Master's degree; or a PhD with 5 years of experience; or equivalent demonstrated experience.
Industry Experience: Significant experience in a high-volume, globally distributed medical device or GxP-regulated company is required.
Working Conditions
Travel 50% Internationally
Preferred Skills and Experience
·         Direct experience auditing and managing worldwide 3PL providers, temperature-controlled distribution, and global supply chain logistics in a regulated medical device environment.
·         Exposure to auditing service suppliers and distributors in a regulated medical device environment.

This role partners closely with the sales team, specifically the Clinical Sales Representative and Clinical Sales Manager, to ensure safe and effective product adoption and quality control while driving positive patient outcomes.
The DaVinci Specialist is a dedicated program execution & clinical education partner for hospitals running a da Vinci robotic surgery program.   Based on its expertise, this role focuses on identifies and tailors the nature and extent of staff in-servicing, day-to-day program execution, technology onboarding and operational support, communicating identified needs to hospital OR operations and leadership. Essential Job Duties
Collaboration & Field Partnership (Within a CSM Team)
Partner with the local CSR/CSM and cross-functional business partners to create, own, scale and execute best practices and deployment of ecosystem resources.
Lead account support plans that drive safe program execution and increase customer autonomy over time, including setting objectives, timelines and resources for relevant customers, in consultation with CSR/CSM.
Identify, solicit and provide field feedback and customer insights to internal teams to improve training, support resources, and customer experience.
Support adoption of digital solutions by helping customers build comfort and capability through in-servicing and troubleshooting.
Clinical & Technical Support
Identify and provide on-site, non-scrubbed operating room support for procedures utilizing the da Vinci Surgical System and associated technologies.
Support OR teams with room readiness and procedural workflow, including system setup support, docking workflow support, and intraoperative troubleshooting.
Serve as a clinical product expert to help ensure optimal, safe system use and adherence to applicable IFUs, hospital policies, and safety protocols.
Motivate and support adoption of advanced instruments and accessories by ensuring teams understand proper setup, handling, and intended use.

Assist with operational support activities such as facilitating appropriate internal handoffs for service needs.

Support onboarding and education for new users through structured training touchpoints (e.g., new staff orientation, refresher training, workflow standardization).
Lead new site start-ups by identifying and delivering onboarding programs and coordinating training logistics with the CSR/CSM and hospital stakeholders.

Act as a resource for ongoing education, product updates, and workflow optimization.

Analyze and leverage utilization, turnover, and other relevant case data to recommend operational changes to customers
Provide first-line support and expertise for common setup and workflow issues during live cases and training sessions.
Identify, resolve and where necessary escalate issues appropriately to internal partners (e.g., Technical Support, Field Service, Clinical/Medical counterparts).
Market & Clinical Insights
Collect and communicate customer feedback and experiences to clinical counterparts and internal business partners.  Prioritizing, distilling and reporting relevant customer feedback, in real time.
Stay up to date on clinical literature, competitive products, and evolving treatment guidelines.
Assist in clinical trial support when required.
Assist in field action activities when necessary.

Experience: 2+ years in an operating room-related role

Exhibit a working knowledge of typical hospital policies.
Excellent communication, teaching, and interpersonal skills.
Strong problem solving and troubleshooting skills.
Ability to work in high-pressure environments (managing multiple ORs) and coordination of multiple tasks at one time.
Adaptability to evolving technologies and complex procedures.
Team oriented with a commercial mindset.
Willingness to travel up to 40%. Primary travel will be within a CSM team.
Ability to travel within a Clinical Sales Manager team geography, supporting multiple hospitals.
Flexibility to support early starts, after-hours cases, and weekend procedures based on customer need and territory utilization.
Required Education and Training
Associates degree. Bachelor’s degree preferred.
Degrees in (RN, PA, NP, RT, or other clinical credentials) are welcomed.
Working Conditions
Ability to stand for extended periods and provide in-person case support within an operating room (OR) environment, which includes pushing, pulling, lifting and squatting.

title: da Vinci Specialist
description:
It started with a simple idea: what if surgery could be less invasive and recovery less painful? Nearly 30 years later, that question still fuels everything we do at Intuitive. As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care, our technologies—like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion—have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide.
We’re a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.
The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful—because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare, you’ll find your purpose here.
*Please note: Candidates must live within or be willing to relocate to the Memphis Area to perform the duties of this role.
Primary Function of Position
The DaVinci Specialist (DVS) will provide expert clinical & technical support, build, customize and coordinate education & training to physicians, nurses, and hospital staff on the use of DaVinci surgery, devices and therapies. This role partners closely with the sales team, specifically the Clinical Sales Representative and Clinical Sales Manager, to ensure safe and effective product adoption and quality control while driving positive patient outcomes.
The DaVinci Specialist is a dedicated program execution & clinical education partner for hospitals running a da Vinci robotic surgery program.   Based on its expertise, this role focuses on identifies and tailors the nature and extent of staff in-servicing, day-to-day program execution, technology onboarding and operational support, communicating identified needs to hospital OR operations and leadership. The DVS will work alongside the daVinci Clinical Sales Representative .
Essential Job Duties
Collaboration & Field Partnership (Within a CSM Team)
Partner with the local CSR/CSM and cross-functional business partners to create, own, scale and execute best practices and deployment of ecosystem resources.
Lead account support plans that drive safe program execution and increase customer autonomy over time, including setting objectives, timelines and resources for relevant customers, in consultation with CSR/CSM.
Identify, solicit and provide field feedback and customer insights to internal teams to improve training, support resources, and customer experience.
Support adoption of digital solutions by helping customers build comfort and capability through in-servicing and troubleshooting.
Clinical & Technical Support
Identify and provide on-site, non-scrubbed operating room support for procedures utilizing the da Vinci Surgical System and associated technologies.
Support OR teams with room readiness and procedural workflow, including system setup support, docking workflow support, and intraoperative troubleshooting.
Serve as a clinical product expert to help ensure optimal, safe system use and adherence to applicable IFUs, hospital policies, and safety protocols.
Motivate and support adoption of advanced instruments and accessories by ensuring teams understand proper setup, handling, and intended use.
Partner with and promote consistent readiness and workflow by supporting day-to-day execution of the robotic program, coordinating with OR leadership, nursing, SPD/sterile processing, and biomedical teams.
Assist with operational support activities such as facilitating appropriate internal handoffs for service needs.
Ensure the right stakeholders are aligned (OR, SPD, biomed, IT) for successful day-to-day operation and new technology onboarding to help reduce friction.
Maintain accurate internal documentation of support activities per company process (e.g., case support notes, training records, service/escalation tracking).
Training & Education (Care Team Enablement)
Determine the need for, customize and deliver customer-specific hands-on training and in-services to nurses, surgical technologists, SPD teams, and other care team members on safe and effective use of da Vinci platforms and associated technologies.
Support onboarding and education for new users through structured training touchpoints (e.g., new staff orientation, refresher training, workflow standardization).
Lead new site start-ups by identifying and delivering onboarding programs and coordinating training logistics with the CSR/CSM and hospital stakeholders.
Support new technology installs by coordinating readiness activities and providing post-install education to care teams.
Act as a resource for ongoing education, product updates, and workflow optimization.
Escalation & Customer Issue Management
Analyze and leverage utilization, turnover, and other relevant case data to recommend operational changes to customers
Provide first-line support and expertise for common setup and workflow issues during live cases and training sessions.
Identify, resolve and where necessary escalate issues appropriately to internal partners (e.g., Technical Support, Field Service, Clinical/Medical counterparts).
Market & Clinical Insights
Collect and communicate customer feedback and experiences to clinical counterparts and internal business partners.  Prioritizing, distilling and reporting relevant customer feedback, in real time.
Stay up to date on clinical literature, competitive products, and evolving treatment guidelines.
Assist in clinical trial support when required.
Assist in field action activities when necessary.
Required Skills and Experience
Experience: 2+ years in an operating room-related role
Clinical experience is preferred.
Experience as a robotics coordinator, surgical assistant, and/or surgical nurse plus industry experience strongly preferred.
Understanding of soft tissue anatomy & procedures.
Exhibit a working knowledge of typical hospital policies.
Excellent communication, teaching, and interpersonal skills.
Strong problem solving and troubleshooting skills.
Ability to work in high-pressure environments (managing multiple ORs) and coordination of multiple tasks at one time.
Adaptability to evolving technologies and complex procedures.
Team oriented with a commercial mindset.
Willingness to travel up to 40%. Primary travel will be within a CSM team.
Ability to travel within a Clinical Sales Manager team geography, supporting multiple hospitals.
Flexibility to support early starts, after-hours cases, and weekend procedures based on customer need and territory utilization.
Required Education and Training
Associates degree. Bachelor’s degree preferred.
Degrees in (RN, PA, NP, RT, or other clinical credentials) are welcomed.
Working Conditions
Ability to stand for extended periods and provide in-person case support within an operating room (OR) environment, which includes pushing, pulling, lifting and squatting.

description:
Role purpose. The Manager, Canada Cheese & Dairy will lead the procurement strategy and commercial management for the full Canadian Business Unit portfolio of Cheese, Dairy Powders, Cheese Powders and Cream Mix. The role is accountable for category value delivery, supplier strategy, supply continuity, cost competitiveness, cross-border compliance and cross-functional execution across maintenance, productivity and innovation workstreams. The Manager will connect the Canadian Business Unit with North American category experts, translate market and business requirements into a Canada-specific sourcing strategy, and ensure clear information flow between Procurement and Canadian Business Unit leadership. Job Description
Primary Responsibilities:
Strategic Sourcing & Commercial Management • Own and execute end-to-end sourcing strategies for the Canadian Cheese and Dairy portfolio, including market analysis, supplier segmentation, sourcing events, negotiations, contracting, implementation and ongoing commercial governance. • Develop and maintain a multi-year Canada sourcing strategy aligned with North American category strategies while reflecting Canadian market dynamics, business priorities, regulatory requirements and supply-chain constraints. • Partner closely with North American category experts to leverage market intelligence, supplier relationships, sourcing scale and best practices, while maintaining clear accountability for Canadian Business Unit outcomes. • Lead complex and high-value negotiations, supplier award recommendations and contracting, ensuring appropriate cost, service, quality, capacity, flexibility and risk protections. • Develop and communicate a strong point of view on Canadian and North American cheese and dairy markets, including commodity drivers, manufacturing economics, capacity, trade flows, tariffs and regional supply-demand dynamics. • Ensure pricing, contracts, specifications, supplier records and sourcing decisions are accurate, current and compliant within relevant source-to-pay and business systems.
Canada Cheese & Dairy Portfolio Responsibilities • Lead procurement for Cheese, Dairy Powders, Cheese Powders and Cream Mix across the Canadian Business Unit, balancing cost, functionality, specification, service and supply requirements. • Provide portfolio-level governance across maintenance, productivity, innovation, reformulation, promotions, plant transitions, capacity changes and new business opportunities. • Partner with R&D, Quality, Manufacturing, Commercial, Finance, Materials Management and the Canadian Business Unit to define requirements, technical specifications, project economics and implementation timing. • Lead supplier and procurement readiness for innovations, renovations, reformulations, promotions, plant transitions, product maintenance and business continuity initiatives. • Assess and manage category complexity, including product specifications, lead times, minimum order quantities, yields, conversion economics, supplier capacity and cross-border supply lanes. • Build and maintain contingency strategies for critical materials, suppliers, manufacturing locations and logistics routes serving Canada.
Cross-Border, Quota, Tariff & CDC Managemen t • Own procurement coordination for cross-border cheese and dairy flows into and out of Canada, ensuring commercial plans reflect applicable quotas, tariffs, customs requirements and regulatory obligations. • Lead procurement management of Canadian Dairy Commission (CDC) requirements and related processes, working with internal and external experts to support compliant and cost-effective execution. • Monitor quota availability, tariff exposure and cross-border cost implications, incorporating these factors into sourcing decisions, budgets, supplier negotiations and risk assessments. • Coordinate with Trade Compliance, Legal, Finance, Logistics, customs brokers, suppliers and category experts to resolve cross-border issues and maintain continuity of supply. • Maintain clear governance, documentation and escalation paths for quota, tariff and CDC activities affecting the Canadian portfolio.
Forecasting, Inventory & Materials Management • Provide leadership and governance for coordination with Materials Management on forecasts, inventory policies, material requirements, lead times, capacity and availability across the Canadian portfolio. • Lead cross-functional resolution of supply disruptions, delivery issues, allocation constraints and inventory imbalances, with clear escalation, ownership and recovery plans. • Drive improvements in forecasting discipline, inventory visibility, supplier communication and working-capital performance in partnership with Mount Royal Planners, Materials Management and Finance.
Supplier Relationship & Performance Management • Own strategic relationships with key Cheese and Dairy suppliers serving the Canadian market. • Support the management of key Canadian Semi-Finished Goods suppliers, including Agropur and other strategic partners, in close alignment with the relevant North American category owners. • Define supplier strategies and performance expectations across cost, quality, service, delivery, capacity, innovation, sustainability and risk. • Lead strategic business reviews, negotiations, performance interventions, improvement plans and resolution of escalated commercial or supply issues. • Establish fit-for-purpose supply agreements, pricing mechanisms, service commitments, capacity protections and risk mitigations. • Develop a resilient, competitive and capable Canadian supply base, including qualification of alternatives and management of supplier concentration or dependency risks. • Build collaborative supplier relationships that enable innovation, continuous improvement, transparency and long-term value creation.
Canadian Business Unit Leadership & Stakeholder Management • Act as the principal Procurement partner for Cheese & Dairy within the Canadian Business Unit, aligning category strategies and sourcing actions with Business Unit priorities. • Participate in Canadian Business Unit Leadership Team sessions as the Cheese & Dairy Procurement representative. • Cascade relevant market, supplier, cost, supply, policy and project information into the Canadian Business Unit Leadership Team, and communicate decisions, priorities, risks and required actions back to Procurement and North American category teams. • Influence senior cross-functional stakeholders and resolve competing priorities across Procurement, Materials Management, Manufacturing, R&D, Quality, Finance, Commercial and the Canadian Business Unit. • Prepare and deliver monthly business updates to the Associate Director, Cheese & Dairy, covering market developments, category performance, productivity, supplier performance, inventory and supply risks, strategic decisions and next steps. • Represent the category in annual planning, productivity, innovation, risk and business review forums.
Project Management & Continuous Improvement • Lead cross-functional programmes related to productivity, innovation, portfolio maintenance, supplier transitions, specification changes, risk mitigation, supply continuity and process improvement for Canada. • Establish governance, milestones, resources, decision forums and escalation paths for priority category initiatives. • Drive improvements in procurement processes, category analytics, supplier performance management, contracting, forecasting, inventory coordination and cross-border execution. • Ensure compliance with procurement policies, sourcing governance, approval requirements, contracting standards, supplier due diligence and internal controls.

description:
Job Description The iconic Oscar Mayer Wienermobile first hit the hot dog highways in 1936. Our 27-foot-long hot dog on wheels has made it a mission to bring joy and smiles to people around the country even on their “wurst” of days. It is a Customer, Consumer, and Social Media superstar that drives traffic to stores/events and is a top content contributor in all forms of media. The Hotdoggers and Wienermobile offer Oscar Mayer an unparalleled competitive advantage, delivering incremental sales, merchandising, authorizations, and mutual goodwill.
The Hotdogger Program started in 1988 and was designed to hire and develop top-talent, grow future leaders of the company, and create gamechangers, innovators, and cultural champions.
The Hotdogger program is for individuals who are ready to deliver creative solutions on the Kraft Heinz journey to become the indispensable food company in North America.
The Hotdogger Tour The Oscar Mayer Hotdogger Program is a 1-Year assignment (starting and ending the first week of June).
The twelve-month program includes: · Two weeks of immersive onboarding and relevant job training · Regular meetings and coaching from top Advertising, Public Relations and Social Digital teams · Region and partner assignments that provide professional growth and a chance to see the country – Hotdoggers will switch regions and partners halfway through their tour · A chance to be an active and contributing member of a team of twelve top brand ambassadors. · Being the face of a multi-billion-dollar brand, while acting as our trusted “boots on the ground” · On-going coaching and mentorship through additional staff meetings and in-field meetings. · Post tour opportunities/connections with Kraft Heinz and hundreds of successful alumni.
Attributes/Skills/Background of a successful Hotdogger   · Experience working with the public/consumers · Prior travel experience is beneficial · As a highly autonomous position, organizational and time management skills are critical · Understanding of popular social media channels/outlets · Ability to work independently and within a team · Positive and outgoing – “a people-person” · Trustworthiness · Flexibility
The Life of a Hotdogger While no two days are the same in the Hotdogger program, a tour includes: · Representing the Oscar Mayer brand every day you crisscross the hot dog highways of America. · Executing and reporting over 200 events during your one-year tour. · Pitching and appearing on local television, radio, or newspaper media. · Creating social content for multiple Oscar Mayer social platforms including TikTok & Instagram. · Maintaining and driving our 90-year-old icon and piece of American pop culture. · Coordinating all aspects of Wienermobile travel logistics and management of travel expenses.
We Are Looking For... · Outgoing, creative, friendly, exuberant, college graduates who have an appetite for adventure and willing to see the country through the windshield of the iconic Oscar Mayer Wienermobile. · A spokesperson for Oscar Mayer who positively represents the brand in radio and television appearances, newspaper interviews, grocery/retail events, charity functions, and a variety of other activities. · Someone who “Meats” and greets people from coast to coast and leaves them with a positive brand experience and a desire to buy Oscar Mayer meats.  · An individual that embraces working with many different workstyles, internal and external consumer promotion teams, marketing teams, and sales professionals · Individuals craving the autonomy and flexibility of running their own traveling public relations firm on wheels; organizing events/activations and embracing the challenges of a very “fluid” job experience.
Our Values Our Hotdoggers are expected to live out the Kraft Heinz values as cultural champions and leaders in the organization. At Kraft Heinz, our values are: • We are consumer obsessed • We dare to do better every day • We champion great people • We demand diversity • We do the right thing • We own it
The Must-Haves · Bachelor’s Degree required, preferably in public relations, journalism, communications, advertising, or marketing, though applicants are not limited to these degrees. · Excellent communication and relational skills. · Outgoing, friendly, and passionate personality. · Bilingual candidates are encouraged to apply. · A valid Driver’s License is required and a favorable driving record (a driving record will be requested as part of the recruitment process). · Legally authorized to work in the United States and applicant WILL NOT require employment visa sponsorship. · Must be able to work major holidays. · Desire and ability to spend the year on the road as an ambassador for Oscar Mayer. · Must be comfortable with daily road travel in the Wienermobile and staying in hotels or short-term corporate approved housing throughout the United States. · Successful completion of Federal Department of Transportation Physical, Drug/Alcohol Test, Motor Vehicle Records check and standard Kraft Heinz background check. ﻿ What We Offer A One-Of-A-Kind role in a full-time, 1-year assignment with a competitive package including a $39,400 base salary, a weekly allowance of $300 ($15,600/yr.) for meals & personal travel, 18 days of paid time off, full health benefits package, and 100% of hotel expenses covered. If you relish in the chance to hitch a ride in a 27-foot Hot Dog supporting one of the world’s most iconic brands, the Hotdogger program is the place for you!

With iconic and emerging food and beverage brands around the world, we deliver the best taste, fun and quality to every meal table we touch. We’re on a mission to disrupt not only our own business, but the global food industry. A consumer obsession and unexpected partnerships fuel our progress as we drive innovation across every part of our company.
Around the world, our people are connected by a culture of ownership, agility and endless curiosity. We also believe in being good humans, who are working to improve our company, communities, and planet. We’re proud of where we’ve been – and even more thrilled about where we’re headed – as we nourish the world and lead the future of food.

Good isn't good enough. We choose greatness every day by challenging the ordinary and making bold decisions. All while celebrating our wins - and our failures – as we work together to lead the future of food. Challenging the status quo takes talent. Because great people make great companies, and we’re growing something great here at Kraft Heinz.

title: Production Supervisor

description:
The Production Supervisor is a member of the plant leadership team and is responsible for day-to-day manufacturing operations within an assigned area and shift under the direction of the Business Unit Manager. This role provides leadership to deliver business results and operational improvements while achieving productivity, efficiency, customer service, cost, quality, safety, and employee engagement objectives through individual and team contributions.
Key Responsibilities
Manage day-to-day manufacturing operations for the assigned area and shift to meet productivity, efficiency, customer service, cost, quality, safety, and employee engagement objectives.
Provide direction, leadership, development, and support to direct reports through empowerment, teamwork, on-the-job assignments, and continuous improvement projects and initiatives.
Develop, implement, and promote safety programs and safe work practices through participation in plant safety teams, programs, and initiatives.
Promote sound employee and labor relations within the department by developing and maintaining an effective organization with qualified personnel.
Develop, promote, and support continuous improvement efforts and cross-functional initiatives that deliver business results and operational improvements.
Additional Responsibilities
Shift execution: Translate production priorities into daily assignments, communicate expectations, and coordinate staffing, materials, and equipment readiness to support the production schedule.
Operational results: Monitor production output, downtime, waste, yield, and labor utilization. Identify deviations, communicate barriers, and coordinate corrective actions with appropriate support teams.
Safety leadership: Reinforce established safety procedures, personal protective equipment requirements, housekeeping standards, and hazard reporting. Escalate unsafe conditions and support incident reviews and corrective-action follow-through.
Food safety and quality: Partner with Quality and Food Safety personnel to reinforce good manufacturing practices, sanitation requirements, product specifications, and required production checks. Escalate deviations and follow established product hold and disposition procedures.
Cross-functional coordination: Work with Maintenance, Sanitation, Planning, and Warehouse teams to address equipment concerns, changeovers, material availability, and other issues affecting safe and reliable production.
Training and development: Identify training needs, coordinate onboarding and cross-training, reinforce standard work, and maintain required training documentation. Provide clear instructions and timely coaching to support employee development.
Employee communication: Conduct shift meetings, communicate operational updates, recognize team contributions, and promptly elevate employee concerns to the appropriate leader or Human Resources.
Labor relations: Partner with Human Resources and plant leadership to apply established policies and applicable collective bargaining agreement provisions consistently when coordinating assignments, staffing, and employee matters.
Continuous improvement: Use production data and team input to identify recurring losses, support root-cause analysis, implement approved improvements, and confirm that corrective actions are sustained.
Documentation and handoffs: Maintain accurate production records and shift reports. Communicate equipment status, unresolved issues, quality concerns, staffing needs, and follow-up actions to the incoming shift.
Qualifications:

Location
New Ulm, Minnesota – Home of  VELVEETA and DELI DELUXE!
Work Schedule
Monday – Friday work week, 2nd shift, afternoons
Essential Functions & Responsibilities
The Senior Rotating Analyst is responsible for all finished product testing. Occasionally may also be responsible for blender testing, blender standardization, problem solving and in process testing. Works from brief verbal and complex written instructions and is expected to exercise individual judgment and resolve questions independently in a timely manner. When 1 to 2 lines are running, Analysts work alone – therefore they must exercise good judgment with all aspects of in process and finished product testing when issues arise. Rotating Analysts are expected to work between areas and help out when needed. Must have good written and oral communications skills. Work requires mathematical skills including fractions, decimals and knowledge of personal computers. Work is expected to meet the high standards of Kraft Heinz, AOAC and legal parameters. Must be able to perform sensitive adjustments of complex controls requiring skill in fine tuning of the process variables.
Job Responsibilities:
Regular Moisture/Finished Product Testing:
Performs five-hour vacuum moisture tests or NIR moisture test on every hourly sample for every product run daily. Responsible for all accurate recording of data and documenting out of standard results. Performs recheck testing on all samples out of standard and special samples. Calculates all results by use of personal computers and makes decisions accordingly. Performs moisture and fat tests on raw material cheese as requested by supervisor. Responsible for cleaning, labeling and preparation utensils and equipment. Responsible for cleaning and maintaining work area at all times. Responsible for performing pH tests on hourly samples, as specifications require. Accountable for all retests and monitoring of equipment. Responsible for performing extraneous tests as required on finished product and raw materials. Projects as requested by supervisors.
Fat Testing:
Performed tests, requires safety awareness at all times due to the chemicals being worked with. Safety eye wear, apron and gloves are mandatory in this area. Performs fat tests on samples as required by specifications. Performs fat tests on blender samples on an as needed basis. Responsible for all special fat testing required on natural cheese samples. Performs fat testing on ingredients and liquid loads as specifications require. Accountable for all data entry, calculating and recording of fat results. Accountable for any data that is out of standard and must be retested and/or special samples received. Responsible for knowledge of all fat testing procedures, techniques and methods as prescribed by Kraft Heinz, AOAC and legal standards.
Salt and Lactose Testing:
Preforms tests on samples as required by specifications. Accountable for all data entry, calculating and recording of all Salt and Lactose results. Accountable for any data that is out of standard and must be retested and /or special samples received. Responsible for knowledge of the procedures, techniques and methods as prescribed by Kraft Heinz, AOAC and legal standards. Responsible for all critical control point checks performed in areas. Responsible for cleaning and maintaining work area and equipment at all times.
Rapids Area:
When required, responsible for accurate testing of blend samples for moisture and fat on a timely basis. Methods used include NIR, vacuum oven and Roccal Method. Concise and quick decisions must be made based on these results. Responsible for solving blender errors/problems using G40 personal computer. Responsible for activating, adding and deleting liquid load data in the G40 for proper blender standardization. Responsible for maintaining and operating the G40 back up and special standardization programs on the personal computer. Prepares in process testing tools for each blender standardization. Maintains an ample supply of folded, numbered and weighed foils daily. Responsible for knowledge of all methods, techniques and procedures according to Kraft Heinz, AOAC and legal standards. Responsible for maintaining and cleaning work area at all times.
Hot Tests/In-Process Testing:
When required, performs in-process testing on certain blenders on a timely basis. Accountable for all decisions made for corrections at the cooker to adhere to 100% compliance for every product. Timely decision making skills are utilized. Utilizes various methods for testing including a vacuum oven and NIR units. Performs in process testing on wet mix and liquid loads. Responsible for additions and data reporting. Personal computers and mathematical skills are used to compute data. Utilizes a personal computer for computing calculations on all vacuum tests. Responsible for an in-process test on certain blenders of standardized product. Communicates correction/additions to the cook room cooks. Responsible for checking all corrections. Responsible for knowledge of proper methods, techniques and procedures according to Kraft Heinz, AOAC and legal standards. Accountable for maintaining and cleaning of work area at all times. Responsible for all critical control point checks performed in areas.
Responsibilities:
Work on programs and other requests. Record cooker steam out results and grade the steam out pads. Test standardized cream, cream whey and WPC as required by the specifications and record results. When needed, performs blender checks as required. Involves retesting blender samples for moisture and fat. Responsible for the salvage of blender, moisture, fat, NIR, naturals and raw material samples. Miscellaneous testing required on ingredients as to adhere to the specifications. Preparation of solutions for miscellaneous testing (pepsin, acid pH). Responsible for cleaning five-hour ovens centrifuge, grading room buckets, fat bottles, beakers, moisture pans and all other lab dishes and glassware. Prepares fat (Roccal) solution and fills acid bottles. Monitoring and cleaning of water bath and acid dispensers. Monitor the hazardous waste that is produced by some of the testing and dispose of it properly. Responsible for air exposures and swabs for start-up, qualifications and regular production. Responsible for entering COA results into SAP for incoming ingredients. Responsible for net content scale and weight verifications.
Maintenance:
Responsible for all thermometer checks in the Laboratory. (Primary, secondary and calibration thermometers) for start-up. Responsible for all balance and scale calibrations in Laboratory for start-up.
General Requirements:
Computer skills, operating knowledge of SAP, Quality Suites, Excel, demonstrated math skills (including decimals, fractions, divisions) and decision-making skills. Person must be willing to train in other areas of the Lab (Special Testing, Bacti, etc.) or take upgrading when offered.
Safety:
Follow all OSHA and safety procedures. Working with acids, heat and glassware are a safety hazard. Knowledge of proper treatment, response, and care and preventative measures required.
Equipment Operated:
Primarily responsible for the safe and efficient operation of NIR units, G40, 6500, personal computers, vacuum ovens, centrifuges, water baths and scales.
Value of Material:
Lack of responsible decision making skills and inattention to required duties may result in substantial monetary losses, delays or inconveniences. The results not are readily detectable until 10-20 hours later.
Lifting Requirements:
Moderate - Lifting requires handling materials up to 20 lbs. frequently or less and up to 45 lbs. infrequently.
Working Conditions:
Fair – Standing throughout the shift required of several job areas. Hazards are present when working with Laboratory testing reagents and disposals. Work may be a fast pace and hectic; therefore, cautions and common sense must be exercise. Exposure to noise and unfavorable working conditions (such as wet slippery floors) at times.
Training:
The Senior Rotating Analyst will have a three phase training period; 30 days, 3 months and 6 months. An evaluation will be done after each phase. The successful Senior Lab Analyst will be able to demonstrate the following competencies throughout each phase of training:
30 days
Decision making skills
Technical aptitude
Math and computer skills
3 months
Effective communications skills
Dependability
Analytical skills
6 months
Self-confidence
Team working skills
Versatility

Job Description
Job Purpose
The Refrigeration, HVAC, Plant System Design Engineer is a subject matter expert that will lead their discipline as part of the Design and Technical Capabilities team to define standards, consistent processes, and formulate projects that can be used and issued to suppliers for initial budget and final pricing and order placement. The design engineer is responsible for the design, operation, maintenance, and optimization of ammonia-based refrigeration systems used in industries such as food processing, cold storage, and manufacturing. This role requires a strong engineering background, deep technical knowledge of ammonia systems, and strict adherence to safety and regulatory standards. The specialized professional focus will be on ammonia/refrigeration but their responsible will includes oversight of design, engineering, safety and quality support in the following utility equipment systems: Clean steam, RO systems, HVAC systems, plant steam systems, process chillers, compressed/process air, nitrogen, ammonia chillers, refrigeration process, and cooling towers. This individual will work closely with a cross-functional team to meet the needs of the groups they support. This position supports the team on completing capital engineering feasibility studies, develop initial and detailed equipment designs, and creating engineering standards that complement the equipment design and can be utilized for project feasibility and execution phases of projects to improve speed of execution. This individual will require both the project management and technical knowledge to develop the scope for complex utilities projects. While this role will be focused on refrigeration/ammonia expertise, team members are expected to have general knowledge of infrastructure, utilities, wastewater treatment and food and beverages process technologies.
Essential Functions & Responsibilities · Develop initial scope of work, block flow diagrams, equipment selections, and technical reports for ammonia refrigeration systems, including compressors, condensers, evaporators, and associated components. · Perform sizing and selection of refrigeration equipment, control group design, final line sizing, and mass/energy balance calculations. · Maintain engineering standards, stay current with code changes (e.g., NEC, ASHRAE, OSHA, EPA), and ensure compliance with Process Safety Management (PSM) requirements. · Ensure PSM program is compliant. Review PSM audits and provide solutions and alternative options. · Create standard engineering project designs and Capex estimates for major capital initiatives working together with supply development, project leads and their teams. · Provide engineering support to address operational / compliance issues and to ensure equipment is maintained at a level required to provide high reliability maximizing useful life · Provide technical expertise and industry best practices · Lead engineering efforts to resolve equipment and operational problems and ensure problem solving techniques are appropriately utilized · Participate & lead cross functional reviews to define and agree standard process flows ensure all major Capital projects (>$1MM) within the Zone are designed to maintain business continuity, maximize operating income and factory efficiency, including the formulation of: standard designs, cost estimation and challenging timelines together with BU Engineering, ORM, R&D and FS&Q. · Develop equipment standards and designs to enable Procurement to obtain standard pricing structures for particular/preferred suppliers. · Establish benchmarking of common equipment or processes and Capital projects across the Zone to understand key advantages of each the various installed lines and standardize where these bring competitive advantage. · Identify and evaluate Best Available Technologies and engineering practices for their discipline, sharing them across the zone, and globally where appropriate. Job Description:
Role Overview
The Head of Occupational Health provides global medical leadership to protect the health, wellbeing, and work capability of our global workforce.
In this role, you will establish global occupational health standards, design the multi-year strategy, and ensure robust clinical governance and regulatory compliance. Working in close partnership with Health & Safety, People & Organization (P&O), Operations, and Benefits, you will drive continuous improvement in workforce health protection, ensuring a safe, inclusive, and highly resilient working environment.
Key Accountabilities
1. Global Strategy & Medical Leadership
Set the Vision: Develop and execute the global occupational health strategy, establishing clear priorities, standards, and a multi-year roadmap.
Alignment: Ensure the strategy aligns seamlessly with broader business needs, workforce health risks, and organizational objectives.

Risk Assessment: Provide deep medical expertise to identify, assess, and prevent work-related health risks, including occupational exposures, physical hazards, and psychosocial risks.
Collaboration: Partner with Health & Safety and Operations to design and implement highly effective, preventative controls.
3. Clinical Governance & Regulatory Compliance
Standard Setting: Establish global clinical standards, protocols, and assurance frameworks to ensure safe, evidence-based occupational health practices.
Compliance: Oversee medical surveillance programs and ensure strict adherence to local legislations, professional practices, and confidentiality standards globally.
4. Workforce Health & Fitness for Work
Employee Support: Provide medical leadership for fitness-for-work assessments, rehabilitation, reasonable workplace adjustments, and return-to-work processes.
Inclusion: Champion workplace adjustments that support diverse physical capabilities, inclusion, and sustained employee capability.
5. Health Intelligence & Performance Management
Data-Driven Insights: Define key occupational health metrics, analyze workforce health trends, and deliver actionable insights to senior leadership.
Continuous Improvement: Use health intelligence to drive evidence-based interventions and track measurable health outcomes.
6. Service Delivery & Strategic Partnership
Operating Model: Define the global operating model and set standards for external occupational health service providers.
Team Capability: Build the capability and competency of regional and local health teams.
Cross-Functional Synergy: Partner with Benefits, Security, P&O, and Business Leaders on wellness promotion, emergency medical preparedness, and crisis management.
Experience & Capabilities
Required Qualifications
Credentials: Fully qualified Occupational Health Physician with recognized advanced qualifications/board certification in Occupational Medicine.
Experience: 15+ years of progressive, hands-on leadership experience in Occupational Medicine within a large multinational organization. This includes leading strategy across multiple geographies with differing legal frameworks.
Strategic Leadership: Proven track record of designing and implementing global occupational health strategies, with deep expertise in health risk management and clinical governance.
Business Partnering & Influence: Demonstrated ability to influence executive stakeholders and lead organizational change in highly complex, matrixed environments.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience operating within highly complex operational, manufacturing, or supply-chain environments.
Proven experience leading enterprise-level wellness, mental health, or occupational health initiatives.
Recognized external thought leadership in Occupational Health or Public Health forums.

Strategic Mindset & Global Perspective – Able to look ahead to future possibilities and translate them into breakthrough strategies with a global lens.
Drives Vision & Purpose – Painting a compelling picture of the health vision that motivates others to action.
Balances Stakeholders & Organizational Savvy – Navigating complex matrix dynamics and balancing the needs of multiple stakeholder groups.
Plans, Aligns, & Ensures Accountability – Planning work to meet commitments, aligning regional teams, and holding self and others accountable.
Customer/Associate Focus – Building strong customer relationships and delivering customer-centric health solutions.
Def i ning Success in the Role
Success in this role will be measured by:
Measurable Improvements in workforce health protection and the reduction of work-related illnesses.
Effective Control and mitigation of occupational health risks globally.
Robust Clinical Governance and 100% regulatory compliance across all operating regions.
High-Quality Service Delivery from regional teams and external providers, leading to a safer, healthier, and more resilient workforce.

This is a highly visible enterprise leadership opportunity with a mandate to shape the future of Associate Health & Wellbeing at Mars Incorporated. This manager will implement and enforce established policy and area and organizational strategies.

Conversion - Manage the efforts of operating teams of a multi-line, area, or technology on one shift in efficiently converting materials into quality products in a safe, secure, and sanitary manner within the product design specifications.
Change Agent - Implement changes in methods, equipment, systems, and organization, as needed, to ensure that the objectives of the line/area are met and give input and recommendations for such changes by using a continuous improvement mindset.
Mars Supply Excellence – Lead or participate in one or more MSE Pillars; Lead and support the implementation of Autonomous Maintenance (AM) and Autonomous Work Teams (AWTs) in area of responsibility; Lead key connection points and own reliablity data collection accuracy.
Area Ownership – Collaborate with the rest of the Area Leadership Team (Area Manager or Continuous Improvement Engineer, Continuous Improvement Specialist, Maintenance Coordinator) to create and execute the reliability strategy for the area of responsibility.
Coaching – Coach operators to build their functional and leadership capabilities and to drive accountability in safety, Quality and Food Safety, Autonomous Maintenance, and team engagement.
Line Operations - Coordinate materials, staffing and resources to support line operation and changeovers.
Standards Implementation and Adherence – Ensure standards are implemented on shift and in areas of responsibility through effective communication, change management, consistent reinforcement, and coaching, guidance, and accountability measures.
Associate Safety – Ensure safe working conditions, behaviors, and mindsets through the direct implementation of Mars Safety programs and driving a relentless focus among a team of operators.
Food Safety and Product Quality – Ensure the ongoing production of safe and defect-free products consistent with the principles of Mars.  HACCP proficiency is required; this manager owns ongoing training and championing of quality goals and improvements at the Area Shift level.
Associate Advocacy - Manage associate relations issues and guide and direct the hiring, training, retraining, development, and motivation of Operations associates following self-managed, team-working principles with a minimum degree of guidance from the Area Manager or Value Stream Manager.
Engagement - Responsible for facilitating and driving an environment of high associate engagement on the team.

title: Art Director, Research Team
description:
About the Team

OpenAI didn’t begin as a traditional company. It began as an idea: that artificial intelligence could be developed in a way that benefits everyone. As a creative team, our role is to help make sure the work behind that idea is understood, as it leaves the lab and meets the world.

This company works at the frontier of intelligence. Like any frontier, it’s unfinished, constantly shifting, and still being explored. Our job is to stay close to that uncertainty and help shape how this story gets told, in a way that feels grounded and human. We do this through campaigns, launches, films, brand systems, and work that doesn’t fit neatly into any of those categories yet. This team is for people who want to help shape something from the beginning.

About the Role

OpenAI is seeking a hands-on Art Director to partner with the Research team on creative concepts, visual direction, and design. You’ll help define how research stories look and feel, developing ideas and carrying them into compelling visual work. Working directly with researchers, you’ll keep scientific accuracy and clarity central to the creative approach, while finding distinctive ways to capture people’s attention and imagination.

You’ll collaborate with filmmakers, designers, and marketing and creative partners across web, social, film, editorial, and experiences. Your work may range from developing a visual concept and art directing collaborators to designing assets yourself. You’ll create treatments, references, and explorations that establish a clear direction, then help carry that direction through production and final delivery.

This role suits a versatile art director with strong hands-on design craft, a distinct creative point of view, and an interest in AI research. You can move between the overall visual idea and the details of execution, build cohesive visual systems, and give collaborators clear, constructive feedback. You should be comfortable navigating ambiguity and adapting your approach to an evolving research agenda.

In this role, you will:

 - Partner with researchers and creative teams to understand priorities, develop original concepts, and define the visual direction for research stories, announcements, and demos; communicate ideas through treatments, mood boards, references, and design explorations

 - Translate complex research concepts, methods, and findings into clear, compelling visual storytelling, choosing imagery, typography, composition, and motion that serve the idea and accurately represent the underlying work

 - Art direct and design across web, social, film, editorial, and experiences; guide the look and feel through collaboration with filmmakers, designers, animators, illustrators, and other creative partners, providing clear briefs and feedback while staying hands-on with execution

 - Create prototypes and reusable visual systems that carry a creative idea across formats; collaborate with researchers on narratives and demos, and explore visual approaches for film graphics, imagery, and environments that bring research capabilities to life

 - Carry visual direction from concept through delivery, reviewing work for craft, consistency, and clarity; manage multiple creative requests with partners, align on priorities, and adapt to changing research goals and production timelines

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - 5+ years of experience in both art direction and graphic design, with a portfolio demonstrating original concepts, a strong visual point of view, and high-quality execution; clearly show your role in shaping the direction and making the work

 - Can establish a compelling visual direction and develop it into cohesive systems across formats, balancing consistency with the needs of each story and medium

 - Bring strong hands-on craft in typography, layout, composition, color, imagery, and information design, with an eye for how these elements work together in static and moving images

 - Can turn an ambiguous brief into a clear creative approach, present and explain your ideas, and guide execution as technical concepts and project needs evolve

 - Have an experimental nature, a broad range of visual references, and the ability to explore different approaches before refining the strongest idea

 - Have an interest in AI research and can ask thoughtful questions to understand unfamiliar ideas and preserve their meaning

 - Collaborate effectively with researchers, filmmakers, marketers, and creative partners; give thoughtful art direction and actionable feedback, and are comfortable both leading visual work and contributing hands-on to a shared creative vision

title: BIM Designer & Coordinator: Civil
description:
About the Team

Industrial Compute develops the infrastructure that powers OpenAI’s AI systems. Our Design organization connects engineering, construction, and digital delivery to support complex data center campuses from initial planning through deployment.

Working with internal teams, design consultants, and construction partners, we develop coordinated designs that address site constraints, infrastructure requirements, and future growth. Our BIM team provides the models and workflows needed to deliver consistently across the portfolio.

About the Role

We are seeking a hands-on Civil BIM Designer & Coordinator with a minimum of 8 years of relevant experience to support the planning and design of large-scale, mission-critical data center campuses and associated power generation, energy storage, and utility facilities.

In this role, you will develop, coordinate, and maintain civil models using Civil 3D and AutoCAD. Your scope will include site layouts, grading, drainage, roads, and utilities, coordinating buildings with generating equipment, battery energy storage systems (BESS), water treatment plants, gas metering and conditioning facilities, substations, and cooling systems.

You will work closely with civil engineers, BIM team, discipline designers, equipment vendors, and delivery partners to turn engineering requirements into clear models and deliverables. Your work will support early design reviews, resolve site coordination challenges, and establish repeatable civil BIM practices across concurrent projects. Detailed engineering requirements and specialist analyses will be provided by the responsible engineers.

We are looking for a hands-on civil specialist who can independently manage modeling assignments, communicate design dependencies, and maintain quality as projects evolve.

Key Responsibilities

 - Advance feasibility, constructability, and phasing: Prepare layout, grading, routing, and earthwork options for early design reviews; incorporate noise, exhaust dispersion, heat-rejection, safety, and environmental constraints. Model heavy-equipment delivery routes, turning movements, crane areas, laydown, maintenance clearances, staged construction, temporary-to-permanent generation transitions, and future expansion.

 - Lead civil site development: Create and maintain surfaces, grading and earthwork models, equipment and building pads, roads, alignments, profiles, and corridors. Incorporate flood protection, stormwater management, and containment or separation process-drainage requirements.

 - Develop and coordinate plant utility systems: Model gravity and pressure networks for gas supply, cooling and process water, fire water, wastewater, electrical duct banks, and communications. Coordinate utility models, routes, corridors, crossings, connections, and clearances with engineers, consultants, utility providers, vendors, and construction partners.

 - Integrate campus and power-generation infrastructure: Coordinate civil models with buildings, power plants, BESS, substations, water treatment plants, gas metering and conditioning facilities, cooling systems, and other site utilities. Support simple-cycle and combined-cycle gas turbine, reciprocating engine, and CHP layouts while incorporating equipment separation, service access, and fire access.

 - Coordinate equipment, foundation, and thermal interfaces: Integrate vendor general arrangements, foundation footprints, equipment elevations, trenches, pits, and pipe-support locations with inputs from structural, geotechnical, mechanical, and electrical engineers. Coordinate civil interfaces for heat-recovery steam generators, steam-turbine facilities, heat exchangers, cooling towers, air-cooled condensers, radiator arrays, and thermal-distribution corridors.

 - Govern civil model data and multidisciplinary alignment: Manage Civil 3D data shortcuts, external references, coordinate systems, styles, templates, and parts libraries. Coordinate Civil 3D, Revit, vendor, and combined-discipline models; verify coordinates, origins, elevations, units, orientation, and model alignment in Navisworks.

 - Drive coordination and quality: Lead model reviews, investigate clashes and spatial conflicts, communicate design changes, and track issues through resolution. Review civil models and drawings for completeness, reference integrity, consistency, and compliance with project BIM requirements.

 - Deliver and improve civil BIM: Prepare plans, profiles, sections, model exports, review packages, and model-based quantities appropriate to each project phase. Maintain reusable content, document workflows, and improve delivery across data center, power-generation, energy-storage, and utility projects.

Qualifications

 - Minimum 8 years of civil design, BIM modeling, or civil infrastructure drafting experience, plus a relevant degree/diploma or equivalent practical experience.

 - Experience supporting mission-critical facilities or complex industrial infrastructure across multiple disciplines.

 - Advanced Civil 3D and AutoCAD proficiency, including grading, corridors, utility networks, sheet production, data shortcuts, references, coordinate systems, and model dependencies.

 - Experience with site-survey data, GIS, point clouds, NavVis or similar laser-scanning/reality-capture workflows.

 - Experience with Navisworks, Revizto, and Autodesk Forma for model coordination, issue tracking, and markups.

 - Ability to independently deliver civil packages, interpret engineering and vendor information, identify missing inputs, and escalate engineering decisions appropriately.

 - Strong communication and organizational skills across changing priorities and concurrent projects.

Preferred Skills

 - Direct experience with hyperscale, colocation, or other mission-critical data center campuses, from conceptual site planning through detailed design and construction coordination.

 - Experience supporting civil design and model coordination for one or more of the following: gas turbine or reciprocating engine power plants, combined-cycle or CHP facilities, BESS installations, water treatment plants, gas metering and conditioning facilities, or comparable industrial infrastructure.

 - Familiarity with OEM installation requirements, equipment and foundation interfaces, maintenance envelopes, and balance-of-plant infrastructure.

 - Familiarity with Revit-to-Civil 3D workflows, including building locations, elevations, utility interfaces, and phased campus development.

 - Experience with GIS, survey data, point clouds, and civil data exchange workflows.

 - Experience reviewing consultant models, BIM execution plans, levels of development, model quality, and common data environments.

 - Experience improving production through Dynamo, scripting, or other automation tools.

 - For candidates with deeper experience, the ability to guide complex civil modeling packages, mentor colleagues, and improve shared standards.

What Success Looks Like

You deliver dependable civil models and drawings, identify coordination issues early, and maintain clear ownership of civil BIM production and standards. Your work enables coordinated delivery of data center campuses and associated power, energy storage, and utility infrastructure across the portfolio.
