You will build the narratives, content, customer proof, sales tools, and educational programs that help marketers understand the opportunity, make informed investment decisions, and achieve results.

Reporting to the Head of Global Large Advertiser Marketing, you will lead a function spanning enterprise advertising positioning and messaging, thought leadership, solutions storytelling, sales enablement, and customer education. You will translate product capabilities, customer insights, and performance evidence into clear, compelling materials for marketing leaders, media decision-makers, and the teams supporting them.

You will partner closely with Sales, Communications, Product Marketing, and Customer Marketing to create a consistent story across the customer journey. This role requires a strategic leader and exceptional storyteller who can build a scalable content operation while personally developing its most important narratives and materials.




IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Develop the enterprise advertising narrative. Own audience-specific positioning and messaging for enterprise advertisers and agencies, partnering with Product Marketing and Communications to ensure accuracy and consistency.

 - Define the content strategy. Establish editorial priorities, formats, and distribution plans that address customer needs from initial awareness through evaluation, adoption, and growth.

 - Build solutions narratives. Translate advertising capabilities into clear customer use cases, business benefits, and practical guidance tailored to advertiser objectives and agency needs.

 - Exceptional writing, editing, and presentation skills, with the ability to translate complex products and data into clear, credible customer stories.

About the Team

OpenAI’s Legal team helps address the cutting-edge legal questions that arise from developing and deploying advanced AI. The Security and Public Sector Legal team helps protect OpenAI’s technology, systems, data, and people and supports the safe and responsible use of our tools. We work closely with technical and operational teams to provide practical advice on novel, consequential, and fast-moving issues.



About the Role

We are seeking a counsel to help lead legal responses to cybersecurity and AI safety incidents. This is an opportunity to bring deep incident response expertise to some of the hardest questions in AI, and help build the legal frameworks and practices for answering them.



You will advise on complex cybersecurity incidents, from discovery through to resolution, and also help develop our response to incidents involving the safety of our models and tools. AI safety incident response is a new and rapidly evolving legal practice area. Your work will help define how frontier AI companies investigate and respond to safety events such as unexpected model behavior, degradation of safeguards, harmful uses of our services, and potential harm to third parties—often where established legal standards do not yet exist. Working directly with Security, Safety, Product, Engineering, and colleagues across Legal, you will advise on consequential decisions where established approaches may offer little guidance.



We are looking for a practical, dynamic lawyer who can turn incomplete information into clear recommendations, exercise sound judgment on novel questions, and follow matters through to resolution. You will help establish the facts, assess risks, and guide investigations, communications, remediation, and reporting. You will also turn lessons from individual incidents into durable response processes, helping further develop a legal function that evolves alongside the technology.



This role is based in Washington, D.C. or San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.



In this role, you will be:

 - Serving as legal lead on assigned cybersecurity and AI safety incidents, coordinating fact development, legal analysis and advising, cross-functional escalation, and follow-through with the response team.

 - Working with investigators to understand incident scope, attack paths, root cause, and affected systems and data, and potential third-party impacts, while helping teams distinguish established facts from gaps in the evidence.

 - Managing outside counsel and third party service provider engagements necessary to incident response.

 - Serving as key Legal point of contact for cross-functional teams.

 - Preparing concise incident updates and decision materials that distinguish established facts, uncertainties, options, and recommended next steps.

 - Developing severity-based escalation criteria, response playbooks, exercises, and clear decision and handoff processes for cybersecurity and AI safety incidents, adapting established practices to emerging model risks.

 - Supporting post-incident reviews, tracking agreed corrective actions, and turning lessons into practical improvements to safeguards and response processes.

 - A JD and a license or qualification to practice law in your jurisdiction.

 - 5+ years of relevant experience.

 - Relevant legal experience managing cybersecurity or privacy incident responses or comparable complex technology investigations at a technology company, law firm, or government agency, including work with technical teams, other counsel, and communications partners.

description:
About the Team

The Preparedness team is an important part of the Safety Systems https://openai.com/safety/safety-systems org at OpenAI, and is guided by OpenAI’s Preparedness Framework https://openai.com/index/updating-our-preparedness-framework/.

Frontier AI models have the potential to benefit all of humanity, but also pose increasingly severe risks. To ensure that AI promotes positive change, the Preparedness team helps us prepare for the development of increasingly capable frontier AI models. This team is tasked with identifying, tracking, and preparing for catastrophic risks related to frontier AI models.

The mission of the Preparedness team is to:

 1. Closely monitor and predict the evolving capabilities of frontier AI systems, with an eye towards misuse risks whose impact could be catastrophic to our society

 2. Ensure we have concrete procedures, infrastructure and partnerships to mitigate these risks and to safely handle the development of powerful AI systems

Preparedness tightly connects capability assessment, evaluations, and internal red teaming, and mitigations for frontier models, as well as overall coordination on AGI preparedness. This is fast paced, exciting work that has far reaching importance for the company and for society.

 

About the Role

We’re hiring a Data Scientist to help build, evaluate, and continuously improve mitigations that prevent extreme harms from AI systems. This role is for an experienced, highly autonomous individual contributor who can take ambiguous problem statements, structure rigorous analyses, and translate findings into actionable product and policy changes.

This position goes beyond “running evals.” You’ll help create mitigation intelligence and monitoring systems that enable OpenAI to detect issues early, measure effectiveness over time, and reduce both over-blocking (unnecessary friction) and under-blocking (missed harm).





WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Evaluate and improve mitigation systems, including classifiers and detection pipelines across domains (e.g., biosecurity, cybersecurity, and emerging risk areas).

 - Diagnose false positives and false negatives with deep error analysis, root cause investigation, and clear recommendations for mitigation adjustments.

 - Build monitoring and measurement frameworks to track mitigation effectiveness over time and across user segments and use cases.

 - Identify trends in over-blocking vs. under-blocking, quantify customer impact, and propose prioritized interventions.

 - Develop insights from customer feedback, complaints, and usage patterns to detect shifts in adversarial behavior and system failure modes.

 - Expand risk monitoring into new areas, including cybersecurity threats and model loss-of-control or sabotage scenarios, in partnership with domain experts.

 - Communicate results to technical and executive stakeholders with crisp narratives, decision-ready metrics, and clear tradeoffs.

You might thrive in this role if you are:

 - An autonomous operator: you can take a problem statement and independently structure the analysis end-to-end.

 - Strong at executive-ready communication: concise, clear, and outcome-oriented.

 - Skilled in turning analysis into productable changes: you’re comfortable influencing across functions to drive mitigation improvements.


QUALIFICATIONS

 - Significant experience in data science or applied analytics in high-stakes domains (e.g., security, trust & safety, abuse prevention, fraud, platform integrity, or reliability).

 - Strong foundations in experimentation, causal thinking, and/or observational inference; ability to design robust measurement under imperfect data.

 - Fluency in SQL and Python (or equivalent) for analysis, modeling, and building monitoring workflows.

 - Experience building metrics, dashboards, and operational monitoring that meaningfully changes outcomes (not just reporting).

 - Track record of driving cross-functional impact with engineering, product, and research partners.

 - Cybersecurity data science experience (strong preference), including exposure to threat modeling, adversarial dynamics, abuse patterns, or security telemetry.

 - Experience with classifier evaluation, calibration, thresholding, and error analysis at scale.
   Familiarity with detection systems in adversarial settings (e.g., evasion, distribution shift, feedback loops).

 - Trust & Safety experience is helpful, but not required.

 - Genuine interest in AI safety, alignment, and catastrophic risk prevention.

description:

OpenAI’s Forward Deployed Engineering team builds with customers to bring frontier AI into production. Our Cyber FDEs partner with the security and engineering teams that defend globally critical systems, from enterprise software to the core infrastructure it runs on. About the role

You’ll build systems that give defenders an advantage at a scale few engineering teams encounter. You might help an enterprise identify, test, and deploy patches across hundreds of thousands of code repositories, or help a security team analyze petabytes of logs for signs of malicious agents or coordinated attacks. Across these deployments, you’ll build tools that customer engineers can trust to support consequential security decisions.

You’ll work directly with customer security teams, from CISOs to frontline analysts. As AI changes how attackers operate, you’ll help these teams determine where their defenses need to evolve, prioritize what to build, and validate solutions with the engineers who will operate them. Alongside OpenAI’s account teams, you’ll translate security priorities into deployed systems that help defenders cover more ground.

You’ll also help shape what OpenAI builds next. When you identify a gap between what defenders need and what today’s models or products can do, you’ll partner with Research and Product to define, build, and test capabilities that address it.



This role is based in New York. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week. We offer relocation assistance. Travel up to 50% is required.

 - Build evaluations grounded in the decisions defenders make. For a patching agent, test whether a fix blocks a known exploit while preserving expected application behavior. For a detection system, replay historical attacks alongside normal traffic to measure detection speed and false-positive rates.

 - Guide production rollout with the engineers who will operate the system. Provide the observability and controls they need to understand system behavior, intervene when necessary, and expand adoption with confidence.

 - Translate successful approaches across deployments into reusable tools and engineering practices that other defenders can adopt.

title: Intercompany Accountant
description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

OpenAI Finance is responsible for ensuring the organization is set up for success in pursuit of its mission to ensure that artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity.

 


ABOUT THE ROLE

We are looking for an accountant to own an assigned portfolio of intercompany and investment accounting processes. You will manage recurring reconciliations, coordinate the accounting for intercompany funding, review transfer pricing calculations and journal entries, and partner with Technical Accounting on investments. A fundamental part of the role is understanding OpenAI's group structure, partnering closely with Tax on complex transactions, and providing guidance to the wider accounting group on intercompany flows.

You will own work from source data through close, resolve routine issues independently, and improve processes within established policies and approval controls. You will identify matters requiring technical assessment early and bring clear analysis and supporting facts for review. You will be a pivotal interface between global finance teams, treasury, tax, and systems to support our mission-critical financial close and reporting processes.

 


WHAT YOU WILL DO

 - Develop and maintain an understanding of OpenAI's group structure, ownership relationships and intercompany arrangements and flows.

 - Partner with Tax, Technical Accounting and your manager to assess complex intercompany transactions and coordinate implementation of agreed accounting treatments.

 - Provide guidance to the wider accounting group on intercompany flows, accounting treatments and cross-entity accounting questions.

 - Own monthly and quarterly close activities for assigned accounts, including reconciliations and resolution of reconciling items.

 - Coordinate accounting for intercompany funding and settlements with Treasury and Tax, within established approval and execution controls.

 - Review transfer pricing calculations prepared by the TP team for intercompany accounting accuracy, including entity, account, currency and FX rate treatment.

 - Prepare and review assigned journal entries for accuracy, supporting evidence and consistency with approved accounting treatments and controls.

 - Maintain investment accounting records and reconciliations, implement agreed accounting treatments, and partner with Technical Accounting and your manager on new transactions and technical assessments.

 - Maintain close and audit support, document processes and controls, and work with systems teams to improve accounting workflows and resolve reporting issues.


WHAT YOU WILL BRING

 - Experience owning recurring accounting work through close, including balance sheet reconciliations, journal entries, and investigation of reconciling items.

 - A working understanding of US GAAP and multi-entity accounting, with the judgment to distinguish routine application of established policy from matters that need technical review.

 - Familiarity with intercompany transactions, settlements, and foreign currency accounting. Experience with transfer pricing calculations or investment accounting is relevant to this role.

 - Careful review habits and the ability to trace a calculation or journal entry to its source, explain discrepancies, and document how they were resolved.

 - The ability to organize a close calendar, manage dependencies, and communicate clearly with Accounting, Treasury, Tax, and Technical Accounting. You follow through independently and raise issues with enough context for others to act.

 - Comfort working with spreadsheets and accounting systems. Experience with Oracle FCCS or a similar consolidation system, internal controls, or audit support would be useful.


WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

 - Your assigned close activities are completed on time, with accurate entries and reconciliations that are easy to review.

 - Reconciling items are resolved promptly, and unresolved issues have clear owners and next steps.

 - Funding, transfer pricing, and investment accounting records reflect approved transactions and treatments, with complete supporting evidence.

 - Documented processes and practical improvements reduce rework, while complex or unusual matters reach your manager early enough for a considered decision.

title: ML Silicon Performance Lead
description:
ABOUT THE TEAM:

OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops AI-native silicon and system-level solutions for the unique demands of advanced AI workloads. Building on efforts like Jalapeño, the team is developing future generations of AI-native silicon and tightly integrated systems to power the next generation of frontier models. By co-designing chips, systems, tools, and methodologies, the team helps deliver faster, more efficient, and production-ready hardware for OpenAI’s supercomputing platform.


ABOUT THE ROLE:

We’re looking for an ML Silicon Performance Lead to drive hardware/software co-design for our silicon architecture. You will work across models, kernels, compilers, and silicon to shape how ML workloads map to hardware—and how the hardware should evolve to support them. Your work will connect model and workload requirements with compute, memory, and specialized acceleration capabilities to maximize performance, efficiency, and scalability across current and future generations of AI silicon.

You’ll partner closely with ML research, compiler, and silicon architecture teams to jointly develop software approaches and hardware capabilities. From kernel mapping and quantization to new data structures and specialized IP, you’ll evaluate hardware and software tradeoffs to improve performance, efficiency, and utilization across large-scale AI workloads. Through performance modeling, simulation, and hands-on optimization, you’ll guide architectural decisions and validate improvements on representative workloads.


IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Drive hardware/software co-design across ML research, compiler, and silicon teams, jointly shaping kernel implementations and hardware capabilities to meet workload performance and efficiency goals.

 - Partner with ML research to translate model and workload needs into kernel performance targets and compute, memory capacity, and bandwidth requirements, feeding hardware constraints and opportunities back into model and algorithm choices.

 - Map and optimize ML kernels for architecture, using insights from data movement, memory hierarchy, and execution efficiency to guide both software improvements and hardware design.

 - Co-design support for new data structures and quantization formats across kernels, compilers, and silicon, balancing model quality, numerical behavior, performance, power, and implementation cost.

 - Define and help develop specialized acceleration IP, working with compiler and silicon partners to determine the right division of functionality across software, instructions, and dedicated hardware.

 - Drive ML performance modeling and simulation with the compiler team to compare hardware/software design options, expose bottlenecks, and quantify end-to-end benefits on representative workloads.

 - Partner with the Silicon Architecture lead and silicon team to specify and validate new IP, using kernel and simulation results to refine requirements and prioritize architectural improvements.


YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU:

 - Have deep experience with ML accelerator architecture and how compute resources, memory systems, and data movement shape workload performance.

 - Can translate model-level behavior into concrete kernel requirements and hardware design decisions.

 - Have built or used accelerator performance models and simulators, and know how to validate their assumptions and interpret their limitations.

 - Have hands-on experience optimizing ML kernels, including identifying bottlenecks and improving utilization, locality, and execution efficiency.

 - Understand quantization and numerical formats, including their implications for model quality, memory bandwidth, compute efficiency, and hardware support.

 - Have experience with hardware/software co-design and can reason about whether a capability belongs in a kernel, compiler, instruction set, or dedicated hardware.

 - Work effectively across research, compiler, and silicon teams, bringing clarity to ambiguous requirements and building alignment through technical evidence.

description:
About the Team

Security is at the foundation of OpenAI’s mission to ensure that artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity.

 

The Security team protects OpenAI’s technology, people, and products. We are technical in what we build but are operational in how we do our work, and are committed to supporting all products and research at OpenAI. Our Security team tenets include: prioritizing for impact, enabling researchers, preparing for future transformative technologies, and engaging a robust security culture.

We are seeking a senior Global Security Investigator with a technical background to lead complex, long-running security investigations involving a full spectrum of threats – whether originating from internal employees, external threat actors, or supply chain partners. This role is about seeing the full chessboard and independently driving complex, multi-month cases across cyber, physical, and human domains.

 

In this role you will:

 - Independently conduct comprehensive security investigations from initial detection to resolution, including cases involving insiders, external actors, and supply chain and third-party risks.

 - Lead proactive, data-driven threat-hunting efforts that weave together disparate signals to surface undetected insider or external threats before they escalate into incidents.

 - Collect, preserve, and analyze evidence from a variety of sources, including log data, digital forensics, subject interviews, access records, threat intelligence, and open-source intelligence (OSINT), to support investigative findings.

description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops AI-native silicon and system-level solutions for the unique demands of advanced AI workloads. Building on efforts like Jalapeño, the team is developing future generations of AI-native silicon and tightly integrated systems to power the next generation of frontier models. By co-designing chips, systems, tools, and methodologies, the team helps deliver faster, more efficient, and production-ready hardware for OpenAI’s supercomputing platform.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Silicon Design Lead to drive architecture, microarchitecture, and implementation of key IP and subsystems for our AI hardware platforms. You will translate functional, performance, and security requirements into efficient silicon designs, owning technical decisions from architectural definition through implementation and integration.

Part of this role will focus on hardware security implementation in close partnership with OpenAI’s Security team. While the Security team owns the overarching security architecture and requirements, you will translate those requirements into silicon microarchitecture and implementation, balancing security capabilities with performance, power, area, and design complexity. The other part of this role will focus on driving general silicon architecture/microarchitecture. 

In this role, you will:

 - Own architecture, microarchitecture, and implementation of silicon IP and subsystems, from requirements and design specifications through integration and validation.

 - Define hardware interfaces, data flows, and microarchitectural tradeoffs to meet functional, performance, power, and area requirements.

 - Partner closely with OpenAI’s Security team to translate security architecture, requirements, and threat models into implementable hardware capabilities.

 - Design and integrate hardware security mechanisms, including encryption, key management, access controls, isolation, and data protection across silicon subsystems.

 - Evaluate architectural and implementation tradeoffs to ensure security capabilities meet functional and performance requirements.

 - Collaborate with silicon architects, RTL, verification, firmware, and software teams to drive subsystem design, integration, and validation.

 - Review and contribute to RTL implementations, ensuring designs align with architectural intent and system requirements.

 - Evaluate existing and third-party IP, identify architectural or implementation gaps, and drive solutions across subsystem boundaries.

 - Have working knowledge of RTL design and coding proficiency in Verilog or SystemVerilog, with the ability to read, review, and contribute to RTL.

title: Staff Backend Engineer, Financial Engineering
description:
About the Team

Financial Engineering (FinEng) builds the financial systems behind ChatGPT, Codex, and OpenAI’s API platform. These products serve people, developers, and businesses around the world. We make them easy to buy, use, and pay for. Our systems support everything from individual subscriptions to usage-based billing and complex enterprise agreements.

We also build the foundations for how products are packaged, accessed, and used: product catalogs, SKUs and bundles, workspaces, entitlements, and usage metering. These systems connect what customers purchase to the capabilities they can access and the usage they can manage.

That reach creates challenging engineering problems. We build services and data pipelines that handle large volumes of usage and transactions, keep payments, product access, and financial records consistent across systems, and adapt as products and pricing change. The same foundations must support a simple checkout and the detailed spending controls a large business needs.

Your work will help teams launch new products faster and give customers confidence in what they are paying for. The work spans customer experiences, backend services, and data systems, with opportunities to influence technical design and see your work through to production.

We’re hiring Staff+ engineers with strong backend experience. Experience in payments, billing, or financial systems is a strong plus, but not required.

In this role, you will:

 - Design and build systems for purchasing, payments, subscriptions, and billing across OpenAI products and global markets.

 - Build product catalogs, SKUs, and bundles that let product teams launch new offerings and evolve how products are packaged.

 - Develop workspace and entitlement systems that connect purchases and subscriptions to product access for individuals and teams.

 - Keep charges and product access correct when requests are retried, updates arrive late, or another service fails.

 - Build metering systems, data pipelines, and APIs that turn large volumes of usage into accurate bills, timely spending information, and records that are easy to trace and verify.

 - Create reusable building blocks that let product teams launch new offerings, pricing, and payment options without rebuilding the foundations each time.

 - Make complex financial workflows simple for customers and internal teams, using customer feedback and experiments to improve the experience.

 - Scale and evolve live systems while protecting customer access, financial accuracy, performance, and security.

 - Own problems from early design through launch and operation, working with product, design, finance, and other engineering teams to make and test important technical decisions.

description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

The Compute Infrastructure team runs the GPU fleet and large-scale compute clusters that serve the models backing ChatGPT and the API, while also supporting training workloads for our next generation models. We operate a large, modern GPU fleet and provide a unified platform for other OpenAI teams to run production Applied AI and Research training workloads.

We seek to learn from deployment and distribute the benefits of AI, while ensuring that this powerful tool is used responsibly and safely. Safety is more important to us than unfettered growth.




ABOUT THE ROLE

You will join the Compute Infrastructure TPM team as a Technical Program Manager for Capacity Analytics & Tooling. You will serve as the product manager for our supply and demand planning tools, owning the strategy, roadmap, and delivery of the systems teams use to forecast demand, understand supply, and plan allocations. Your users will include Product TPMs, Capacity TPMs, and Compute TPMs, alongside partners across Finance, Accounting, Leadership, Engineering, and Research.

This role combines product management, technical program leadership, data engineering, and applied data science. You will partner with engineering and data teams to build reliable data foundations, improve forecasting and scenario planning, and scale our tools and success metrics across CPU, storage, network, and GPU resources. You will help teams make informed capacity decisions across AWS, GCP, Azure, OCI, and other infrastructure providers.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.




IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Own the product strategy and roadmap for supply and demand planning tools. Understand user needs, set priorities, define success measures, and guide delivery from initial requirements through adoption and ongoing improvement.

 - Build useful planning workflows. Translate complex processes into tools for demand intake, forecasting, supply tracking, scenario analysis, and allocation planning. Help teams understand what infrastructure they need, when it will be available, and which gaps require action.

 - Scale the data infrastructure behind capacity planning. Partner with engineering on ingestion, transformation, storage, and delivery of planning data. Guide technical tradeoffs as the number of resources, providers, data sources, and users grows.

 - Define and scale meaningful success metrics. Measure data quality, forecast performance, planning speed, and tool adoption. Establish consistent ways to track capacity availability, utilization, and efficiency across CPU, storage, network, and GPU resources.

 - Support planning across multiple cloud providers. Build capabilities that account for differences in resource types, regions, availability, commercial commitments, and deployment constraints across AWS, GCP, Azure, OCI, and other providers.

 - Lead delivery across data, infrastructure, and planning teams. Manage dependencies, technical tradeoffs, migrations, risks, and releases. Keep teams aligned on priorities and the decisions needed to move work forward.

 - Drive adoption and reduce manual planning work. Develop simple workflows, documentation, training, and feedback mechanisms. Identify recurring reconciliation and reporting work that can be improved through better data and automation.

 - Make capacity tradeoffs clear to leadership and partner teams. Provide useful views of gaps between supply and demand, allocation options, and their financial and operational consequences. Partner with Finance and Accounting to align planning data with budgeting and reporting needs.




YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU:

 - Have 5+ years of experience leading technical programs or products in data platforms, infrastructure, capacity planning, or a related field, with a record of delivering systems that teams rely on.

 - Have owned an internal product or platform roadmap and translated complex operational needs into requirements, priorities, and releases that users adopt.

 - Have direct experience with capacity planning, including demand forecasting, supply planning, allocations, and resource constraints. You understand how utilization, performance, availability, and cost affect planning decisions.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Compute Infrastructure team runs the GPU fleet and large compute clusters that support OpenAI’s research, ChatGPT, and the API. Our work spans GPUs, CPUs, storage, networking, and cloud infrastructure, bringing these systems together so teams can train and serve models at scale.

We seek to learn from deployment and distribute the benefits of AI, while ensuring that this powerful tool is used responsibly and safely. Safety is more important to us than unfettered growth.




ABOUT THE ROLE

You will own CPU capacity planning and management across Research and Compute. Working with infrastructure owners, you will lead integrated planning for CPU, storage, and network capacity across OpenAI’s global fleet. You will connect workload demand and GPU deployment plans with the foundational resources required to support pretraining, research, and application infrastructure at scale.

You will work closely with workload owners, infrastructure engineering, network deployment teams, Finance, and cloud providers to turn forecasts into supply and allocation plans. You will understand workload architecture, guide decisions when capacity is constrained, and drive opportunities to improve utilization and reduce waste. Your work will span planning over multiple years and ongoing capacity management across regions and providers, including AWS, GCP, Azure, and OCI.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.




IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Lead CPU demand planning across Research, Compute, and application infrastructure, including foundational services, data acquisition, container platforms, robotics, and services supporting GPU clusters. Maintain forecasts that capture workload growth, regional and hardware requirements, timing, and acceptable alternatives.

 - Translate workload growth and GPU fleet plans into integrated CPU, storage, and network requirements. Partner with engineering to determine the capacity, throughput, bandwidth, connectivity, and placement needed to support pretraining and applications at scale.

 - Reconcile current and incoming supply with demand, model constrained scenarios, and drive allocation and prioritization decisions. Lead CPU allocation planning and fulfillment, including quota transfers, rebalancing, and reclaims.

 - Partner with network engineering and deployment teams to translate regional demand into bandwidth and connectivity plans, ordering inputs, and delivery milestones. Coordinate CPU and network allocations as capacity is deployed across the fleet.

 - Understand workload architecture and performance requirements well enough to challenge assumptions and influence technical decisions. Help teams evaluate resource sizing, regional placement, data movement, storage choices, and acceptable alternatives when supply is constrained.

 - Drive fleet efficiency programs that reclaim unused capacity, rightsize workloads, modernize infrastructure, and improve placement or resource sharing. Measure the capacity released and cost improvements while preserving workload performance and reliability.

 - Scale integrated capacity planning across CPU, storage, and network in partnership with resource owners. Improve demand intake, forecasts, scenario models, inventory and allocation records, and the tools that automate recurring workflows.

 - Partner with cloud providers, Finance, Procurement, and engineering to shape capacity orders, commitments, and renewal decisions. Evaluate regional availability, delivery lead times, cost, and technical fit, and drive resolution of supply gaps.

 - Align capacity plans with cluster and application deployment milestones. Work across infrastructure owners to ensure CPU, storage, and network dependencies are ready when workloads need them, and resolve gaps that would delay usable capacity.

 - Give teams and leadership a clear view of demand, supply, allocation tradeoffs, forecast changes, and risks. Turn ambiguous or competing needs into decisions, accountable owners, and executable plans.

ABOUT THE TEAM

Research Compute Services builds the systems that help researchers use OpenAI’s compute fleet effectively. We partner with Research and Compute Infrastructure to support workloads across the compute stack, including pretraining, synthetic data generation, sampling, research inference, and reinforcement learning.

Our work connects changing research needs with capacity planning, allocation, and scheduling. We build tools and services that help researchers express their compute needs, access the right resources, and run their workloads effectively. As the fleet and our research ambitions grow, we continually improve how compute is planned, allocated, and used.




ABOUT THE ROLE

You will be part of an engineer-first TPM team, partnering closely with the Research Compute Services team. Your primary responsibility will be to build and own the tools, data, and platform that turn Research plans and workload signals into concrete compute demand and manage allocations across the fleet.

This is a hands-on technical role. You will build alongside researchers and engineers, working directly with code and data to prototype solutions, automate workflows, and deliver tools that teams use every day. You will combine technical judgment and program leadership to connect capacity planning with the deployment, scheduling, and optimization systems that make allocated compute usable.

You will work across a broad range of Research workloads, understanding their different requirements and ensuring those needs shape the platform. Success means researchers can express their needs, understand their allocations, and use compute effectively as priorities and workloads change.




IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Build with Research. Work directly with researchers across pretraining, research inference, and other workloads. Treat these communities as core users, and translate their needs into improvements across compute services, tooling, and scheduling.

 - Own Research demand and allocation systems. Own the roadmap and delivery of the tools, data, and platform used to capture demand, support allocation decisions, and manage allocations. Carry this work from requirements and design through adoption and ongoing improvement.

 - Turn research plans into actionable demand. Develop systems that translate evolving plans and workload requirements into concrete capacity needs, including resource requirements, timing, and constraints.

 - Connect capacity supply and demand. Partner with Capacity Planning, Research, and infrastructure teams to reconcile demand with available supply. Build the tools and workflows needed to evaluate scenarios, manage changes, and make allocation tradeoffs visible to decision makers.

 - Build reliable data and useful tools. Create data models, views, and automation that show what researchers need, what capacity is available, what has been allocated, and how it is being used. Improve self-service workflows for requesting and managing compute.

 - Connect allocations to workload execution. Partner with engineers working on Kubernetes deployments and scheduling systems so allocation plans reflect workload constraints and translate into resources that researchers can use.

 - Improve allocation and scheduling efficiency. Work with engineers to evaluate optimization approaches, including solvers operating at fleet and local scheduling levels. Help define constraints and objectives, assess tradeoffs, and measure improvements in fleet utilization.

 - Find and address systemic gaps. Use workload and fleet data to identify bottlenecks, unused capacity, and recurring manual work. Build durable improvements to the tools and systems behind those problems.

 - Lead technical delivery across teams. Own plans, dependencies, and decisions across Research, Research Compute Services, Capacity Planning, and infrastructure engineering. Keep teams aligned on what needs to be built, how it will be adopted, and who will operate it.

 - Make progress and tradeoffs clear. Give working teams and leadership a clear view of demand, allocation constraints, delivery progress, and decisions that need attention.




YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU:

 - Have a strong engineering foundation, developed through relevant education or demonstrated technical experience.

 - Have led and delivered complex technical programs involving large-scale compute, distributed systems, infrastructure platforms, or research environments.

 - Have practical experience with capacity planning, including supply and demand management, compute allocations, and the tools and data that support those decisions.

 - Have personally built or materially contributed to tools, data systems, or automation used by engineering or research teams. You are comfortable working directly with code and operational data.

 - Are familiar with Kubernetes deployments and scheduling systems, and understand how resource constraints and placement decisions affect workload execution.

 - Understand optimization solvers and can reason about their use in fleet-wide allocation and local scheduling. You can evaluate constraints, objectives, and tradeoffs without losing sight of researcher needs.

 - Can work closely with researchers to understand evolving requirements and translate them into systems that are practical to build and useful in daily work.

title: User Education Lead
description:
About the team

Customer Education helps people and organizations build the skills and confidence to use AI effectively. We create courses, live learning, community programs and product education that help people apply OpenAI’s products to their work.

About the role

We’re looking for a User Education Lead who is excited about what AI can make possible for people at work and wants to bring more people along on that journey.

You’ll lead education for enterprise users who are getting started with AI or need help turning early experimentation into everyday use. You’ll help people discover what’s possible, build confidence through practice and develop the judgment to use AI well.

This is a hands-on role for someone who loves both building and teaching. You’ll explore new products, work directly with learners, create practical education and test what helps people make progress. You’ll develop role-based learning and new approaches to teaching AI, then turn what works into frameworks and resources that can reach more people.

You’ll work closely with teams across Customer Education, Product and go-to-market to connect this foundational learning to the broader customer experience and help learners progress as their skills grow.

In this role, you will:

 - Own the education roadmap for people getting started with AI at work. Identify the skills they need, where they get stuck and the opportunities to help them make meaningful progress.

 - Build and deliver role-based learning. Create courses, live sessions, demonstrations and exercises grounded in the work people actually do, helping learners apply AI to useful tasks in their own roles.

 - Develop and test new approaches to AI education. Experiment with how concepts are explained, how practice is structured and how learners are supported. Turn what works into frameworks and resources that others can adapt and use.

 - Help people build lasting skills and confidence. Design learning that helps people move from a first useful experience to independent, repeat use, with clear paths into more advanced education.

 - Stay close to the product and the learner. Explore new capabilities firsthand, listen to customers and work with Product and customer-facing teams to keep education relevant as their needs change.

 - Measure and improve your work. Assess whether people are developing skills and applying what they learn, then use those insights to improve the learning experience and guide future investment.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have built and led education programs that help people develop practical skills and change how they work.

 - Are an engaging teacher and clear writer who can make complex ideas accessible and exciting without oversimplifying them.

 - Are energized by AI’s potential for workers and curious about how to help people who are uncertain, skeptical or just getting started.

 - Use AI actively in your own work, test what you teach and can explain both where it helps and where human judgment matters.

 - Love finding better ways to teach. You listen to learners, try new approaches, learn from the results and share what works.

 - Can set a focused direction, build strong partnerships and deliver high-quality work as products and customer needs evolve.

THE ROLE
Apparel Production Associate
Quince is hiring a Apparel Production Associate t o be a critical utility player across our entire production operation. You'll work across pre-production order staging, machine support, post-decoration finishing, and quality control — adapting daily to where the floor needs you most. On a high-volume floor, you'll stage orders for machine operators one hour, trim and inspect finished goods the next, and support operators with setup and supplies the next. You'll report to the Production Lead and partner closely with the Warehouse + Receiving Lead, machine operators, and the Shipping + Fulfillment Coordinator to keep production moving seamlessly.
Your success means faster order turnaround, zero quality gaps, operators who never stop working because they have what they need, and a clean, organized production floor. You're the backbone of production efficiency.
This is a fully on-site role, Monday through Friday during regular business hours at our facility in Santa Fe Springs, CA.
Responsibilities
Stage and validate orders for production — confirm all inventory and materials were received, verify work instructions and machine locations are clear, check that threads and supplies are in stock, and ensure the order is ready for operators to pull and produce.
Trim threads, backing, and excess materials from embroidered and decorated goods immediately after decoration — keeping pace with machine output so finished goods do not back up.
Inspect every decorated piece against the job ticket: placement, adhesion, color accuracy, and overall appearance.
Pull and set aside any defective or non-conforming pieces; log defect type, quantity, and job number and hand off to the Production Lead for disposition.
Fold, bag, tag, or poly-bag finished pieces per job ticket and customer specifications (pending packing team rollout); ensure all finished goods are presentation-ready before moving to the handoff area for Shipping.
Assist machine operators — embroidery, heat transfer, DTG, and screen print — with loading, unloading, setup, and in-process support as needed throughout the shift.
Restock machine supplies (thread, backing, transfer paper, tape, polybags, etc.) proactively so operators stay running without interruption.
Support the Warehouse + Receiving Lead with job staging, material pulls, and receiving tasks during high-volume periods.
Assist the Shipping + Fulfillment Coordinator with packing and order handoffs when finishing volume allows.
Adapt quickly to shifting priorities — the Production Lead will direct where support is most needed at any given time.
Maintain a clean, organized, and safe production floor throughout the shift.
Qualifications
Required:
1+ year of experience in a production, manufacturing, warehouse or similar environment.
Ability to stand, move, and work on your feet for a full shift (8+ hours).
Strong attention to detail — you catch what's off and you don't let it slide.
Ability to maintain accuracy and quality at a consistent production pace.
Adaptable and self-directed — comfortable shifting between tasks as the floor demands.
Reliable and punctual; production schedules depend on everyone showing up and staying focused.
Preferred:
Experience in a production, apparel, manufacturing, or warehouse environment.
Familiarity with embroidery, screen printing, heat transfer, or decorated apparel finishing.
Experience with quality inspection or production order workflows.
Bilingual (English/Spanish) a plus.
PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS:
Fully on-site production floor role.
Must be able to stand and move throughout the full shift.
Ability to lift and carry up to 30 lbs. regularly.
Manual dexterity required for trimming and finishing tasks.
Comfortable working in a production environment with machinery noise, heat press equipment, and production materials.

title: RTL Design Engineer
description: About Rivian Rivian is on a mission to keep the world adventurous forever. This goes for the emissions-free Electric Adventure Vehicles we build, and the curious, courageous souls we seek to attract. As a company, we constantly challenge what’s possible, never simply accepting what has always been done. We reframe old problems, seek new solutions and operate comfortably in areas that are unknown. Our backgrounds are diverse, but our team shares a love of the outdoors and a desire to protect it for future generations. Role Summary We are seeking an RTL Design Engineer to join the Neural Network Engine (NNE) design team in Palo Alto. In this hands-on role, you will define the microarchitecture and deliver production-quality RTL for compute, memory, datapath, and control blocks in an advanced SoC environment. You will work from architectural and physical design requirements, develop them into a microarchitecture specification. You partner closely with design verification, physical design, firmware, compiler, and silicon-validation engineers. The ideal candidate is comfortable owning a block from definition through implementation, debug, quality checks, and integration. Responsibilities Translate architectural requirements into clear microarchitectural specifications and design documentation. Analyze performance and power characteristics of existing hardware and software to identify areas for improvement. Develop and utilize AI agents to streamline RTL development tasks Define and review block-level interfaces, including data movement, handshakes, clocking, reset behavior, and error handling. Design, implement, integrate, and debug synthesizable RTL for NNE blocks and interfaces. Design with performance, power, area, functional safety, and physical implementation constraints in mind. Collaborate with design verification engineers to create test plans, assertions, coverage goals, and debug strategies. Use simulation, lint, CDC/RDC, formal or equivalence checking, synthesis, and timing analysis to evaluate and improve RTL quality. Investigate functional, performance, timing, and power issues across RTL, verification, and implementation flows. Participate in design reviews and contribute to coding standards, reusable RTL patterns, and development methodology improvements. Support block integration, regression closure, RTL handoff, and pre-silicon validation. Communicate design decisions, assumptions, risks, and trade-offs clearly across partner teams. What you will bring A disciplined approach to writing simple, readable specifications that enable development of clean, reusable, and verifiable RTL. Curiosity about how architecture, implementation, verification, and physical design interact. Comfort working through ambiguous problems, making explicit assumptions, and iterating with partner teams. A bias toward early validation, clear documentation, and high-quality handoffs. The ability to balance block-level ownership with system-level thinking. Qualifications Basic qualifications Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience. Professional experience designing and delivering synthesizable RTL for ASIC, SoC, or other complex digital hardware. Strong proficiency in Verilog and SystemVerilog. Understanding of synchronous digital design, pipelining, finite-state machines, interfaces, memories, and reset/clock behavior. Experience debugging RTL through simulation and waveform analysis. Ability to read and contribute to architectural, microarchitectural, interface, and verification specifications. Strong written and verbal communication skills, especially to write clear design documentation, with a collaborative and ownership-oriented approach. Preferred qualifications Experience with compute engines, neural-network accelerators, floating point computation, memory subsystems, high-throughput datapaths, or SoC control logic. Experience with clock-domain crossings, reset-domain crossings, clock gating, power-aware design, or functional-safety concepts. Familiarity with RTL quality and implementation flows such as lint, CDC/RDC, formal/equivalence checking, synthesis, static timing analysis, and power analysis. Experience with Synopsys VCS, Verdi, or comparable simulation and debug tools. Experience building Python or other software models to explore architecture, validate behavior, or accelerate RTL development. Experience with Git-based development, code review, continuous integration, and automated regressions. Familiarity with physical-design constraints and PPA trade-offs. Experience working across hardware, firmware, compiler, verification, physical design, and silicon-validation teams. Experience developing hardware for automotive, safety-critical, or other reliability-sensitive applications. Demonstrate proficiency in robust problem-solving tools (e.g., 5-Why, Fishbone, Is/Isn't) to resolve recurring issues. Drive controls for weld defects, dimensional variation, distortion, missing welds, spatter, undercut, porosity, burn-through, and rework. The Component Quality Technologist is responsible for the inspection of individual components, both internally manufactured and externally sourced, to ensure they meet required quality standards. The role requires knowledge of geometric dimensioning and tolerancing (GD&T), the ability to read technical drawings, and the use of measuring equipment to confirm product conformity. The Technologist ensures that component defects are identified, documented, and resolved before components proceed further in the production process.
In this job you will be responsible for inspecting fabricated parts, sub-assemblies and final assemblies, including painted components, made from various machines such as shears, punch presses, and welding work centers. You will be required to work with assembly and detailed prints, industry standards, routings, BOMs, specifications, instruction bulletins, and customer notes. Inspecting the products will require you to use various pieces of inspection equipment and the ability to select the appropriate measuring equipment such as tape measures, go/no go gages, special gages, torque wrenches, thread plug gages, fluke meters, and fuses holder standards. The job will require you to clearly communicate verbally and in written format. Abnormal conditions, must be clearly recorded on the Checklist, DPU report, and/or on a NMR. All defects will be recorded and clearly explained to assembly team members and shop floor leadership. There will be times when product will be placed on hold until you clearly explain the abnormal conditions to engineers so they can determine if the product could be sent to the customer or needs to be reworked.

Record and document inspection results, including the identification of non-conforming materials.

location: Remote - Austin; Remote - Seattle; San Francisco, CA, United States
description:
Who we are
Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.
About this role:
Samsara’s cloud-connected sensor platform collects observations about the world in near real-time. Samsara builds an extensive set of products, including battery-powered, wireless sensors, Linux-based IoT gateways, and Internet-connected dashcams. These devices are the building blocks Samsara uses to construct enterprise solutions for a wide range of verticals, including commercial fleet management and industrial monitoring. Through a unique integration of sensor data such as GPS, acceleration, temperature, video, and more, we enable our customers to gain greater insights into operations, identify and eliminate inefficiencies, and react to alerts all in near real-time.
As a Firmware Engineer at Samsara, you will develop software that runs on millions of devices, deployed by our industrial and enterprise customers. You’ll tackle challenges including evaluating and selecting hardware components, bringing up new hardware platforms and sensors, building systems to gather data and detect meaningful events, and structuring recorded data to allow efficient analysis across thousands of devices while providing deep insights into individual events.
We use C for our MCU-based platforms, Golang for embedded applications on Linux-based gateways and backend services, Google protocol buffers to structure data, and various AWS technologies to process and store data. Experience with these exact technologies is not required.
You should apply if:
You want to impact the industries that run our world: Your efforts will result in real-world impact—helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, reduce emissions, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.
You are the architect of your own career: If you put in the work, this role won’t be your last at Samsara. We set up our employees for success and have built a culture that encourages rapid career development, countless opportunities to experiment and master your craft in a hyper growth environment.
You’re energized by our opportunity: The vision we have to digitize large sectors of the global economy requires your full focus and best efforts to bring forth creative, ambitious ideas for our customers.
You want to be with the best: At Samsara, we win together, celebrate together and support each other. You will be surrounded by a high-caliber team that will encourage you to do your best.
Click here to learn more about Samsara's cultural philosophy.
In this role, you will:
Shape the hardware, not just the code that runs on it. Sit in reviews with our electrical engineers and help choose the right SoC, amount of flash/RAM, and combination of sensors, then prove those choices out on prototypes that reach real customers in months, not years.
Be the first person to make a new board do anything at all. Bring up new platforms and prototypes from virgin silicon: configure I/O, get SPI, I2C, UART, BLE talking, debug system init, validate the design, and turn unproven hardware into a product.
Build the layers everything else depends on. Peripheral drivers, secure bootloaders, device firmware updates, as well as the core management layers like power and connectivity, that determine whether a device in the field quietly recovers on its own or becomes an RMA.
Chase every microamp. Design protocols and hardware management for battery-powered sensors and gateways where the gap between good firmware and great firmware is measured in years of device life.
Work with the people who ship the whole product. Partner with product, full-stack, mobile and quality engineers so the data your firmware produces arrives intact and useful as it lands in the hands of dispatchers, fleet managers, and technicians who depend on it every shift.
Raise the bar for the engineers around you. Your designs, reviews, and instincts help raise the ceiling for the whole team. You will help shape how Samsara works, keep a high bar, be intellectually honest, work with urgency and deliver iteratively, as we scale globally and across new offices.
What you bring
2+ years building firmware for resource-constrained systems , on products that shipped to real customers and then had to survive in the field.
Fluency in C. You know what the compiler is doing, and you can read a linker map, a stack trace, or a corrupted heap without guessing.
Solid bare-metal and RTOS experience - Zephyr, FreeRTOS, or equivalent. You have made scheduling, memory and timing decisions. Mutexes and semaphores are everyday tools for you.
You have helped bring up new boards. First power-on of unproven hardware, at the bench with the electrical engineer who drew it up, working out whether the bug is in your code, a library, the schematic, or the part itself.
Fluency in the low-level interfaces - SPI, I2C, UART, CAN, ADC and the ability to debug the seam between hardware and software.
Real bench instincts. The usage of an oscilloscope, network analyzer, or RF spectrum analyzer, is how you form a hypothesis, not what you reach for after the print statements run out.
Cross-team scope. You have contributed to work spanning hardware, firmware, cloud and quality from concept to shipped product. You have worked effectively across teams to build consensus.
Cross-layer judgment. You can trace how a decision at the driver level surfaces in a customer's experience three layers up, and you factor that into your design decisions.
You write things down. Design docs, review comments and post-mortems that other engineers can actually act on.
You ship fast without shipping poorly. Comfortable iterating on customer feedback at speed, backed by automated testing and code you would be content to inherit.
You use AI smartly. It’s part of your every day work flow and multiplies your output without watering things down.
What will set you apart
BLE at depth - You understand what’s going on down the PHY and can build orchestration for the system to use in a performant and power efficient way.
Cellular IoT - LTE-M or NB-IoT modem integration, power state management, and the certification gauntlet (FCC, PTCRB, carrier approval).
Securing embedded systems end to end - secure boot, firmware signing, cryptography, and key management that survives contact with manufacturing.
OTA and device firmware update at fleet scale - A/B partitions, rollback, and the discipline of never bricking a device you cannot physically reach.
Embedded Linux on the gateway side - Yocto or Buildroot, kernel drivers, device trees.
CAN and J1939 work on commercial vehicles , including reverse-engineering data bus parameters across makes and models.
Python and Bash for tooling , and hardware-in-the-loop test automation.
You’ve been on the factory floor - You have an understanding of the processes behind the mass production and quality assurance of electronics. You have a track record of fixing production show stoppers.

Samsara is building an AI/ML team inside its Operations team to make our supply chain AI native. You would be one of its first AI/ML engineers.
We design connected hardware (cameras, vehicle gateways, sensors), build it with joint development manufacturing partners, and deliver it to tens of thousands of customers in industries that keep the economy running. Every link in that chain often runs on emails, flat files and manual reconciliations. We are moving our internal operations into the future with modern AI capabilities.
We expect you to work across the supply chain including fulfillment, inventory, returns, cash, planning, components, suppliers and cost management. You will partner directly with Planning, Procurement, Fulfillment, Finance, Sales, and the hardware, firmware and quality engineering teams.

What makes this unique:
11 years of untapped operational data:  ERP systems (e.g. NetSuite, e2open, Propel), IoT sensor streams, Salesforce, Slack, Gong call insights, and real-world hardware telemetry
Own the full stack: Modeling, MLOps, deployment, monitoring—build production systems that drive real business decisions
Real hardware supply chain: Complex multi-tier supplier networks, lead times, high-stakes NPI ramps
Direct executive partnership: Collaborating cross-functionally with teams in Product, Engineering, Procurement, and Finance
You'll shape the team's roadmap, scientific agenda, and modeling standards. Ideal for a deeply technical IC who thrives in ambiguity, thinks strategically, and enjoys end-to-end ownership.
This is a remote role open to candidates residing in the US or Canada.
Why this role matters:
Real-world impact at massive scale:
Your models will help prevent supply shortages for customers in construction, utilities, transportation, and public safety —industries that literally keep the world running.
Optimize inventory for hardware deployed across 98% of US roads and 70+ billion miles driven annually.
Drive sustainability initiatives by reducing waste and improving supply chain efficiency across global operations.
Unique technical challenges:
Build demand, inventory and cost forecasting systems for highly variable, seasonal SKUs with intermittent patterns and long lead times.
Model supplier risk using real-time IoT telemetry, geopolitical signals, and market data —not just historical sales.
Design cost optimization algorithms balancing inventory carrying costs, expedite fees, and revenue risk across multiple regions.
Create anomaly detection systems for cellular connectivity spend and supply chain disruptions using multimodal data.
A data playground unlike any other:
Access to 10+ trillion data points annually from connected operations.
Work with ERP data, IoT sensor streams, third-party market intelligence, and operational metrics.
Build features from unique real-world signals —vehicle diagnostics, utilization patterns, failure modes.

You are motivated by impact: Your work will drive smarter, faster, more sustainable supply chain decisions across Samsara's operations.
You combine scientific rigor with real-world pragmatism: You're skilled at navigating trade-offs between model complexity, performance, and maintainability.
You want to work on hard problems: You'll tackle forecasting volatility, cost optimization, anomaly detection, and more using large, noisy, high-dimensional datasets.
You are a self-directed leader: You identify analytical white space, set multi-quarter plans, and mentor others through influence.
You enjoy building models that matter: Your solutions will be deployed in production, drive decisions, and be regularly evaluated against business KPIs.
You seed AI/ML capabilities and enable the broader organization: You establish foundations, set standards, and empower cross-functional teams to adopt data-driven decision making.

Define the end-to-end AI transformation roadmap for supply chain alongside the Senior Director of Supply Chain AI Transformation, aligning with company OKRs and executive stakeholders
Design, train, validate, and deploy ML models to production (demand forecasting, inventory optimization, supplier risk scoring, cellular spend prediction, HW cash flow), ensuring robust MLOps practices and measurable ROI
Build predictive models to forecast demand, inventory, lead times, and spend across Samsara's global supply network
Create novel features using large-scale ERP, IoT, and third-party datasets; build pipelines and ETL jobs to serve models and stakeholders
Deliver production-grade code that supports both batch and real-time inference with MLOps best practices
Act as the AI liaison to Product, Engineering, Procurement, and Finance—ensuring alignment on data requirements, integration, and change management
Drive enhancements to our data infrastructure and analytics platform to support real-time model training, monitoring, and inference at scale
Mentor junior scientists through code reviews and collaborative project work
Act as a key scientific voice in roadmap planning, experimentation frameworks, and modeling strategy discussions
Identify gaps in data, tools, and processes—and lead initiatives to close them
Establish governance frameworks , documentation standards, and quality controls for model development, validation, and lifecycle management
Partner with Ops management to drive adoption of AI tools, define new processes, and train supply chain teams on insights-driven workflows
Champion Samsara's cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally
Minimum requirements for the role:
Experience & Education:
8+ years in applied data science or ML, ideally in supply chain, operations research, logistics, or manufacturing
Master's or PhD in Computer Science, Statistics, Data Science, EE, OR, or related technical field
Core ML & Technical Skills:
Expert in statistical modeling and ML : time series forecasting, optimization, anomaly detection, causal inference
Strong Python coding skills and fluency in SQL ; proven experience developing and deploying production ML systems
Proficiency in MLOps practices : automated testing, CI/CD, model versioning, monitoring, performance tracking
Experience building real-time inference pipelines and managing GPU/TPU resources for training at scale
Familiar with data visualization tools (Tableau, Power BI) and cloud platforms (AWS, GCP, Azure)
Mindset & Collaboration:
Passion for operational excellence, cost efficiency, and scalable solutions
Builder mindset, with a track record of taking products or systems from 0 to 1.
Exceptional  problem-solving, critical thinking, and communication skills—able to explain complex technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders
Track record of  collaborating cross-functionally and driving adoption of data-driven solutions
An ideal candidate also has:
Deep Statistical Expertise: Able to design and validate experiments (A/B, multi-armed bandits) and apply Bayesian methods for uncertainty quantification.
Time-Series Mastery: Proven track record building advanced forecasting models (e.g., Prophet, LSTMs, Transformer-based) for intermittent demand and seasonal patterns.
Cost Optimization Mindset: Skilled in profiling ML workloads and driving down cloud/GPU spend through model compression (quantization, pruning) and serverless architectures.
Cross-Region Scaling: Demonstrated ability to deploy low-latency inference across multiple geographic regions with fail-over and disaster-recovery strategies.
Vendor & Open-Source Savvy: Experience evaluating and integrating third-party ML platforms and contributing to or leveraging relevant open-source projects.
Domain Expertise: Deep understanding of supply chain concepts (S&OP, IBP, safety stock, EOQ), ERP systems (SAP, NetSuite, E2DP, Propel), and inventory optimization theory. Ideal background in consumer electronics or B2B hardware manufacturing.

Experience building and deploying large-scale machine learning systems with feedback loops for continuous improvement.

Customer orientation and intensive focus on improving the customer experience.
Experience building, deploying, and optimizing AI systems than span edge devices and the cloud.
Experience with VLMs, foundation models, or multi-task architectures in production settings — particularly in constrained compute environments.
Background in AV, robotics, or fleet telematics domains where safety and reliability are first-class requirements.
Contributions to or deep familiarity with the academic research literature in CV and perception and the ability to evaluate what's worth bringing in from research and what isn't.

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.
Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.
About the role:
Samsara's Product Operations team is looking for a hands-on builder to join our Platform team and help accelerate our enterprise-ready roadmap. You will support the Billing, Org & Auth, and Security product teams, working closely with R&D leaders to turn ambiguous questions into rigorous analyses, repeatable workflows, and internal tools used across our Product and Engineering organization.
You move ARR. Not "contribute to." Revenue (or an equivalent business result) grows because of decisions you made . You might investigate why enterprise customers stall on a security or permissions requirement, combine signals from thousands of support tickets and customer conversations to find what's blocking expansion, or build a dashboard that helps hundreds of product managers and engineers see how platform gaps translate into pipeline and retention risk.
This is an individual-contributor role for someone who has already shown they can build and ship. You do not need a technical background. However, you do need to use modern AI and development tools to move beyond a prototype: work with data, write and debug code using AI, validate the results, put a useful tool in front of users, and improve it until people trust and rely on it.
This is a remote position open to candidates residing in the US.
You should apply if:
You want to impact the industries that run our world: Your efforts will help keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, reduce emissions, and, most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.
You are the architect of your own career: If you put in the work, this role won't be your last at Samsara. We set you up for success and have built a culture of rapid career development, with countless opportunities to experiment and master your craft in a hyper-growth environment.
You're energized by our opportunity: Our vision to digitize large sectors of the global economy requires your full focus and best efforts to bring forth creative, ambitious ideas for our customers.
You want to be with the best: At Samsara, we win together, celebrate together, and support each other. You will be surrounded by a high-caliber team that encourages you to do your best.
You measure yourself by revenue outcomes: You want your work tied directly to ARR, and you're accountable for the result, not just the activity.
In this role, you will:
Drive ARR through platform decisions. Identify the enterprise-readiness gaps that most limit new business, expansion, and retention, and shape prioritization so that fixing them measurably moves ARR.
Accelerate enterprise-ready delivery by partnering with the Billing, Org & Auth, and Security product teams to define priorities, remove blockers, and track progress against the commitments customers and Sales are waiting on.
Build and ship internal data and AI products that help Product and Engineering teams understand platform usage, customer friction, and the highest-impact opportunities to improve.
Analyze large volumes of structured and unstructured data, including product telemetry, support tickets, customer conversations, feature requests, surveys, and product metadata, to find patterns that would be difficult to see manually.
Turn one-time analyses into reliable, repeatable tools and workflows with clear data definitions, quality checks, documentation, and feedback loops.
Translate complex findings into clear, decision-ready recommendations for R&D leadership, while preserving the evidence and methodology behind them.
Quantify the revenue impact of platform investments and report on it, so every roadmap bet has a clear, defensible ARR case before and after launch.
Own projects end to end: scope the problem, identify and connect the right data, build the first version, launch it, measure adoption and business impact, and continue improving it.
Use AI-assisted development tools thoughtfully, checking outputs, debugging failures, and applying sound judgment rather than treating generated work as automatically correct.
Champion, role model, and embed Samsara’s cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices.
Minimum requirements for the role:
8+ years of professional experience in a role such as product operations, data or product analytics, business operations, consulting, technical product management, or another environment where you solved ambiguous problems with data and technology.
A demonstrated record of building and shipping something useful for real users, such as an internal tool, application, dashboard, automation, data product, or repeatable analytical workflow.
A track record of connecting your work to revenue or an equivalent business result (ARR, retention, expansion, cost), and the ability to show how your decisions caused it.
Experience structuring and analyzing messy or large datasets, validating the results, and explaining what the analysis does and does not prove.
Strong product and customer judgment: you start with the user problem and business outcome, not the technology.
Clear written and verbal communication. You can explain technical or analytical work to non-technical partners and executives without losing the important details.
High ownership, curiosity, and attention to detail. You are comfortable learning quickly, asking sharp questions, forming a point of view, and iterating through ambiguity.
An ideal candidate also has:
Experience in a B2B technology company or working closely with Product and Engineering teams.
Experience in Product Operations functions: defining and tracking product roadmaps and feature requests, and bringing the voice of the customer to every product conversation.
Familiarity with enterprise platform domains such as billing and monetization, identity, access, and org management, or security and compliance, and with what enterprise buyers require in each.
